items.title: Bed management

milestone.title: R4 — Hospital system complete
milestone.description: General availability for hospitals: the rest of OPD, IPD and billing (lab, nursing, OT, insurance/TPA, statutory registers). Was the open part of M3, M4, M5.

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
## Situation

MediCore currently has no authoritative record of physical bed capacity. Admission, transfer and discharge decisions are therefore taken outside the platform — on whiteboards at the nursing station and over phone calls between the ED charge nurse, the ward nurse and the admissions desk. The consequences are concrete: a patient is admitted to a bed that has not been cleaned, two departments claim the same ICU bed, and an isolation patient is placed in an open bay because nobody could see which side rooms were free.

Affected roles are the admissions officer (who must promise a bed at the point of registration), the ward nurse (who owns the physical reality of the bed), the ED charge nurse (who needs to know within seconds whether a critical-care bed exists), the housekeeping supervisor (who owns turnaround) and the infection-control nurse (who owns isolation placement).

This matters clinically because incorrect placement of an isolation or neonatal patient is a direct patient-safety failure, and operationally because bed-occupancy and average-length-of-stay evidence is required for NABH accreditation review. It also matters commercially: without a bed state machine, IPD billing cannot compute accurate bed-day charges, and SafetyConnect evacuation planning cannot know which patient is in which physical location.

Bed management is the foundation for issue #107 (ward management), IPD admission/transfer/discharge and the evacuation-priority work in SafetyConnect. Nothing downstream is trustworthy until bed state is authoritative.

---

## Task

### User or System Story

**As an** admissions officer, ward nurse or ED charge nurse
**I want** a single live, authoritative view of every bed with a controlled state machine for allocation, occupancy, transfer, cleaning and blocking
**So that** every patient is placed in a bed that is genuinely available and clinically appropriate, and occupancy is accurate at all times.

### Scope

**In scope**

* Bed master data: facility → building → floor → ward → room → bed hierarchy, with bed class (general, semi-private, private, ICU, HDU, isolation, neonatal, day-care) and physical attributes (oxygen point, suction point, ventilator-capable, bariatric-rated).
* Bed lifecycle state machine — `available`, `reserved`, `occupied`, `cleaning`, `blocked`, `out_of_service` — with legal transitions enforced server-side, never client-side.
* Allocation and reservation with a hold expiry, so a reservation made at registration cannot silently occupy capacity indefinitely.
* Transfer between beds and wards, preserving a continuous, gapless occupancy history per patient encounter.
* Domain events (`BedAllocated`, `BedOccupied`, `BedReleased`, `BedBlocked`, `PatientTransferred`) published to NATS JetStream for billing, housekeeping and safety consumers.
* Live occupancy and availability query API with filtering by ward, bed class and required attributes, backed by a Redis-cached projection.
* Full audit of every state change with actor, reason code and timestamp.

**Out of scope**

* Ward-level staffing ratios, shift rosters and nurse-to-bed assignment — owned by #107 (ward management).
* Bed-day tariff calculation and IPD invoice lines — owned by the MediCore billing epic; this issue only emits the occupancy events billing consumes.
* Housekeeping task dispatch, cleaning SLA tracking and porter assignment — consumed from `BedReleased` by FacilityConnect work-order handling.
* Discharge-planning and estimated-date-of-discharge forecasting — a later analytics story on the OLAP store.
* Operation-theatre table and recovery-bay slots — those are theatre resources, owned by #108.

---

## Recommended Solution

Implement a `beds` module in the Go/Gin modular monolith with GORM models under PostgreSQL 16 row-level security, tenant-scoped through the shared data-access layer so no query can omit `tenant_id`.

### Data model

```sql
CREATE TABLE bed (
  id              uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  tenant_id       uuid NOT NULL,
  facility_id     uuid NOT NULL,           -- HFR-linked facility master
  ward_id         uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES ward(id),
  room_id         uuid NOT NULL,
  code            text NOT NULL,           -- e.g. "ICU-2-07"
  bed_class       text NOT NULL,           -- general|semi_private|private|icu|hdu|isolation|neonatal|day_care
  attributes      jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',  -- oxygen_point, ventilator_capable, bariatric_kg
  state           text NOT NULL,
  version         bigint NOT NULL,         -- optimistic concurrency
  UNIQUE (tenant_id, facility_id, code)
);

CREATE TABLE bed_occupancy (
  id           uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  tenant_id    uuid NOT NULL,
  bed_id       uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES bed(id),
  encounter_id uuid NOT NULL,              -- FHIR Encounter
  patient_id   uuid NOT NULL,
  occupied_from timestamptz NOT NULL,
  occupied_to   timestamptz,               -- NULL = current
  release_reason text
);
-- No bed may have two open occupancies:
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX bed_single_open_occupancy
  ON bed_occupancy (tenant_id, bed_id) WHERE occupied_to IS NULL;

CREATE TABLE bed_state_event (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY, tenant_id uuid NOT NULL, bed_id uuid NOT NULL,
  from_state text, to_state text NOT NULL, reason_code text NOT NULL,
  actor_id uuid NOT NULL, occurred_at timestamptz NOT NULL
);
```

The partial unique index is the safety net: double-allocation becomes a database constraint violation rather than a race the application must win. Allocation runs in a single transaction using `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on the bed row plus the `version` column check.

Reservations are held in Redis with a TTL (default 30 minutes, configurable per facility via the Country/Facility profile) and mirrored to `bed.state = 'reserved'`; a Temporal timer releases the hold and emits `BedReleased` with `reason_code = 'reservation_expired'` so expiry survives a process restart.

### API surface

* `GET /api/v1/beds` — filter by `ward_id`, `bed_class`, `state`, `requires[]` attributes.
* `GET /api/v1/beds/{id}` and `GET /api/v1/beds/{id}/history`.
* `POST /api/v1/beds/{id}/reserve` — body `{encounter_id, hold_minutes}`.
* `POST /api/v1/beds/{id}/occupy` — converts a reservation or admits directly.
* `POST /api/v1/beds/{id}/release` — body `{reason_code}`; transitions to `cleaning`.
* `POST /api/v1/beds/{id}/state` — `blocked` / `out_of_service` with mandatory reason.
* `POST /api/v1/transfers` — body `{encounter_id, to_bed_id, reason}`; atomic release-and-occupy.
* `GET /api/v1/wards/{id}/occupancy` — live counts, served from the Redis projection.

### Events

Published to NATS JetStream subjects `medicore.bed.*`:

```json
{ "event": "BedOccupied", "tenant_id": "…", "facility_id": "…",
  "bed_id": "…", "ward_id": "…", "bed_class": "icu",
  "encounter_id": "…", "patient_id": "…", "occurred_at": "2026-07-20T09:14:22+05:30" }
```

Consumers: billing (bed-day accrual), FacilityConnect (cleaning work orders on `BedReleased`), SafetyConnect (live patient-location roll call), analytics via CDC into the OLAP store with patient identifiers removed.

### Authorisation

OpenFGA model — bed access is relationship-based through the ward, not a flat role:

```
type ward
  relations
    define facility: [facility]
    define nurse: [user] or nurse from facility
    define charge_nurse: [user]
    define can_allocate: charge_nurse or admissions_officer from facility
    define can_block: charge_nurse or biomedical_tech from facility
type bed
  relations
    define ward: [ward]
    define can_view: nurse from ward
    define can_allocate: can_allocate from ward
    define can_transfer: can_allocate from ward
```

Blocking a bed as `out_of_service` for an infrastructure fault additionally requires the FacilityConnect engineering relation, so a nurse cannot silently retire capacity.

### Sequencing, risks and mitigations

Depends on the facility master (HFR-linked) and on #107 for ward records; ward may be stubbed with a minimal record to unblock. IPD admission consumes this API rather than writing bed tables directly.

The principal risk is double allocation under concurrent ED and elective demand — mitigated by the partial unique index plus row-level locking, with a contention test that fires 50 concurrent allocations at one bed and asserts exactly one success. The second risk is drift between the Redis occupancy projection and PostgreSQL — mitigated by treating Redis as a cache only, rebuilding it from the events stream on startup, and running a nightly reconciliation job that alerts on any divergence. The third risk is cross-tenant leakage in the availability query, mitigated by row-level security plus an adversarial isolation test in CI.

---

## Acceptance Criteria

### Primary Scenario

**Given** ICU bed `ICU-2-07` is in state `available` and the admissions officer holds `can_allocate` on the ICU ward
**When** they reserve it for encounter `E-1042` and the ward nurse then confirms occupancy
**Then** the bed state becomes `occupied`, an open `bed_occupancy` row exists with `occupied_from` set and `occupied_to` null, `BedAllocated` and `BedOccupied` are published to NATS, and the ward occupancy count increments within 2 seconds.

### Failure or Validation Scenario

**Given** two admissions officers in different departments attempt to occupy the same `available` bed at the same instant
**When** both requests reach the API
**Then** exactly one succeeds; the other receives `409 Conflict` with error code `BED_ALREADY_OCCUPIED`, no second occupancy row is created, no duplicate event is published, and the losing request is offered the next matching bed in the response.

### Edge Cases

* A reservation reaches its TTL while the patient is still in transit from ED — the Temporal timer releases the bed, emits `BedReleased` with `reservation_expired`, and the ED charge nurse receives a notification rather than a silent loss of the bed.
* A ward nurse attempts to place an isolation-flagged patient in a bed whose `bed_class` is `general` — the request is rejected with `CLINICALLY_INCOMPATIBLE_PLACEMENT` and can only proceed with an infection-control override that is recorded with actor and reason.
* A transfer is submitted twice with the same idempotency key (poor connectivity on a ward tablet) — the second call returns the original result and produces no second `PatientTransferred` event.
* A bed is marked `out_of_service` by biomedical engineering while it is `occupied` — the transition is refused; the bed may only be flagged for service after release, and the request creates a FacilityConnect work order instead.
* An occupancy query for a ward with zero beds configured returns an empty result with a distinguishable "ward not yet configured" state, not a zero-occupancy figure that reads as full availability.
* A user with a nurse relation on Ward A queries beds in Ward B of the same facility — only permitted bed identifiers and no patient identifiers are returned.

---

## Engineering Guardrails

Complete the applicable items before the story is closed.

### Code Quality

* [ ] The change is limited to the agreed scope.
* [ ] Existing behaviour remains backward-compatible unless explicitly approved.
* [ ] Code follows the team’s agreed standards and architecture.
* [ ] No temporary code, debug output or unnecessary complexity remains.
* [ ] Error handling is explicit and does not silently ignore failures.

### Test-Driven Development

* [ ] Acceptance criteria were converted into test scenarios.
* [ ] New or changed business logic was developed using Red–Green–Refactor where practical.
* [ ] Bug fixes include a regression test that fails before the fix and passes afterwards.
* [ ] Tests validate behaviour rather than private implementation details.

### Automated Testing

* [ ] Unit tests cover new and changed logic.
* [ ] Positive, negative and important boundary scenarios are covered.
* [ ] Integration or contract tests are updated where service boundaries change.
* [ ] Critical user journeys are covered by Playwright or an equivalent E2E framework.
* [ ] Existing tests pass.
* [ ] No new flaky or skipped tests are introduced without justification.

### Security and Access

* [ ] Authentication and authorisation are enforced at the appropriate layer.
* [ ] Users and services can access only the data and actions they require.
* [ ] Input is validated and sensitive information is not exposed in logs or errors.
* [ ] Secrets and credentials are not stored in source code.
* [ ] Security and dependency scans pass.
* [ ] Tenant, account or customer isolation is tested where applicable.

### Accessibility and User Journey

* [ ] The primary user journey works from start to completion.
* [ ] Loading, empty, success and error states are handled.
* [ ] Keyboard navigation and focus behaviour work correctly.
* [ ] Controls have clear labels and accessible names.
* [ ] The change meets the team’s agreed WCAG accessibility level.
* [ ] The experience works across supported devices and browsers.

### Performance and Reliability

* [ ] The change does not introduce unnecessary API calls, database queries or processing.
* [ ] Timeouts, retries and failure behaviour are defined where applicable.
* [ ] Duplicate requests do not create inconsistent data.
* [ ] Performance-sensitive changes are tested against an agreed threshold.
* [ ] Partial failures do not leave the system in an invalid state.

### Observability

* [ ] Important failures are logged with useful diagnostic context.
* [ ] Logs do not contain sensitive information.
* [ ] Metrics or traces are added where the change affects a critical workflow.
* [ ] The team can determine whether the feature is working correctly after deployment.

### Documentation

* [ ] Relevant README, API or technical documentation is updated.
* [ ] Configuration or environment changes are documented.
* [ ] Deployment, migration or rollback steps are documented where required.
* [ ] Known limitations are recorded.

---

## Result

Define what success looks like.

* Expected user or system outcome: every occupied bed in the facility is represented by exactly one open occupancy row, and admissions, ED and ward staff work from the same live availability view rather than a whiteboard.
* Expected business or operational outcome: bed-day charges accrue automatically from occupancy events, and occupancy/ALOS evidence is exportable for NABH accreditation review without manual compilation.
* Success metric or validation method: zero double-allocation incidents in the first 30 days; `GET /api/v1/wards/{id}/occupancy` p95 under 200 ms at 500 beds per facility; allocation-to-occupancy confirmation p95 under 400 ms; nightly Redis-to-PostgreSQL occupancy reconciliation at 100% agreement; contention test proves exactly one winner from 50 concurrent allocations.
* Monitoring period, where applicable: 30 days post-deployment, with OpenTelemetry alerts on the `bed.allocation.conflict` rate and on any reconciliation divergence.

---

---

## Pull Request Evidence

The pull request should include:

* [ ] Link to this story.
* [ ] Summary of the change.
* [ ] Test evidence.
* [ ] Screenshots or recordings for UI changes.
* [ ] Security, accessibility or performance evidence where relevant.
* [ ] Deployment and rollback notes for higher-risk changes.
* [ ] Known risks or follow-up work.

---

## Definition of Done

The story is complete when:

* [ ] All acceptance criteria pass.
* [ ] Required tests pass locally and in CI.
* [ ] No critical or high-severity security or quality issues remain.
* [ ] The critical user or system journey has been validated.
* [ ] Documentation is updated.
* [ ] Code review is complete.
* [ ] The change has been deployed or is ready for deployment through the standard pipeline.
* [ ] Post-deployment validation is defined or completed.
* [ ] Any exception is documented with an owner and reason.

---
## Exceptions

None — all guardrails apply. The availability and transfer screens are used on ward tablets by staff working one-handed, so keyboard navigation, focus order and accessible control names are in scope and validated with the shared design-system components.

items.body:
# AGENT SYNC V2 — pg_trickle-based AgrregateX / CyberForge 2026

**This supersedes Issue #1.** Repository `main` was replaced with the upstream Apache-2.0 pg_trickle snapshot at AgrregateX commit `24fb2f4bbaf47e8a447012e709caf1b03e9d485f` (upstream `821323c327d1e445a647347b6b33c8ae5fdd6cc5`). The old custom FastAPI, loader, acceptance suite and `docs/collaboration/` have been removed from current main, and survive only in `archive/agrregatex-before-pg-trickle-20261031T090817Z`. **Never assume old code still runs.**

## Mission
Build an original, properly attributed, PRD-specific multi-tenant aggregation product ON TOP OF pg_trickle. Mandatory FR-1–FR-7 plus all five Great targets at 10M/100 skewed tenants, if empirically achievable; preserve honesty on gaps. Upstream source `src/`, root `sql/`, `Cargo.toml`, existing tests and workflows stay unchanged unless an explicitly approved narrow PR proves a need.

## Agent assignments (start in parallel)
- **CODEX / user's Fedora:** create isolated `hackathon/` scaffolding, PRD/benchmark matrix and independently executable SQL oracle + latency/freshness/OLTP-safety instrumentation, then REST API, tenant identity and RLS tests after versioned engine contract. Own `hackathon/app/**`, `hackathon/benchmark/**`, `hackathon/docs/handoffs/codex.md` and `hackathon/docs/proposals/codex/**`.
- **OPUS / teammate:** evaluate scheduled DIFFERENTIAL vs IMMEDIATE vs trigger/WAL CDC on PG18, implement `hackathon/sql/**`, SQL/CDC correctness tests for UPDATE/DELETE, multi-database behavior proof, publish versioned ENGINE_CONTRACT for Codex; later loader/bootstrap and repair. Own `hackathon/sql/**`, `hackathon/integration/**`, `hackathon/docs/handoffs/opus.md`, `hackathon/docs/proposals/opus/**`.
- **SHARED** `hackathon/compose.yaml`, `hackathon/docs/CONTRACTS.md`, `PRD_SCORECARD.md`, `COORDINATION_PROTOCOL.md`, `ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md`, root README and all upstream files: modify only after human approval, one integration owner edits canonical docs.

## Important research constraints
- Pinned source version `0.108.4` is pre-1.0 and must be runtime-verified; no assumption that another container uses identical code.
- pg_trickle multi-DB support means **one scheduler per database**, **not** cross-database stream tables; source topology requires organizer generator clarification, at least a 2-DB proof, and a laptop worker budget.
- RLS must be explicitly applied to stream tables as well as source/API boundaries.
- Determine actual refresh strategy/status; configured DIFFERENTIAL can be FULL fallback.
- Scheduled freshness (<30s) versus write impact (<10%) is a tradeoff to measure, not a guaranteed pass.
- Never load 10M until a bounded 1M pass, disk/resource preflight and human authorization. Dataset from organizer not yet available => official schema compatibility NOT VERIFIED.
- Previous custom AgrregateX G3 failure measurements do NOT measure pg_trickle performance.

## GitHub communication protocol
Agent reads this Issue at START, interface handoff, before PR and when human resumes it, **not in an infinite polling loop**. Message:

```
[AX-AGENT]
FROM: CODEX | OPUS
TO: CODEX | OPUS | HUMAN
PHASE: P0..P7
STATUS: STARTED | WORKING | PROPOSAL | BLOCKED | HANDOFF_READY | REVIEW_REQUESTED | DONE_WAITING_REVIEW
CONTRACT_VERSION: vN
BRANCH / PR: ...
OWNED FILES CHANGED: ...
EVIDENCE: command, dataset, measured output, tests
REQUIRES: explicit reviewer/decision or NONE
NEXT SAFE ACTION: ...
```

**When to work:** begin independent P0/P1 research/tests on separate branches immediately. Continue owned work while peer is running. **When to wait:** Codex waits for Opus's approved ENGINE_CONTRACT before wiring real aggregate SQL; Opus waits for human approval before cross-owned/architectural changes; both wait for signed-off 1M and disk gate before 10M; both stop after opening PR and posting `DONE_WAITING_REVIEW`. Other agent comments do not grant human approval. Stopped AIs do not automatically wake when comments arrive; human starts next run.

## Proposed phase gates
P0 baseline and coordination; P1 DIFFERENTIAL vs IMMEDIATE spike + SQL oracle; P2 tenant-safe API + exact aggregate contract; P3 1M/10 and controlled 10M/100 test harness + multi-DB proof; P4 optimize measured G1–G5 failures; P5 high-value bonuses B1/B5/B3/B2; P6 cross-review/integration; P7 demo/release. Work in parallel within file ownership. Measure everything; never fake PASS.

## Human decisions needed
1. Request real organizer generator/schema, judge topology and dataset semantics.
2. Approve candidate approach after Opus spike and Codex measurements.
3. Authorize full 10M experiment only when evidence/space checks pass.
4. Merge tested PRs, decide feature freeze and submit.

Agents: post STARTED with chosen branch and a first milestone. No background autonomous work or auto-merge.

items.title: Fix dbt schema tests
items.body:
**Goal:** `dbt test` runs and passes against the real model.

## Context
`dbt-project/models/schema.yml` declares model `person_unified` with columns `tenant_id, legacy_id, name, extra_field`.
Problems:
- The model file is `models/person_unified.sql` but sets `alias='person'`; the output table has no `name` column
  (it has `firstname`, `surname`). The `name` not_null test will error.
- No uniqueness test on the incremental key `(tenant_id, legacy_id)` (the table has `UNIQUE(tenant_id, legacy_id)` in
  `postgres-init/new_system.sql`).
- `schema.yml` source `staging.person_staging` is declared but the SQL does not use `source()`; it selects from
  `person_staging` directly. Either switch the SQL to `{{ source('staging','person_staging') }}` or leave as is.

## Tasks
1. Replace the `name` test with `firstname` and `surname` not_null.
2. Add a `unique` combination test on `(tenant_id, legacy_id)` (use `dbt_utils.unique_combination_of_columns` -> needs
   `packages.yml` + `dbt deps`, or a singular test in `dbt-project/tests/`, which needs no package).
3. Add `accepted_values` for `tenant_id` (tenant_a1, a2, b1, b2).
4. Run: `docker compose exec cdc-consumer dbt test --project-dir /dbt --profiles-dir /dbt` (stack must be up).

## Done when
`dbt test` exits 0 with data present; deliberately inserting a duplicate key or a bad tenant makes it fail.
Do not touch consumer/API code.

---
## Shared project context (all tickets)
- Pipeline: 4 legacy Postgres DBs (tenants `tenant_a1`, `tenant_a2` = Legacy A with `data_1/2/3`;
  `tenant_b1`, `tenant_b2` = Legacy B with `data_a/b/c`) -> Debezium -> Kafka topics
  `legacy_<x>.public.person` -> `cdc-consumer/consumer.py` -> `person_staging` (new-system DB)
  -> `dbt run` (`dbt-project/models/person_unified.sql`, incremental, alias `person`) -> `person`.
- `data_2` (A) and `data_c` (B) both map to `extra_field`. `modernized_only` (DATE) exists only in the new system.
- API (Flask, `api/api.py`, port 5000): `GET/POST/PUT /api/persons`, `/api/legacy/<tenant>/persons[/<id>]`, `/api/health`.
  POST/PUT write to the legacy DB; the change returns via CDC.
- Compose services (`docker-compose.yml`): kafka, schema-registry, postgres-legacy-{a1,a2,b1,b2},
  postgres-new-system, debezium (8083), cdc-consumer, api (5000), web (8000).
  Credentials: legacy `legacyuser/legacypass` (dbs `legacy_a1` etc.), new system `newuser/newpass` (db `new_system`).
- Currently there are NO automated tests. `TESTING.md` is a manual runbook.

items.title: Архитектура | Шардирование и партиционирование — микростатья
[B] Modèles Gym, User et réglages de paiement
items.body:
## Contexte
Socle de données du multi-tenant réel. **Références :** CDC §4.2.3 (profil salle), §4.2.10 (rôles), §6.3 (isolation), contrat v0.3.0 (schémas `Gym`, `User`, `UserRole`, `PaymentMethodSetting`).

## Ce qu'il faut faire
- Modèle et migration **`Gym`** (la salle = le tenant) : champs du schéma `Gym` du contrat, fuseau `Africa/Abidjan`, devise XOF
- Modèle **`User`** relié à une salle (`tenant_id`), rôle `admin` ou `cashier` (`UserRole`), champ `is_active`
- Modèle **`PaymentMethodSetting`** (7 moyens, `enabled`, configuration non sensible, `credentials` **chiffrés** avec le cast `encrypted`, jamais sérialisés)
- `TenantContext` alimenté à partir de l'utilisateur authentifié (middleware), prêt pour le ticket d'authentification
- Supprimer `ExampleRecord` (prévu dans son commentaire) et adapter les tests d'isolation aux vrais modèles
- *Seeders* fictifs : 2 salles (« FitZone Test », « Salle Témoin »), un gérant et un caissier chacune (données de `docs/rapports/strategie-de-tests.md` §5)

## Critères d'acceptation
- [ ] Migrations réversibles, cohérentes avec les schémas du contrat
- [ ] Tests d'isolation sur `User` et `PaymentMethodSetting` (lecture et écriture refusées pour une autre salle)
- [ ] `credentials` chiffrés en base et absents de toute sérialisation (test)
- [ ] CI `backend` verte (validate, audit, Pint, tests)

## Périmètre
`backend/` uniquement.

## Dépendances
Aucune.

items.title: [B] Authentification (Sanctum)
items.body:
## Contexte
**Références :** CDC §4.2.1, §6.2, §6.4. Contrat v0.3.0 (section Authentification). Arbitrages de Rufin (PR #20) : **Sanctum**, jeton d'accès **1 h** rafraîchi tant qu'il y a de l'activité, session **plafonnée à 8 h**, option « se souvenir de cet appareil » jusqu'à **30 jours**.

## Ce qu'il faut faire
Implémenter, **conformément au contrat** :
- `POST /auth/login` : cookie `httpOnly` (backoffice) et jeton Bearer
- `POST /auth/refresh`, `POST /auth/logout` (révocation du jeton), `GET /auth/me` (utilisateur, rôle, salle)
- `POST /auth/forgot-password` (lien valable 1 h, email via le driver `log` en développement), `POST /auth/reset-password` (8 caractères, 1 majuscule, 1 chiffre)
- Mots de passe en bcrypt (cost ≥ 12). Limitation des tentatives : 5 par minute et par IP, avec `429` sur toutes les routes concernées
- Un utilisateur désactivé (`is_active = false`) ne peut pas se connecter

## Critères d'acceptation
- [ ] Les réponses (codes et corps) correspondent au contrat pour chaque route
- [ ] Tests : connexion OK et KO, `429` après 5 échecs, jeton révoqué après déconnexion, expiration à 1 h, plafond de 8 h, mot de passe non conforme refusé, utilisateur désactivé refusé
- [ ] Aucun mot de passe ni jeton dans les logs
- [ ] CI `backend` verte

## Périmètre
`backend/` uniquement.

## Dépendances
Ticket des modèles `Gym` / `User` (même sprint).

items.title: [invariant-ops] SDK 拡張・変更捕捉・console CRM 境界を整備する
items.body:
## 目的

関係状態の正本 Twenty をコア無改造で使い、customer-graph と console が同じ法人・商談・サイト・テナントを参照できる状態にする。優先1。Twenty repo 側は SDK 定義、既存独自コードの整理、Webhook 設定・資格情報・版固定を担当し、customer-graph 側 API/outbox 実装との結合を完了条件にする。

### 実装項目

- [ ] `twenty-app` を版管理し、Company/Person/Opportunity に `ciId`/`personId`/Twenty UUID の `dealId`/`tenantId` 等を追加。Tenant（`tn_self` 初期値）、Site、WPInstance、PlatformListing、Retainer、Contract、SubsidyCase、ConsentState 投影とリレーションを SDK の可能範囲で宣言する。法人事実は6項目の一方向参照、同意・抑止は outreach-policy の投影、金額実績は freee、診断詳細と PDF は Evidence Store に限定する。snake_case ↔ camelCase 変換を境界に閉じる。
- [ ] 4 パイプライン（web-production、content-ops retainer、backoffice、subsidy）と stage/event 対応をコード管理し、全オブジェクト・フィールドの出典、更新日時/主体、deep link、4 標準ビュー、CSV/JSON エクスポートを用意する。Python 営業ビューは SDK/console、メール集計は metabase へ移し、旧ビューは移行検証後に凍結・削除する。連絡先履歴の契約検証は結合状況を調べ outreach-policy/マージ監査へ置換する。
- [ ] customer-graph のみが Twenty を書く。エージェント書込みは書込ハンドラから outbox へ、人間 GUI は object×create/update/delete でフィルタした Webhook を主経路にする。Secret/HMAC-SHA256、timestamp/nonce/replay を検証し、`eventName + record.id + record.updatedAt` で両経路を重複排除する。実ペイロード（`event/data/timestamp` と `eventName/record/updatedFields` の不一致）を記録し変換層で吸収する。
- [ ] Webhook は at-most-once（失敗再試行なし・60件/分超の破棄）なので `updatedAt[gte]` API ポーリングを **常設・初期5分** で行い、取りこぼし件数と dedupe 件数を記録する。API 100 req/分・最大200件/ページ、同じ updatedAt が複数ページになる `afterId` 境界、論理削除、権限で見えない行を検証する。Workflow HTTP と DB CDC は採用しない。Webhook 登録は SDK 外なので検証環境で手動設定し構成を記録する。
- [ ] `TwentyApi.create/update/get/find/updatedSince/deployApp` と `TwentyWebhookPayload` に対応する本番アダプタと秘匿化 fixture を customer-graph と調整する。`TwentyObjectName` に Contract がなく oss 側にある一方、CG 側の ConsentState 等との差があるため契約変更を無断で確定しない。
- [ ] vault のキーをエージェント・console-ro・書込み・集計用に分離し最小権限/四半期ローテーション。固定 release tag/Docker tag、日次バックアップ、四半期復元/SDK/API/Webhook 互換試験を用意する。

### console API（customer-graph が公開し、Twenty を裏で読む）

`GET /v1/pipelines?tenant_id=`、`GET /v1/pipelines/{pipeline}/board`、`GET /v1/companies?q=&stage=&tenant_id=&cursor=`、`GET /v1/companies/{ci_id}/crm`、`GET /v1/deals/{deal_id}`、`GET /v1/sync/status`、`POST /v1/deals/{deal_id}/stage`。応答の全項目は連携文書の表に従う（board の件数/金額/score/next_action、crm の people/deals/activities/consent/links、sync の `unresolved_count` を含む）。既存マージ・テナント・export API は CG 正本を再利用。console の直接 GraphQL を禁止、30秒の Twenty API キャッシュ、board は ETag、console の再取得は1分以上。

### 受け入れ・不一致の扱い

- [ ] GUI の件数と board が一致、全会社に ci_id、不明行は unresolved_count、GUI 更新が通常60秒以内・Webhook 取りこぼし時も6分以内にイベント/board へ。偽署名・再送・60件/分超過・停止再開・ページ境界・tenant 越境・金額/契約条件の GUI 変更検知と差戻し候補を試験する。
- [ ] 原文の FR-CG-18「1時間」、oss 第6章「片方が使えればよい」は ADR-006 の常設5分照合で置き換える。NFR-CG-02/AC-CG-04/AC-RE-06 の60秒と AC-INT-TW-02 の6分は通常経路/復旧経路として測定し、達成範囲を明記する。
- [ ] oss 第4章と CG 第7.2章の stage ラベル・種類、Python ビュー削除と連携文書の凍結、Contract/ConsentState/Activity 型、顧客 export の L0/L2 の差は既存差分として記録し、承認された契約へ揃える。Q-TW/CG/INT-TW は閉じる証拠を残す。SDK のライセンス扱い、workspace/tenant 境界、実ペイロードを推測しない。

### 状態・実装境界

本 Issue は invariant-ops の Draft 要件を外部 repo 側で実装・検証するためのバックログ。要件文書上の clone、型、fixture、fake の存在は本番接続完了を意味しない。着手時にこの repo の実装と API を調べ、差分表、固定 release tag、依存先、未決事項を更新する。完了していないチェックは未完了のままにする。

ADR-005 の順序（公式 API/SDK/Webhook → サイドカー → 理由を記録した最小 fork）を守る。独自サービスの API を追加する場合はサイドカー/担当コンポーネントに置き、本体の内部 API や DB へ無断で書き込まない。資格情報は vault の短命 lease と `secret_ref`、正本・tenant・承認の境界は維持する。ライセンスや未確認の製品仕様は本 Issue で法的・技術的に確定したとは扱わず、対象版の証拠を残す。

### 横断の完了条件

- [ ] INV-01〜INV-12 を適用し、承認、送信直前の policy 再検証、予算、10 秒以内の kill switch、テナント分離、マスク、構造化出力、証跡失敗時の失敗処理を該当境界で試験する。署名・支払・申告提出は人間の L3。外部作用の `succeeded` に空の `evidence_ids` を許さない。
- [ ] console 向け API は `X-Tenant-Id`/`tenant_id`（各応答行にも付与、`all` は owner のみ）、`console-ro`/`console-op`（ro から操作は 403）、`Idempotency-Key`（操作は必須、再送時同一結果）、cursor/limit/next_cursor（50/最大200）、ETag/If-None-Match、時差付き ISO8601、429/Retry-After、既定 ro 300/op 60 req/分を実装する。操作受付は 202、完了はイベントで反映する。引下げ・停止解除・予算引上げには該当時 `reauth_token`。
- [ ] 一覧・件数・時系列は原則 `rm_*` read model。各 repo の直接 API は詳細と操作を担当し、個別連携文書の一覧 API との分担は実装差分表で明示する。`genre` を Job/判断/イベントに伝搬し、console の業務画面にソフトウェア名を併記しない。
- [ ] 実 API の request/response と失敗を秘匿化した fixture、契約テスト、異常系、テナント越境、重複、権限、レート制限、依存停止、証跡・秘密混入の試験を残す。実顧客への送信、契約署名、公開、支払で試験しない。
- [ ] 要件 ID → 対応コード/設定 → テスト → 実行結果を記録する。固定版の更新・バックアップ・復元・ロールバック手順を用意し、未接続/未検証を成功と記載しない。

### 要件追跡（この repo の担当境界と跨 repo の結合条件）

以下は固定 SHA の正本へのリンク。関連コンポーネント全体をこの repo に移す指示ではない。各行のうちこの repo の責任を実装し、残りは担当コンポーネントとの依存・結合試験として追跡する。Q は解消・一部解消・未解消の原文状態を保ち、推測で閉じない。

#### [oss-modifications/twenty.md](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/oss-modifications/twenty.md)

- [Q-TW-01](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/oss-modifications/twenty.md#L97) **解消済みの参照**（未実装チェックではない）。Twenty 2.0 で Webhook がオブジェクトイベントに対して提供されているか、署名検証の仕組みがあるか / 公式ドキュメントと検証環境で確認 / 解消（2026-10-24。Webhook あり、object × 操作でフィルタ可、Secret 設定時のみ HMAC。再試行なし。`docs/research/2026-10-twenty-change-capture.md`）
- [ ] [Q-TW-02](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/oss-modifications/twenty.md#L98) SDK によるカスタムオブジェクト定義が版を跨いで安定しているか、破壊的変更の履歴 / release notes を 1.x から 2.0 まで確認
- [ ] [Q-TW-03](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/oss-modifications/twenty.md#L99) 既存 twenty repo の「連絡先履歴の契約検証」コードが本体に結合されているか、独立しているか / repo を読み、結合していれば削除し outreach-policy に置き換える
- [ ] [Q-TW-04](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/oss-modifications/twenty.md#L100) SDK 定義が AGPL 上の「改変」に当たるか / ライセンス条文と Twenty の商用ライセンス案内を確認
- [ ] [Q-TW-05](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/oss-modifications/twenty.md#L101) 複数ワークスペースで顧客テナントを分けるか、単一ワークスペースで `tenantId` フィルタにするか / 顧客テナントが 3 つを超える前に決める。RLS 相当の権限制御が Twenty 側にあるかで決まる

#### [requirements/11-human-console/integrations/twenty.md](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/requirements/11-human-console/integrations/twenty.md)

- [ ] [AC-INT-TW-01](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/requirements/11-human-console/integrations/twenty.md#L65) `board` の件数が Twenty の GUI のパイプライン表示と一致する
- [ ] [AC-INT-TW-02](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/requirements/11-human-console/integrations/twenty.md#L66) Twenty の GUI でステージを変えてから 6 分以内に `revops.deal.*` が出て `board` に反映される
- [ ] [AC-INT-TW-03](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/requirements/11-human-console/integrations/twenty.md#L67) `companies` の全行に `ci_id` がある。無い Twenty レコードは `sync/status` の `unresolved_count` に数えられる
- [ ] [AC-INT-TW-04](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/requirements/11-human-console/integrations/twenty.md#L68) console のコードに Twenty の GraphQL を直接呼ぶ箇所が無い
- [ ] [Q-INT-TW-01](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/requirements/11-human-console/integrations/twenty.md#L74) `next_action`（次にやること）を Twenty の Task から取るか、Control の判断から合成するか / 初期は Control の判断から合成。Twenty の Task は活動として表示
- [ ] [Q-INT-TW-02](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/requirements/11-human-console/integrations/twenty.md#L75) パイプラインのステージ定義を Twenty 側に持つか customer-graph 側に持つか / Twenty 側に持ち、customer-graph はラベルを写す
- [ ] [Q-INT-TW-03](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/requirements/11-human-console/integrations/twenty.md#L76) 人間が Twenty GUI で金額や契約条件を変えた時の差し戻し手順（ADR-006） / deal-to-cash が検知して `decisions` に「差し戻し」を出す

#### [requirements/02-customer-graph/README.md](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/requirements/02-customer-graph/README.md)

- [ ] [FR-CG-10](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/requirements/02-customer-graph/README.md#L92) 7章のエンティティを Twenty 2.0 の SDK でカスタムオブジェクトとフィールドとしてコード定義し、`twenty-app` として版管理・デプロイできる

items.title: Trino 473 Unable to Query Hudi 1.0.x Tables (COW and MOR) - GENERIC_INTERNAL_ERROR
items.body:
Hi Trino community,

I am encountering an issue with **Trino 473** when attempting to query Hudi tables (both COW and MOR types) after upgrading Hudi from **0.14.0 to 1.0.1**. **The same tables can be queried successfully in Apache Flink with Hudi 1.0.1 and in Trino with Hudi 0.14.0**, but they fail in Trino 473 with Hudi 1.0.1, resulting in a GENERIC_INTERNAL_ERROR. I would appreciate your assistance in diagnosing and resolving this issue.

### Environment

- Trino Version: 473

- Hudi Version: 1.0.1 (previously 0.14.0)

- Hive Metastore Version: 3.1.3

- Flink Version: 1.19.1 

- Deployment: Docker containers

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a Hudi catalog and table in Flink using Hudi 1.0.1. Below is the Flink SQL used :
   
   sql
   
   ```sql
   -- Create Hudi catalog
   CREATE CATALOG hudi_catalog_3 WITH (
      'type' = 'hudi',
      'catalog.path' = 's3a://catalog_name/data_pool2/hudi_catalog_3',
      'hive.conf.dir' = 's3a://catalog_name/data_pool/conf_hms_8084',
      'table.external' = 'true',
      'mode' = 'hms'
   );
   
   -- Create COW table
   CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS hudi_catalog_3.data_pool2.file_metadata_cow_1_4 (
    -- Primary key
    uuid STRING,
    object_id STRING,
    -- Base fields
    tenant_id STRING,
    store_type STRING,
    store_object_key STRING,
    file_name STRING,
    file_path STRING,
    file_format STRING,
    source_channel STRING,
    description STRING,
    tags MAP<STRING,STRING>,
    -- High-frequency search fields
    file_width INT,
    file_height INT,
    duration DOUBLE,
    alarm_id STRING,
    device_id STRING,
    skill_name STRING,
    -- Skill attributes
    skill_attrs ROW<
      labels ROW<
        alertname STRING,
        business STRING,
        orgUuid STRING,
        requestID STRING,
        roiID STRING,
        skillID STRING,
        trackerID STRING
      >,
      annotations ROW<
        callback STRING,
        desc STRING,
        imageTimestamp STRING,
        isMeter STRING,
        predictions STRING
      >
    >,
    created_at TIMESTAMP(3),
    updated_at TIMESTAMP(3),
    deleted_at TIMESTAMP(3),
    delete_status TINYINT,
    -- Processing time
    proc_time AS PROCTIME(),
    PRIMARY KEY (uuid) NOT ENFORCED
   ) WITH (
    'connector' = 'hudi',
    'path' = 's3a://catalog_name/data_pool2/data/file_metadata_cow_1_4',
    'table.type' = 'COPY_ON_WRITE',
    'hoodie.datasource.write.recordkey.field' = 'uuid',
    'hoodie.datasource.write.precombine.field' = 'updated_at',
    -- Partition configuration
    'hoodie.datasource.write.partitionpath.field' = 'tenant_id,file_format,source_channel',
    -- Lock configuration
    'hoodie.write.lock.provider' = 'org.apache.hudi.client.transaction.lock.InProcessLockProvider'
   );
   ```

2. Run a simple query in Trino:
   
   sql
   
   ```sql
   SELECT * FROM hudi_catalog_2.data_pool2.file_metadata_cow_1_4;
   ```

3. The query fails with the following error:
   
   ```text
   Query 20250320_073504_00043_kf9gm failed: Internal error
   ```

4. The only relevant log from the Trino Docker container is:
   
   ```text
   2025-03-20T07:35:04.474Z  INFO  dispatcher-query-81  io.trino.event.QueryMonitor
   TIMELINE: Query 20250320_073504_00043_kf9gm :: FAILED (GENERIC_INTERNAL_ERROR) :: elapsed 395ms :: planning 395ms :: waiting 0ms :: scheduling 0ms :: running 0ms :: finishing 0ms :: begin 2025-03-20T07:35:04.078Z :: end 2025-03-20T07:35:04.473Z
   ```

### Observations

- The issue affects both COW and MOR tables in Hudi 1.0.x.

- Queries succeed in Trino with Hudi 0.14.0 and in Flink with Hudi 1.0.1, indicating a compatibility issue between Trino 473 and Hudi 1.0.1.

- The failure occurs during the query planning phase, suggesting potential issues with metadata parsing or query planning.

- Hive Metastore metadata is intact, as confirmed by successful queries in Flink.

### Suspected Cause

Hudi 1.0.1 may have introduced changes (e.g., in metadata format or table structure) that are not yet supported by Trino’s Hudi connector in version 473.

### Questions

- Does Trino 473 support Hudi 1.0.1 for COW and MOR tables?

- If not, is there a planned update to add support, or are there any known workarounds to enable querying these tables?

- Could you provide any guidance on debugging or resolving the GENERIC_INTERNAL_ERROR?

Thank you for your time and support!

items.title: Unit tests for consumer parsing and API routing
items.body:
**Goal:** fast tests (no Docker) for pure logic. Independent of the e2e tickets.

## Context
- `cdc-consumer/consumer.py`: `CDCConsumer.convert_date` (Debezium date = int days since epoch -> ISO string),
  op mapping (`c/u/d/r` -> INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/INSERT), `TENANT_MAPPING` topic -> tenant, and `stage_record`
  (builds the INSERT into `person_staging`). Message parsing and mapping are inline inside `consume_messages`
  and `__init__` connects to Kafka/DB, so they are hard to test.
- `api/api.py`: `LEGACY_DB_CONFIG` routing (legacy_a vs legacy_b column choice), validation (400s), and SQL chosen
  per type. DB access via `get_legacy_conn`/`get_new_system_conn` (psycopg2).

## Tasks
1. Small refactor allowed (behaviour-preserving): extract from consumer a pure function
   `parse_event(topic, raw_bytes) -> (tenant_id, operation, row_dict) | None`, and make `CDCConsumer.__init__`
   not required for testing it (module-level function).
2. `tests/unit/test_consumer.py`: convert_date (None, int, str, 0, 19000), op mapping, unknown topic -> None,
   payload with and without the `payload` wrapper, `after: null` (delete) case - record the current behaviour
   and `xfail` if it is wrong (see ticket 03, bug 2).
3. `tests/unit/test_api.py` using Flask `test_client()` and monkeypatched `get_legacy_conn`/`get_new_system_conn`
   (fake cursor recording SQL+params): POST for a tenant_a* writes `data_2`, for tenant_b* writes `data_c`;
   400 for missing fields / unknown tenant; PUT requires `tenant_id` and `legacy_id`; PUT with `modernized_only`
   issues the new-system UPDATE; empty `extra_field` handling.
4. Note `api/api.py` runs `time.sleep(10)` only under `__main__`, so importing it is safe.
5. Requirements in `requirements-test.txt` (pytest). Mock `confluent_kafka` import if not installed.

## Done when
`pytest tests/unit` passes in <5s with no network/Docker.

---
## Shared project context (all tickets)
- Pipeline: 4 legacy Postgres DBs (tenants `tenant_a1`, `tenant_a2` = Legacy A with `data_1/2/3`;
  `tenant_b1`, `tenant_b2` = Legacy B with `data_a/b/c`) -> Debezium -> Kafka topics
  `legacy_<x>.public.person` -> `cdc-consumer/consumer.py` -> `person_staging` (new-system DB)
  -> `dbt run` (`dbt-project/models/person_unified.sql`, incremental, alias `person`) -> `person`.
- `data_2` (A) and `data_c` (B) both map to `extra_field`. `modernized_only` (DATE) exists only in the new system.
- API (Flask, `api/api.py`, port 5000): `GET/POST/PUT /api/persons`, `/api/legacy/<tenant>/persons[/<id>]`, `/api/health`.
  POST/PUT write to the legacy DB; the change returns via CDC.
- Compose services (`docker-compose.yml`): kafka, schema-registry, postgres-legacy-{a1,a2,b1,b2},
  postgres-new-system, debezium (8083), cdc-consumer, api (5000), web (8000).
  Credentials: legacy `legacyuser/legacypass` (dbs `legacy_a1` etc.), new system `newuser/newpass` (db `new_system`).
- Currently there are NO automated tests. `TESTING.md` is a manual runbook.

items.title: P3 OPUS — Two physical tenant shards, tenant router and partition-aware dashboard
items.body:
## Goal and motivation
Judge feedback after Round 1: show **real horizontal sharding** plus behavior under **network partitions**, not merely tenant_id isolation in a single DB. Implement a bounded sharded demo on top of PR #18's FastAPI + pg_trickle stack; retain exact tenant analytics.

## Starting point
- main at 6d867a8; PR #18 `feat/hackathon-dashboard-api` is OPEN and still targets old `feat/hackathon-frontend` though PR #16 is merged. Retarget/rebase safely, review, and do not auto-merge.
- Existing source keys: `(tenant_id, order_id)`, `(tenant_id, product_id)`, `(tenant_id, customer_id)`. Three stream-table queries group by tenant_id.
- The current `db.py` pools bind to one `AX_DB_HOST`; `compose.yaml` contains one `db`. This is not sharding.
- pg_trickle does not support a stream table whose sources span different databases. Each shard must have its own three stream tables and scheduler.
- User's Fedora machine previously had only ~1.3GiB available RAM and used swap. DO NOT start multiple DBs / memory-heavy builds if current preflight makes it unsafe.

## Approved P3 bounded design proposal (build on isolated branch/worktree)
1. Two **independent PostgreSQL DB server instances** `shard_a`, `shard_b`, with **distinct source data and volumes**, each with three pg_trickle stream tables, required roles, RLS and oracle. Seed **10,000 orders TOTAL**, not 10k per shard, spread across 10 tenants; 100k only if resource preflight allows and the human approves.
2. Stable explicit, versioned tenant-to-shard directory. For the current 40/20/rest skew: A tenants {1,3,4}, B {2,5,6,7,8,9,10}, approximately 50/50 orders. Validate no tenant exists on both shards and that all keys/joins are tenant-local. Never use arbitrary modulo reassignment once rows exist.
3. Tenant-aware FastAPI routing at the DB connection factory, **not** in frontend only; route requests, writer mutations, RLS session variables, and SQL-oracle requests to tenant's owning shard. Connection pools per shard with bounded size and timeouts. Auth tenant check runs BEFORE routing. Never issue write to another shard when owner is unreachable.
4. Keep existing `/api/tenants/{id}` contract; expose operator-only `/api/shards` with each shard's health, assigned tenants, per-shard refresh status, pending CDC work, and explicit partial/degraded states. For global views, never silently present a partial result as a complete total.
5. Add `hackathon/compose.sharded.yaml` (or clearly named isolated demo override), `hackathon/sharding/**` as needed, simple runbook and small safely seeded live writer (initial rate <= 2 changes/sec). Isolated project name, ports, networks and volumes; do not change existing Compose data or delete volumes.
6. Document failure semantics: when router cannot reach shard A, tenant A reads/writes return **503**, with bounded timeout, no phantom success, no cross-shard fallback; B tenants still work. Dashboard clearly shows A unavailable. On network restoration, A resumes, refreshes catch up, direct SQL oracle returns 0 mismatch. Demonstrate partition + recovery with owned demo network only, not uncontrolled host/network changes.
7. Do NOT claim automated failover, quorum, replication, AP or 10M acceptance. Fail-closed per-shard partition handling with healthy-shard continuity is an honest bounded step. Follow-up replica/leader election is a separate proposal.
8. Source-code patch for `pg_trickle` P1 null-safe join is still untested; do not modify upstream Rust. Preserve existing correctness oracle, exact time boundaries and RLS; add tests for inserts, updates/cancellations, cross-tenant 403, cross-shard 503.

## Ownership and handoff
OPUS owns `hackathon/app/**`, `hackathon/frontend/**`, `hackathon/sql/**`, `hackathon/compose.sharded.yaml`, `hackathon/sharding/**`, and `hackathon/docs/handoffs/opus-sharding.md` for this task. CODEX owns benchmark/fault-injection checks under `hackathon/benchmark/**` and must not edit Opus-owned paths. Coordinate status + API contract in #12.

## Acceptance (must be demonstrated, not assumed)
- A and B have disjoint tenant/order rows; global counts match seed; baseline single-DB oracle unchanged.
- Tenant on A and tenant on B each have correct API results; one real mutation per shard appears in its local stream tables.
- During isolated network partition A, A requests fail explicitly, B succeeds, no data leakage/false successful writes; upon recovery A's oracle passes.
- Record measured query latency, commit→visible lag, OLTP throughput delta and resource use, including failures; do not invent compliance with G1–G5.
- End in PR + DONE_WAITING_REVIEW; no auto-merge, no 10M, no destructive data operations. If hardware unsafe, produce working code/tests with NOT RUN status and stop.

items.title: Durable repo-external community activity substrate

labels.name: epic
labels.description: A big time intense ticket with related sub-tasks

items.body:
## Context

Discussion #15139 graduated Neo's missing repo-global community-activity source: a durable, replayable way to notice external issues, pull requests, reviews, comments, Discussion replies, edits, deletions, and state transitions without turning provider noise into assignment, ranking authority, or wake storms.

The live falsifier was a new external reply inside an already-closed Discussion that Neo discovered late. Existing addressed-notification routing admits only narrow per-viewer reasons, existing repository sync stores current resource snapshots with bounded child coverage, and runtime readers require a known resource before they can inspect its conversation. Five cross-family design cycles established that the gap is not “add another GitHub MCP method”; it is the authority chain from provider acquisition through durable admission, queryable awareness, and explicit claim.

This requires an Epic because the converged shape crosses independently owned source adapters, Memory Core operational state, tenant isolation, Bird View contracts, A2A Task claim authority, local/hosted connector topology, instrumentation, and optional attention projection. A single PR cannot safely establish those contracts and their executable evidence.

## The Problem

Neo currently has three useful but incomplete primitives:

- addressed GitHub notification delivery for `mention|review_requested`;
- eventual repository content sync and bounded conversation reads;
- temporal Bird Views and A2A Task state machinery for already-admitted facts.

None is a repo-global event ledger. A per-viewer notification coalesces occurrences; a resource snapshot cannot prove which edit/delete/reply was observed; compacted GraphLog is CDC rather than permanent history; and Task creation alone cannot prevent two peers from minting two canonical Tasks for one source event.

The cloud boundary makes a local-only fix structurally wrong. One tenant may register multiple repositories; connectors own provider acquisition and secrets; Memory Core must own neutral tenant-scoped admission; every dedicated-table read/write must enforce server-authoritative tenant/source isolation; and automatic paths may carry only metadata/counts until explicit trust-projected drill-down.

## Intended Solution Shape

Establish one provider-neutral community-activity authority chain:

1. **Completeness:** exhaustive resource-family reconciliation is authoritative. Notifications, webhooks, repository events, Actions, and root deltas are accelerators only.
2. **Admission:** a provider connector submits reproducible normalized batches into a tenant-scoped Memory-Core transaction keyed by server-owned registration. Connector-local durable capture is added only when an acquired batch cannot be reconstructed after crash or ambiguous admission.
3. **Identity:** source registration, provider entity, occurrence/revision, retry batch, delivery attempt, monotonic admitted sequence, checkpoint, and later Task binding remain distinct identities.
4. **Registration:** Memory Core owns a neutral lifecycle `REQUESTED → PROVISIONED → ACTIVE → REVOKED`; connectors own provider grants/secrets. Local single-user deployments may use subject=tenant; hosted bootstrap is deployment-operator managed until a real tenant-membership/source-admin authority exists.
5. **Read path:** a provider-neutral temporal Bird View inherits the existing citation, coverage, pagination, and honest-degradation envelope. Automatic hooks/wakes remain tenant-scoped metadata/count-only; prose requires explicit tenant/source-relative trust projection.
6. **Claim:** one unique atomic `sourceEventId → taskId` binding precedes existing A2A Task authority. Community activity remains outside `LifecycleFrontier` until that explicit transition.
7. **Attention:** ship the Bird View and bounded count-only projection before any leased steward wake. No cadence, retention, TTL, steward, pagination, or wake threshold becomes code-ready before shadow instrumentation supplies the named measurements.

The initial consistency posture is one Memory-Core SQLite/WAL instance. Horizontal multi-writer or HA requirements reopen ADR 0015 rather than silently weakening compare-and-set semantics. Registration is not AiConfig: ADR 0019 continues to govern actual Agent OS configuration, while community-source registration has its own operational lifecycle. ADR 0035 remains authoritative for zero-authority federation and keeps unclaimed community items outside `LifecycleFrontier`.

The retained observation window binds caller revision, selected tenant/source registration and admission receipts to the actual resolved store in the deployment plane. Its provenance record includes a redacted store identity or digest and the plane-coherence result; unavailable bindings remain unknown. Test-store selection flags alone do not attest deployment provenance. This keeps scratch-store overrides distinguishable during the [independent runtime-provenance audit](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-brain/pull/1322#pullrequestreview-5674570490).

The live parent-child relationship graph remains authoritative for decomposition. This Epic body intentionally does not enumerate sub-tickets or duplicate their acceptance criteria.

## Architectural Reality

The Agent OS structure map was executed on 2026-07-14. Current ownership boundaries are:

- source-specific acquisition/conversation trust: `ai/services/github-workflow/`;
- local connector coordination: `ai/daemons/orchestrator/` and `ai/daemons/orchestrator/services/TenantRepoSyncService.mjs`;
- provider-neutral durable admission/query state: `ai/services/memory-core/` plus its established SQLite operational-store helpers;
- public tool contracts: `ai/mcp/server/github-workflow/` and `ai/mcp/server/memory-core/`;
- source-relative content trust: `ai/services/shared/contentTrust/`;
- Native Edge Graph: explicitly not the community historical ledger.

Shipped siblings to inherit include `PullRequestHistoryService` for exhaustive temporal conversation reads, `TenantRepoSyncService` for acquisition→neutral-admission dependency direction, current trust projection helpers, stable event-id/typed-event machinery, and the existing temporal Bird-View envelope.

## Signal Ledger

- `gpt` author family: [AUTHOR_SIGNAL by @neo-gpt](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/15139#discussioncomment-17631283) at body `updatedAt 2026-07-14T04:49:30Z`.
- `claude` non-author family: [GRADUATION_APPROVED by @neo-opus-grace](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/15139#discussioncomment-17631315) at body `updatedAt 2026-07-14T04:49:30Z`.
- `gemini`: inactive for quorum; `@neo-gemini-pro` is `operator_benched`.

## Unresolved Dissent

None at graduation. Grace's §5.2 sweep dispositioned 8/8 points with 0 blockers. The author's temporary timing objection was explicitly superseded by the operator's waiver and did not challenge the converged architecture.

## Unresolved Liveness

Gemini family is operator-benched. Revalidation trigger: if Gemini returns while this Epic is active, request an independent challenge of (a) reconciliation completeness and provider revision identity, (b) tenant registration/RLS and local-vs-hosted authorization, and (c) instrumentation-gated attention/wake thresholds. A material blocker reopens the relevant contract through Discussion #15139 and ADR 0036.

## Discussion Criteria Mapping

- **Divergence/peer cycle:** five peer cycles, the operator waiver, the complete 24-option convergence disposition, and exact-anchor quorum are preserved in Discussion #15139 and this Signal Ledger.
- **Source coverage:** the resource × event-family matrix maps to exhaustive reconciliation plus explicit unsupported/loss semantics in the Intended Solution Shape.
- **Identity/replay:** registration, batch, occurrence/revision, admitted sequence, receipt, checkpoint, and Task binding are separate contract identities.
- **Durable owner:** tenant-scoped Memory Core owns neutral operational history; provider-local capture is conditional; Native Edge Graph and GraphLog are not historical authority.
- **Seen/claim/resolve:** per-viewer seen state is non-authority; one atomic source-event→canonical-Task transition enters existing A2A authority.
- **Consumers:** Bird View, bounded count-only projection, staged wake, future Fleet reads, and METRIC use preserve evidence-not-intent and no-ranking boundaries.
- **Trust/tenancy:** automatic paths are metadata/count-only; drill-down is trust-projected; dedicated tables apply tenant/source RLS on every read/write and are never `sharedEntity` or `visibility:'team'`.
- **Deployment portability:** local L and hosted M share one neutral contract; N is transitional; O is measurement-gated; T/R own registration; U/W are the initial mutation authorities; V/X remain deferred.
- **Density/cost:** shadow instrumentation is the first implementation gate and no operational threshold is intuition-derived.
- **Step-Back:** tenant-relative trust, atomic `sourceEventId → taskId`, and shadow-first measurement are mandatory downstream contracts.
- **Decision record:** ADR 0036 is required before threshold-bearing or authority-bearing implementation becomes code-ready.

## Decision Record

**Required: ADR 0036, first in merge order.**

Decision Record impact: **depends on ADR 0015, aligns with ADR 0019, and composes ADR 0035 without superseding them.** ADR 0036 must make the durable event/admission identity model, tenant/source isolation, source-registration lifecycle, local/hosted connector boundary, Task-claim transition, Bird-View authority, trust projection, shadow-first measurement, and explicit revalidation triggers durable. The human merge gate accepting ADR 0036 is the implementation authority transition.

## Out of Scope

- Horizontal multi-writer/HA Memory Core; that reopens ADR 0015.
- Treating the community ledger as Native Edge Graph ontology or GraphLog as permanent history.
- Importing community activity into Golden Path ranking, automatic assignment, or `LifecycleFrontier` before explicit claim.
- Tenant self-service administration before an authoritative membership/source-admin substrate exists.
- Automatic title/body/excerpt delivery; prose stays behind explicit trust-projected drill-down.
- A neutral HTTP/queue receiver without measured backpressure that falsifies authenticated connector push.
- GitLab implementation in the first adapter; the consumer/admission contract must nevertheless remain provider-neutral.
- Cadence, retention, TTL, steward, or wake values selected from intuition.

## Avoided Traps

- **Expand notifications only:** rejected because addressed, per-viewer thread state is not repo-global occurrence history.
- **Pull-only explorer:** rejected as durability; retained as the Bird-View consumer.
- **Graph snapshot / compacted GraphLog as ledger:** rejected because snapshot state and CDC cannot preserve required history.
- **Webhook-only authority:** rejected because delivery can be missed/reordered and local deployments lack a receiver.
- **All-resident wake:** rejected because rare signal does not justify duplicated interruption and tenant fan-out leaks authority.
- **Knowledge Base / AiConfig registration:** rejected because activity-source lifecycle must not mutate configuration freshness or reimplement ADR 0019.
- **Connector-local registry as neutral authority:** rejected because provider migration must preserve one durable source identity.
- **`sharedEntity` / `visibility:'team'`:** rejected because those bypass tenant-private community isolation.
- **MCP `admin` projection as authorization:** rejected because authentication/tool tier is not tenant membership.
- **Premature self-service or queue topology:** deferred until the missing authority/scale evidence exists.

items.title: PostgreSQL 18 is the minimum supported version (floor, enforcement, and the simplifications it allows)
items.body:
## Decision

**PostgreSQL 18 becomes the minimum supported version.** FraiseQL is built for self-hosting, so managed-provider version lag does not constrain it.

## Why

The documented floor is not what is tested:

- `docs/database-compatibility.md` claims "PostgreSQL 14+";
- CI runs only `postgres:16` (plus one stray `postgres:11`), so nothing verifies 14 or 15;
- PostgreSQL 14 reaches end of life in November 2026.

A single supported major version removes the "does this work on 14?" question from every migration. It also lets the engine use:

| Feature | Since | Use in FraiseQL |
|---|---|---|
| `NULLS NOT DISTINCT` | 15 | Each partial-index *pair* in the account store (#1088) becomes one index. |
| `MERGE … RETURNING` | 17 | Upsert-shaped mutations as one statement. |
| `JSON_TABLE` and SQL/JSON | 17 | Simpler compiled SQL over JSONB `data` columns. |
| `RETURNING OLD.*, NEW.*` | 18 | Before/after row images straight from the write, for `after:mutation` (#1340/#1440), CDC and `when` predicates. |
| `uuidv7()` | 18 | Time-ordered keys in place of `gen_random_uuid()` (v4), for B-tree locality. |
| B-tree skip scan | 18 | `(tenant_id, …)` indexes serve queries that do not filter on the tenant. |
| Asynchronous I/O, virtual generated columns | 18 | Free read performance; computed columns without storage. |

## Scope

### 1. Floor: tested and enforced
- Every CI image moves to PostgreSQL 18: `.dagger/main.go`, workflows, `ghcr.io/fraiseql/postgres`, pgvector, and the stray `postgres:11`. Same for `docker-compose` files, examples and the dev `make db-up`.
- The server refuses to boot against a server below 18 (`server_version_num < 180000`), naming the version found and the minimum. The CLI's database commands refuse the same way. Do not leave it to an obscure SQL error later.
- Docs (`database-compatibility.md` and every "14+" or "14 floor" mention) and CHANGELOG `### Breaking`, with the upgrade path (`pg_upgrade` / dump-restore).

### 2. Simplifications the floor allows
Each is its own PR, TDD, and has no version-detection dual paths:
- Collapse the account-store partial-index pairs into `NULLS NOT DISTINCT` unique indexes, migrated in place.
- Audit every other PG < 18 workaround in the tree (grep for "PostgreSQL 14", "PG 14", "NULLS NOT DISTINCT", `COALESCE(tenant_id, '0000…')`-style uniqueness).

### 3. Evaluations (separate issues, decided by measurement)
- `RETURNING OLD/NEW` for mutation responses and the after-mutation row image.
- `uuidv7()` as the default id generator.
- `JSON_TABLE` / SQL/JSON in the compiler's generated SQL.

## Also check
- pg_tviews and pgvector on 18.
- Logical-replication and CDC paths (`cdc-outbound`, observers' change log).
- Any `pg_catalog` queries whose shape changed between 16 and 18.

items.title: ReplicationPoller restarts the db_events RateCounter with the limit read at init, ignoring a changed max_events_per_second
items.body:
## Bug

Raising a tenant's `max_events_per_second` doesn't change the Postgres Changes limit while its `ReplicationPoller` is running. The update stops the `{:channel, :db_events, tenant_id}` `RateCounter`, and the poller starts it again with the limit it read in `init/1`. The poller keeps dropping changes at the old threshold.

This is the Postgres Changes counterpart of #2274, which #2275 fixed for channels. #2274 mentions this case as a follow-up.

## Deterministic reproduction

In `test/extensions/postgres_cdc_rls/replication_poller_test.exs` (`describe "poll"`, tenant at `max_events_per_second: 123`):

1. Start the poller and let it poll once. The `db_events` counter has `limit.value == 123`.
2. Call `Realtime.Api.update_tenant_by_external_id(tenant_id, %{"max_events_per_second" => 1_000})`. `maybe_restart_rate_counters/1` publishes `:update` for `db_events_per_second_key/1`, and the counter stops. Its cache entry expires one second later.
3. Have the next poll return a change. The poller calls `RateCounter.get(state.rate_counter_args)`.

## Expected

The restarted counter enforces `limit.value == 1_000`.

## Actual

The restarted counter has `limit.value == 123`.

## Root cause

`ReplicationPoller.init/1` builds `rate_counter_args = Tenants.db_events_per_second_rate(tenant)` once and keeps it in state. `RateCounter.get/1` starts a missing counter with the args it's given. Since #1479/#1584, the poller is the only process that gets or starts the `db_events` counter, so after the restart from #1669 it's always the poller that brings the counter back, and always with the init-time limit. A `max_events_per_second` change doesn't restart the poller: only `extensions`, `jwt_secret`, `jwt_jwks` and `suspend` do. The new limit therefore only applies after the poller restarts for some other reason.

## Impact

When a tenant that's hitting `MessagePerSecondRateLimitReached: Too many postgres changes messages per second` gets a higher limit, the poller keeps skipping changes (`[:realtime, :replication, :poller, :changes, :skip]` with `reason: :rate_limited`) at the old threshold. The slot has already consumed those changes, so they're never delivered. Lowering the limit is also ignored, so the poller keeps sending at the old, higher rate.

items.title: PRD: real-time pipeline activity and errors pane in the web UI
items.body:
## Problem
The demo UI shows data (legacy tables and the unified `person` table) but not *what the pipeline is doing*. When a record
is saved in a legacy system, the audience cannot see the change travel Debezium -> Kafka -> consumer -> staging -> dbt ->
`person`, and when something goes wrong (DB down, a message dead-lettered, a dbt batch failing and wedging the stack) the
only way to find out is `make logs`. The pipeline has several known silent-failure modes (issues #4, #12), so visibility
is also a debugging need, not just a demo nicety.

## Goal
A pane docked at the bottom of the web UI (:8000) that shows, in near real time, **what is happening in the pipeline**:
each change as it moves through the stages, and every error, newest first, without opening a terminal.

## Users
- **Presenter** running the demo: wants to point at a change and show it arriving.
- **Developer/tester** (this repo's owner): wants errors surfaced the moment they happen, and to confirm a test scenario
  did what was expected.

## Non-goals
- No log aggregation product (ELK/Loki/Grafana), no metrics history, no auth, no multi-user concerns. This is a POC.
- No raw container log streaming. **Containers must not get Docker access** (repo hard rule), so the API cannot tail
  `docker logs`. Components report their own events instead.
- Not a replacement for `make logs`/`make debug`.

## Proposed behaviour

### The pane
- Fixed/collapsible bottom pane, full width; a header strip with counts (events/min, errors, dead-lettered) and a
  **pipeline status line**: Debezium connectors (4x RUNNING/FAILED), consumer last activity, staging backlog
  (`processed = FALSE` rows), dead-letter count.
- Event list, newest on top, auto-scrolling unless the user has scrolled/paused. Controls: pause/resume, clear (view
  only), filter by tenant, filter by severity (info / warn / error), free-text search.
- Each row: time, tenant, stage badge, one-line summary (e.g. `tenant_a1 person#42 UPDATE staged`), severity colour.
  Click to expand the detail (Kafka topic/partition/offset, error text, raw payload for dead letters).
- Errors are visually distinct and sticky: an error count badge on the collapsed pane so a closed pane still signals trouble.

### Events to show (stage -> what)
| Stage | Emitted by | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| `api` | API | write-through accepted / failed (`POST/PUT` to legacy tenant), validation 400s |
| `consumer.received` | cdc-consumer | message received (topic, partition, offset, op) |
| `consumer.staged` | cdc-consumer | record staged (tenant, id, operation) |
| `consumer.retry` | cdc-consumer | DB error, message rewound and retried (attempt count) |
| `consumer.dead_letter` | cdc-consumer | message could not be staged (see #12), with error and payload |
| `dbt` | cdc-consumer | dbt run started / finished (duration, rows staged in batch) / **failed** (stderr tail) |
| `connector` | API (polls Debezium REST) | connector state change (RUNNING -> FAILED etc.) |

A single change should be traceable end to end by `(tenant_id, legacy_id)` so the pane can group or highlight one record's journey.

## Proposed design (open to change in review)
Because components cannot be log-scraped, the **new-system Postgres is the event bus for the pane**:
1. New table `pipeline_event(id BIGSERIAL, ts TIMESTAMPTZ, source, stage, severity, tenant_id, legacy_id, message, detail JSONB)`.
   Created idempotently by the writer (same approach as `person_dead_letter` in #12) so existing volumes work. Capped
   retention (e.g. delete rows older than 24h or beyond N rows, done by the consumer).
2. cdc-consumer and API insert events at the points above. Event writes must be **best effort and never break the
   pipeline**: a failure to write an event is swallowed (printed) and must not affect staging or offset commits.
3. API: `GET /api/events?since_id=<n>&limit=<m>&severity=&tenant=` returns events with `id > since_id`, plus
   `GET /api/pipeline/status` for the status line (connector states via Debezium REST `:8083`, staging backlog, dead-letter
   count, last consumer activity).
4. UI: polls `/api/events?since_id=` every ~1s (the UI already polls with `setInterval`; keep that style). Server-Sent
   Events is a possible later upgrade, not required for v1.
5. Single-file UI (`web/index.html`) keeps its current structure; no build step or framework introduced.

Alternatives considered: (a) stream container logs via Docker socket - rejected (root on host); (b) emit events to a
Kafka topic and have the API consume it - more moving parts for a POC, but nicer fan-out; revisit if polling Postgres
proves too slow; (c) parse stdout in a log-shipper sidecar - needs Docker log access.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A bottom pane is visible on :8000 and can be collapsed/expanded; collapsed state still shows an error badge.
- [ ] Creating or updating a person via the UI shows, within ~3s, the chain `api` -> `consumer.received` -> `consumer.staged` -> `dbt` for that record.
- [ ] A dead-lettered message (#12) and a failed dbt run each appear as `error` events with detail.
- [ ] Stopping `postgres-new-system` shows consumer retry events once the DB is back (events are written when possible); stopping a Debezium connector shows a connector state change in the status line.
- [ ] Filtering by tenant/severity, pause/resume and expand-for-detail work.
- [ ] An event-write failure (events table unavailable) does not stop staging or change offset-commit behaviour (unit test).
- [ ] Event table growth is bounded.
- [ ] Unit tests for event emission and `/api/events` (since_id paging, filters); an e2e test that a created record produces the expected stage sequence. Docs updated (README, `docs/TESTING.md`). All via `make` in Docker.

## Open questions
1. Is a ~1s polling delay acceptable, or do we want SSE/WebSocket from the start?
2. Retention: time-based, row-count-based, or both? Should errors be kept longer than info events?
3. Should the pane also show Kafka consumer lag (needs Kafka admin calls from the API)?
4. Show raw payloads in the UI (may contain personal data in a real deployment; fine for the POC's fake data)?

## Suggested breakdown
1. Event table + best-effort emit helper (consumer, API) + unit tests.
2. `/api/events` and `/api/pipeline/status` + tests.
3. UI pane (list, filters, status line, error badge).
4. Debezium connector state polling, dbt run/failed events.
5. e2e test and docs.

Depends on: #12 (dead-letter table and retry events). Related: #4.

items.title: End-to-end pytest harness + happy-path tests
items.body:
**Goal:** an automated, self-asserting replacement for TESTING.md scenarios 1-7.

## Context
See shared context in README.md. Tests run on the host against the running compose stack
(`docker compose up -d --wait`); the stack takes ~30s+ to settle (consumer sleeps 30s at start, api 10s).
Host access: API `http://localhost:5000`, Debezium `http://localhost:8083`. Postgres ports are probably NOT published
to the host - check `docker-compose.yml`; if not, either add published ports on a test override file
(`docker-compose.test.yml`) or write legacy rows through the API's `POST /api/legacy/<tenant>/persons`
(this exists and takes `firstname, surname, date_of_birth, city, data_1/2/3` or `data_a/b/c`).

## Tasks
1. Create `tests/e2e/` with `conftest.py`, `requirements-test.txt` (pytest, requests, psycopg2-binary).
2. Helpers: `wait_until(fn, timeout=30, interval=0.5)` that polls (NO fixed sleeps); an `api` client fixture;
   a session fixture that waits for `/api/health` and all 4 Debezium connectors RUNNING
   (`GET /connectors/<name>/status`, names `legacy-a1-connector` ... `legacy-b2-connector`).
3. Use unique names per test (uuid in `surname`) so tests do not depend on a clean DB and can run repeatedly.
4. Tests (each asserts via `GET /api/persons` polling):
   - insert directly into legacy A and legacy B -> appears with correct `tenant_id`, and `extra_field`
     == `data_2` / `data_c` respectively.
   - POST `/api/persons` for each of the 4 tenants -> legacy row exists AND synced row appears; returned `legacy_id` matches.
   - PUT `/api/persons` -> new values appear in new system.
   - Tenant isolation: same-named person in two tenants stays two rows; PUT to tenant X with a `legacy_id` that
     exists in tenant Y does not change Y's row.
   - Unknown tenant -> 400; missing required fields -> 400.
5. Add `pytest.ini` with a `e2e` marker and a 60s per-test timeout.

## Done when
`pytest tests/e2e` passes twice in a row against a fresh `docker compose up`, with no `sleep` > 1s used for sync waits.
Out of scope: deletes, modernized_only, failure injection (ticket 03), CI (ticket 05).

---
## Shared project context (all tickets)
- Pipeline: 4 legacy Postgres DBs (tenants `tenant_a1`, `tenant_a2` = Legacy A with `data_1/2/3`;
  `tenant_b1`, `tenant_b2` = Legacy B with `data_a/b/c`) -> Debezium -> Kafka topics
  `legacy_<x>.public.person` -> `cdc-consumer/consumer.py` -> `person_staging` (new-system DB)
  -> `dbt run` (`dbt-project/models/person_unified.sql`, incremental, alias `person`) -> `person`.
- `data_2` (A) and `data_c` (B) both map to `extra_field`. `modernized_only` (DATE) exists only in the new system.
- API (Flask, `api/api.py`, port 5000): `GET/POST/PUT /api/persons`, `/api/legacy/<tenant>/persons[/<id>]`, `/api/health`.
  POST/PUT write to the legacy DB; the change returns via CDC.
- Compose services (`docker-compose.yml`): kafka, schema-registry, postgres-legacy-{a1,a2,b1,b2},
  postgres-new-system, debezium (8083), cdc-consumer, api (5000), web (8000).
  Credentials: legacy `legacyuser/legacypass` (dbs `legacy_a1` etc.), new system `newuser/newpass` (db `new_system`).
- Currently there are NO automated tests. `TESTING.md` is a manual runbook.
