items.title: SQL Server: the plugin-owned workflow-name columns become exact too (D60 follow-up to #3635)
items.body:
**Filed by WS-cleat-3 (WS-3) at the coordinator's request. Unclaimed.**

Migration `011` (#3635, owner D60) makes every workflow-definition name column that **core** migrations create compare exactly on SQL Server. Three plugins create tables of their own at worker boot, outside the core migration chain, and a core migration cannot name a table that may not exist yet. Their definition-name columns are still `SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS` after #3635, so D60 is not complete until they move too.

**Measured 2026-10-30** on a scratch SQL Server 2022 database that had booted a worker (so the plugin tables exist), by catalog query:

| plugin | table.column | type | collation |
|---|---|---|---|
| eventtriggers | `dbo.event_subscriptions.def_name` | nvarchar(max) | SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS |
| scheduler | `dbo.schedules.workflow_name` | nvarchar(max) | SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS |
| jobqueue | `dbo.task_queue.def_name` | nvarchar(max) | SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS |

```sql
SELECT SCHEMA_NAME(t.schema_id)+'.'+t.name+'.'+c.name, c.max_length, c.collation_name
FROM sys.columns c JOIN sys.tables t ON t.object_id=c.object_id
WHERE c.collation_name IS NOT NULL AND (c.name LIKE '%workflow%' OR c.name LIKE '%def%');
```

**Limit of that list:** it covers the plugins whose tables exist in that database. A plugin that did not boot there, or one whose column is not named like `*workflow*` / `*def*`, would not appear. Whoever takes this should re-derive it against a worker with every built-in plugin enabled.

**Scope (the same rule as #3635):** each plugin's migration (`plugins/eventtriggers/migrations.go`, `plugins/scheduler/migrations.go`, `plugins/jobqueue/migrations.go`) converts its own definition-name column to `Latin1_General_100_BIN2` on SQL Server, with the same care #3635 took: check for dependent indexes and constraints before altering (these are `nvarchar(max)`, so none can be indexed, but verify rather than assume), and a before/after lookup on a seeded mixed-case name. #3635 measured that changing the collation of an unindexed column with unchanged type and nullability is metadata-only on SQL Server 2022 (1M-row `event_history.child_name`: no measurable time).

**Not in scope:** MySQL (#3640). Instance/run-id columns (#3639).

Carried from #3635 so that it can close honestly.

items.title: De-identified analytics warehouse

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
## Situation

Issue #481 delivers the pipeline that moves data out of the clinical OLTP cluster into a per-country analytical lake. It deliberately does not decide what is *allowed* to be in that lake. Without this issue, the conformed layer carries patient names, phone numbers, addresses, ABHA numbers and free-text clinical notes — a full PHI copy sitting outside the clinical access-control perimeter, queryable by anyone with an analyst role. That is a larger exposure than having no warehouse at all.

The DPDP Act 2023 permits processing only for the purpose for which consent was given. Analytics, product telemetry and benchmarking are not the purpose a patient consented to when they were admitted. The lawful route is to remove identifiability before analytical use, so that the data ceases to be personal data for those purposes. The platform's architectural rules already state that analytics holds de-identified or aggregated data only, and that identifiable PHI must never be exposed in analytics without a lawful basis.

The tension is that de-identified data still has to be *useful*. A hospital admin needs readmission rates by department, a lab manager needs turnaround time by test and analyser, a clinical governance lead needs sepsis-bundle compliance — all of which require stable patient linkage across encounters without knowing who the patient is. Naive column-dropping destroys longitudinal analysis; naive hashing of an ABHA number is trivially reversible by anyone who can guess candidate values.

Affected roles: the **DPO**, who must be able to state what leaves the clinical perimeter and in what form; the **hospital admin** and **lab manager**, whose reporting depends on this; and the platform **data engineer**, who needs one enforced transform rather than per-dataset judgement calls.

---

## Task

### User or System Story

**As a** Data Protection Officer
**I want** the analytical serving layer to contain only de-identified or aggregated data, produced by an enforced, auditable transform, with a narrow and separately authorised re-identification path
**So that** analytics is lawful under the DPDP Act 2023 while remaining clinically useful for longitudinal and cohort reporting.

### Scope

**In scope**

* A **de-identification transform** applied between the conformed and serving layers of the #481 lake, driven by the classification registry from #480 — no dataset reaches `serving/` untransformed.
* **Pseudonymisation** of patient, practitioner and staff identifiers using keyed HMAC with a per-country, per-purpose salt held in KMS, producing stable research IDs that support longitudinal linkage without reversibility by lake readers.
* **Generalisation and suppression** rules: dates of birth to age band, dates of service to week or month depending on dataset, pin codes truncated to district, rare values binned.
* **k-anonymity enforcement** at query time in the semantic layer: result cells below a configured minimum group size are suppressed rather than returned.
* **Free-text handling**: clinical notes and other unstructured fields are excluded from `serving/` by default; where a dataset requires them, a Vertex AI entity-redaction step runs and the output is quarantined for review before promotion.
* A **re-identification workflow** — break-glass, two-person, time-boxed, fully audited, used only for legally compelled disclosure or safety investigation.
* **Direct-identifier deny list** enforced structurally: raw ABHA numbers, Aadhaar-derived tokens, phone numbers, email addresses, full names and full addresses can never be written to `serving/`, verified by an automated scan on every promotion.

**Out of scope**

* The lake, CDC pipeline, Iceberg tables and Temporal orchestration themselves — owned by #481.
* Data classification registry and retention policy — owned by #480; this issue consumes classifications.
* Consent capture and the consent-artefact lifecycle — owned by the ABDM Consent Manager epic.
* AdminConnect dashboards and reports — owned by the AdminConnect Analytics epic; they query the serving layer this issue produces.
* Differential privacy for externally published aggregate statistics — a later issue if and when the platform publishes data outside the tenant.

---

## Recommended Solution

Implement a `deident` stage as a mandatory Temporal activity in the #481 conformed → serving DAG. Promotion to `serving/` is only possible through this activity; the serving prefix's IAM policy grants write to the transform's service identity alone, so an engineer cannot hand-place an untransformed dataset.

**Pseudonymisation.** Research IDs are `HMAC-SHA256(kms_key[country, purpose], mdm_id)` truncated to 128 bits and stored as `research_patient_id`. The key never leaves KMS — the transform calls KMS MAC operations rather than fetching key material. Two properties follow: the same patient yields the same ID across all encounters within a purpose, enabling readmission and longitudinal cohort analysis; and different purposes yield unlinkable IDs, so a product-analytics dataset cannot be joined against a clinical-quality dataset to narrow identity. Because the key is in KMS, revoking analytical access is a key-disable operation, and destroying the key crypto-shreds linkability entirely — which is what makes DPDP erasure tractable in the lake without rewriting Parquet history.

```sql
-- serving.mart_encounter  (Iceberg, k-anonymity enforced at query)
tenant_id            uuid  NOT NULL
research_patient_id  bytea NOT NULL      -- HMAC, per-country per-purpose
age_band             text  NOT NULL      -- '0-1','1-5','5-18','18-30',… ,'90+'
sex                  text
district_code        text                -- pin code truncated, never full pin
facility_hfr_id      text  NOT NULL
department           text  NOT NULL
admitted_week        date  NOT NULL      -- generalised from timestamptz
length_of_stay_days  int
primary_icd_block    text                -- ICD chapter/block, not full rubric for rare codes
discharge_disposition text
-- NO name, phone, email, address, abha_number, aadhaar_token, free-text columns
```

```sql
CREATE TABLE deident_rule (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY, tenant_id uuid NOT NULL, country_profile text NOT NULL,
  dataset text NOT NULL, column_name text NOT NULL, classification text NOT NULL,
  strategy text NOT NULL CHECK (strategy IN
    ('pseudonymise','generalise','suppress','bin','redact_text','pass_through')),
  params jsonb NOT NULL, version int NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE (tenant_id, country_profile, dataset, column_name, version)
);

CREATE TABLE reidentification_request (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY, tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
  research_patient_id bytea NOT NULL, legal_basis text NOT NULL,
  requested_by uuid NOT NULL, approved_by uuid, approved_at timestamptz,
  expires_at timestamptz NOT NULL, resolved_mdm_id uuid, digest bytea,
  CHECK (approved_by IS NULL OR approved_by <> requested_by)   -- two-person rule
);
```

The `CHECK` constraint enforces two-person approval in the database rather than only in application code, so no service path can bypass it.

**Deny-list enforcement.** A promotion gate scans the candidate serving dataset's schema against the classification registry and a structural pattern scan of sample values (Aadhaar-shaped 12-digit runs, 10-digit Indian mobile patterns, `@` sequences, 14-digit ABHA patterns). Any hit fails the promotion and the dataset stays in `conformed/`. This catches the realistic failure — an identifier leaking into a column nobody classified, such as a phone number typed into a free-text remarks field.

**k-anonymity at query.** The semantic layer rewrites aggregate queries to compute group counts, and suppresses any output cell whose contributing distinct `research_patient_id` count is below `k` (default 5, configurable per tenant, never below 3). Suppression returns an explicit `suppressed` marker so dashboards show "below reporting threshold" rather than a misleading zero. This closes the small-cell re-identification path — a single rare-diagnosis patient in a small department is otherwise identifiable from an aggregate alone.

**API surface**

```
GET  /v1/deident/rules?dataset=&country_profile=
PUT  /v1/deident/rules/{id}
POST /v1/deident/datasets/{dataset}:promote        # runs gate + transform
GET  /v1/deident/promotions/{id}                   # gate findings
POST /v1/deident/reidentification-requests
POST /v1/deident/reidentification-requests/{id}:approve
GET  /v1/deident/reidentification-requests/{id}
```

**Events.** Consumes `AnalyticsDatasetRefreshed` from #481 to trigger promotion. Publishes `DatasetDeidentified` (dataset, rule version, k, row count), `DeidentificationGateFailed` (dataset, finding type — never the offending value), and `ReidentificationPerformed` (request ID, approver, basis) for the compliance audit trail.

**OpenFGA.**

```
type serving_dataset
  relations
    define tenant: [tenant]
    define viewer: analyst from tenant or hospital_admin from tenant

type reidentification_request
  relations
    define tenant: [tenant]
    define requester: clinical_governance_lead from tenant or dpo from tenant
    define approver: dpo from tenant
    # approver must differ from requester; enforced by DB CHECK and OpenFGA contextual tuple
```

Re-identification is deliberately not grantable to `analyst` or `platform_admin`.

**Sequencing.** Depends on #480 (classification registry), #481 (lake and conformed layer) and the MDM patient master. Blocks every AdminConnect analytics dashboard issue.

**Risks.** The principal risk is re-identification by linkage — combining age band, district, rare diagnosis and admission week can single out an individual even with no direct identifier. Mitigations are the k-anonymity query gate, ICD generalisation to block level for low-prevalence codes, week-level rather than date-level service dates, and per-purpose salts preventing cross-dataset joins. A second risk is analytical utility loss making the warehouse unused; mitigated by validating each mart against the actual reporting questions from AdminConnect before promotion, and by tuning generalisation per dataset rather than applying one global aggressiveness.

---

## Acceptance Criteria

### Primary Scenario

**Given** a conformed `fact_encounter` dataset for an Indian tenant containing patient names, phone numbers, full dates of birth and ABHA numbers
**When** the promotion to `serving/mart_encounter` runs
**Then** the resulting dataset contains a stable `research_patient_id` that is identical across that patient's separate encounters, ages expressed as bands, service dates generalised to week, districts in place of pin codes, no name, phone, ABHA or free-text column present, `DatasetDeidentified` is published with the rule version and effective k, and a readmission-rate query over the mart returns the same value as the equivalent query against OLTP.

### Failure or Validation Scenario

**Given** a new `remarks` column has been added upstream containing free text into which staff have typed patient mobile numbers, and the column is classified `operational` in error
**When** promotion to the serving layer is attempted
**Then** the pattern scan detects Indian mobile-number-shaped values, the promotion fails, the dataset remains in `conformed/` and is not readable by any analyst, `DeidentificationGateFailed` is published carrying the finding type and column but never a sample value, the DPO is alerted, and the previous good serving snapshot continues to serve unchanged.

### Edge Cases

* A department with two patients in a rare ICD block — the aggregate cell is suppressed under k-anonymity rather than returned, and the dashboard renders "below reporting threshold".
* A patient exercises DPDP erasure — the per-purpose KMS key path allows their linkage to be destroyed without rewriting historical Parquet files; aggregate counts already published remain valid.
* The same patient appears under two MDM records later merged by de-duplication — a re-promotion regenerates a single `research_patient_id` and the mart is rebuilt; the merge does not silently double-count in the interim.
* An analyst attempts to join `mart_encounter` against a product-analytics mart on `research_patient_id` — the per-purpose salts mean the IDs do not match and the join yields zero rows by construction, not by policy.
* KMS is unavailable during promotion — the transform fails closed, nothing is written to `serving/`, and Temporal retries; no fallback to unsalted hashing exists in code.
* A re-identification request is submitted and approved by the same user — the database `CHECK` rejects it and the attempt is audited as a policy violation.

---

## Engineering Guardrails

Complete the applicable items before the story is closed.

### Code Quality

* [ ] The change is limited to the agreed scope.
* [ ] Existing behaviour remains backward-compatible unless explicitly approved.
* [ ] Code follows the team’s agreed standards and architecture.
* [ ] No temporary code, debug output or unnecessary complexity remains.
* [ ] Error handling is explicit and does not silently ignore failures.

### Test-Driven Development

* [ ] Acceptance criteria were converted into test scenarios.
* [ ] New or changed business logic was developed using Red–Green–Refactor where practical.
* [ ] Bug fixes include a regression test that fails before the fix and passes afterwards.
* [ ] Tests validate behaviour rather than private implementation details.

### Automated Testing

* [ ] Unit tests cover new and changed logic.
* [ ] Positive, negative and important boundary scenarios are covered.
* [ ] Integration or contract tests are updated where service boundaries change.
* [ ] Critical user journeys are covered by Playwright or an equivalent E2E framework.
* [ ] Existing tests pass.
* [ ] No new flaky or skipped tests are introduced without justification.

### Security and Access

* [ ] Authentication and authorisation are enforced at the appropriate layer.
* [ ] Users and services can access only the data and actions they require.
* [ ] Input is validated and sensitive information is not exposed in logs or errors.
* [ ] Secrets and credentials are not stored in source code.
* [ ] Security and dependency scans pass.
* [ ] Tenant, account or customer isolation is tested where applicable.

### Accessibility and User Journey

* [ ] The primary user journey works from start to completion.
* [ ] Loading, empty, success and error states are handled.
* [ ] Keyboard navigation and focus behaviour work correctly.
* [ ] Controls have clear labels and accessible names.
* [ ] The change meets the team’s agreed WCAG accessibility level.
* [ ] The experience works across supported devices and browsers.

### Performance and Reliability

* [ ] The change does not introduce unnecessary API calls, database queries or processing.
* [ ] Timeouts, retries and failure behaviour are defined where applicable.
* [ ] Duplicate requests do not create inconsistent data.
* [ ] Performance-sensitive changes are tested against an agreed threshold.
* [ ] Partial failures do not leave the system in an invalid state.

### Observability

* [ ] Important failures are logged with useful diagnostic context.
* [ ] Logs do not contain sensitive information.
* [ ] Metrics or traces are added where the change affects a critical workflow.
* [ ] The team can determine whether the feature is working correctly after deployment.

### Documentation

* [ ] Relevant README, API or technical documentation is updated.
* [ ] Configuration or environment changes are documented.
* [ ] Deployment, migration or rollback steps are documented where required.
* [ ] Known limitations are recorded.

---

## Result

* **Expected user or system outcome:** The analytical serving layer contains no direct identifiers and no free text, supports longitudinal cohort analysis through stable per-purpose pseudonyms, and suppresses small cells automatically.
* **Expected business or operational outcome:** The DPO can state and evidence that analytics processes de-identified data only; AdminConnect dashboards, accreditation reporting and product analytics proceed without a DPDP blocker; enterprise and government security reviews on secondary use can be satisfied.
* **Success metric or validation method:** Zero direct identifiers detected in the serving layer by a scheduled independent scan over 90 days; 100% of serving datasets produced through the enforced transform (no out-of-band writes, verified from bucket audit logs); k-anonymity holds at k≥5 for 100% of returned aggregate cells; a re-identification linkage attack exercise by the security team against the serving layer achieves a match rate below 1% on a known-identity holdout set; analytical utility validated by ≤2% deviation between mart-computed and OLTP-computed readmission rate and lab turnaround time.
* **Monitoring period:** 90 days, with a monthly linkage-attack exercise and monthly review of every re-identification request raised.

---

## Pull Request Evidence

The pull request should include:

* [ ] Link to this story.
* [ ] Summary of the change.
* [ ] Test evidence.
* [ ] Screenshots or recordings for UI changes.
* [ ] Security, accessibility or performance evidence where relevant.
* [ ] Deployment and rollback notes for higher-risk changes.
* [ ] Known risks or follow-up work.

---

## Definition of Done

The story is complete when:

* [ ] All acceptance criteria pass.
* [ ] Required tests pass locally and in CI.
* [ ] No critical or high-severity security or quality issues remain.
* [ ] The critical user or system journey has been validated.
* [ ] Documentation is updated.
* [ ] Code review is complete.
* [ ] The change has been deployed or is ready for deployment through the standard pipeline.
* [ ] Post-deployment validation is defined or completed.
* [ ] Any exception is documented with an owner and reason.

---

## Exceptions

**Guardrail:** Accessibility and User Journey — keyboard navigation, focus behaviour, WCAG level, cross-device support.
**Reason:** The deliverable is a transform stage, a promotion gate and an API. The one human-facing flow, the re-identification approval screen, is delivered in the AdminConnect Compliance console issue where the accessibility guardrail applies in full.
**Alternative validation:** The suppression contract is validated at the API level — suppressed cells return an explicit typed marker with a human-readable reason string, so consuming dashboards cannot render a suppressed cell as zero.
**Residual risk:** Low, contingent on the console issue landing in the same release train as the first dashboards.
**Approved by:** Data & AI team lead, reviewed by the DPO.

items.body:
> Retour de test du PO du 16/09/2026 — demande tracée dans #804.

## Contexte

Le produit est un SaaS vendu à des salons, des spas et des barbershops. Pour
vendre, l'éditeur doit pouvoir **ouvrir un établissement** pour chaque nouveau
client, puis remettre au gérant son accès et le lien de réservation que ses
clientes utiliseront. Le PO l'a formulé ainsi : « on devrait même avoir une
interface pour générer un lien unique pour le manager qu'il utilisera pour ses
clients ».

Le CDC §2.3 range les tenants dans le module Identité & accès, et le §2.4 fait du
Tenant l'entité racine du modèle.

## Constat

- **Aucun code ne crée d'établissement.** Une recherche de `tenant.create` ou de
  `createTenant` dans `apps/api/src` ne rend rien. Les 117 établissements de
  `spa_dev` viennent du seed (`apps/api/prisma/seed.ts`) et des jeux d'essai de
  recette.
- `POST /v1/users` (ADMIN) invite un compte **dans un établissement qui existe
  déjà** (`users.controller.ts:220-241`). Rien ne crée le premier administrateur
  d'un établissement neuf.
- La racine `/` du produit ne propose rien à un gérant ni à l'éditeur (capture).

## Critères d'acceptation

1. **Arbitrage du PO (16/09) : les salons s'ouvrent depuis une console
   plateforme réservée à l'éditeur, sans inscription en libre-service.** Un
   ADR tranche le modèle d'**opérateur plateforme** :
   - une identité hors établissement, dans une table dédiée sans `tenant_id` ;
   - une authentification distincte de celle des établissements, avec MFA exigée.

   L'ADR explique aussi pourquoi cette table ne contredit pas la règle « toute
   table métier porte `tenant_id` ».
2. `POST /v1/platform/tenants` est réservé à l'opérateur plateforme. En une seule
   transaction, il crée :
   - l'établissement : nom, slug, fuseau IANA, devise ISO 4217, pays ;
   - son compte ADMIN, sans mot de passe.

   La réponse rend trois liens :
   - le lien de réservation absolu, sur le sous-domaine du salon :
     `https://{slug}.{domaine}/reservation`, construit par `tenantPublicUrl`
     (#837) ;
   - le lien d'invitation de l'administrateur ;
   - l'URL de connexion du back-office,
     `https://{slug}.{domaine}/admin/connexion`.
3. Le slug est un label DNS valide, et son unicité est garantie par la
   base (409 `TENANT_SLUG_TAKEN`). Les slugs réservés sont refusés, avec la
   liste partagée de #837.
4. `GET /v1/platform/tenants` liste les établissements, avec pagination.
   `POST /v1/platform/tenants/:id/invitation` réémet l'invitation de
   l'administrateur.
5. Les deux espaces sont étanches dans les deux sens, et un test d'intégration
   couvre chaque sens :
   - un jeton d'établissement, même ADMIN, reçoit 401 sur toute route
     `/v1/platform/*` ;
   - un jeton plateforme reçoit 401 sur toute route d'établissement.
6. La création est journalisée : qui, quand, quel établissement. Elle est
   idempotente sur l'en-tête `Idempotency-Key`.
7. Un opérateur plateforme se crée par une commande
   (`npm run platform:operator -- --email …`), jamais par une route publique.

Dépend de #837

## Points d'attention

- **Isolation.** Les lectures non scopées existantes sont recensées dans
  `identity.repository.ts:275-285`. Celles de la console s'y ajoutent,
  recensées de la même façon et gardées par le lint de scoping (ADR 0006,
  portée des gardes).
- **Périmètre.** Le multi-établissement **côté client** — un gérant qui pilote
  plusieurs salons — reste hors périmètre (CDC §1.4). Ici, c'est l'éditeur qui
  ouvre un établissement par client.
- Le jeton d'invitation ne doit jamais apparaître dans les journaux.

## Références

CDC §1.2, §2.3, §2.4 · `apps/api/src/modules/identity/users.controller.ts` ·
`apps/api/src/common/tenant/public-tenant-request.ts`

## Capture

**La racine du produit n'offre aucun accès à un gérant ni à l'éditeur**

![La racine du produit n'offre aucun accès à un gérant ni à l'éditeur](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TMap-Works/spa-booking/qa-captures/docs/retour-po/captures/retour-po-20260916/po-a1-1.png)

items.title: Rejected Postgres Changes joins retain a counted tenant user
items.body:
A rejected Postgres Changes join can leave its websocket transport counted as a connected tenant user until the websocket closes.

Reproduced on upstream `217744c20389fce5c91636ac8273878f1b4f7c73`; the affected code is unchanged on `5a258870f3c7ce0ceccdfbbe64eda56a096eff61`.

### Reproduction

1. Connect a websocket with a valid tenant JWT, without another successfully joined channel.
2. Join a channel using this config while the CDC connection cannot become ready before the timeout:

```json
{"config":{"postgres_changes":[{"event":"INSERT","schema":"public"}],"postgres_changes_options":{"wait":true,"timeout":100}}}
```

3. Observe the join return `PostgresChangesSubscribeTimeout` and keep the websocket open.
4. Check `Realtime.UsersCounter.already_counted?(transport_pid, tenant_id)`: it returns `true` despite the rejected join.

For a deterministic local regression, the existing channel test harness can stub `Extensions.PostgresCdcRls.handle_connect/1` to return `nil`, connect through `UserSocket`, and call `subscribe_and_join/3` with the config above. Assert the timeout error, assert the transport remains alive, then refute `UsersCounter.already_counted?/2`. The final assertion fails on upstream with `Expected false or nil, got true`.

### Expected / actual

Expected: a transport with no successful channel join is not added to the tenant user census by a rejected join.

Actual: the rejected join adds the transport to the census, and the entry remains while the transport stays alive.

### Root cause and impact

`RealtimeChannel.join/3` calls `UsersCounter.add/2` before `await_muster_join/2` and `start_postgres_subscribe/4` succeed. The subscription wait added in #2109 can reject the join after this registration. The census monitors the transport, so rejecting the channel does not remove that registration.

This consumes tenant concurrent-user capacity without a successful channel and can keep the tenant's idle-connection logic seeing an active user. A slow or unavailable CDC connection is enough to trigger it with `wait: true`.

Moving registration into the successful join branch makes the deterministic regression pass; existing successful-join and counter tests also pass.

items.title: IS-004: Data Ownership / Resource Boundary
items.body:
# IS-004 — Data Ownership / Resource Boundary

## Status
READY

## Architecture
- Class: B — Platform Service / foundational component mechanism
- Level: 0 — Modular Monolith
- Source of Truth: `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` v1.2.0 RATIFIED
- Predecessors: IS-001 Identity / Tenant Context, IS-002 Tenant Authority / Tenant Lifecycle, IS-003 Authorization Boundary / Permission Authority

## Goal
Prove that an authorized request can operate only on a resource owned by the data-owner component and cannot bypass the IS-003 authorization boundary.

## Core invariant
`ALLOW` from IS-003 is not direct data access. The data owner remains the final enforcement boundary.

## Required invariants
1. Every resource has exactly one data owner.
2. Tenant A cannot access Tenant B resources, including by changing `resource_id` or caller-supplied `tenant_id`.
3. A request with IS-003 `DENY` must not reach the owned-data operation.
4. Authorization dependency failure or malformed/non-authoritative dependency response fails closed to `DENY`.
5. The effective tenant comes from IS-001; IS-004 must not create a second tenant-context mechanism.
6. The public component surface must not provide an access path that bypasses the resource-owner enforcement boundary.
7. Security-sensitive refusals are auditable and observable with request/correlation and actor/tenant context where applicable.

## Minimal resource model
A proof resource may contain:
- `resource_id`
- `resource_type`
- `owner_component`
- `tenant_id`
- `state`

Do not turn this slice into a generic ORM/data platform.

## Required acceptance proof
### A. Authorized access
Identity A → effective Tenant A → IS-003 ALLOW → Resource A → success.

### B. Tenant isolation
Identity A / Tenant A requesting a Tenant B resource → DENY.

### C. Authorization enforcement
IS-003 DENY → owned-data operation is not invoked.

### D. Dependency failure
Authorization unavailable/invalid → DENY → owned-data operation is not invoked.

### E. Bypass resistance
No public access path may allow the owned resource to be obtained without the enforcement boundary.

Tests must prove behavior, not merely inspect source strings.

## Component Contract
Declare the machine-readable minimum required by architecture:
`api`, `events`, `data_export_cdc`, `ui`, `configuration_schema`, `data_ownership`, `authn`, `authz`, `compatibility_policy`, `dependencies`.

For this slice:
- `data_ownership` must identify the owner and scope.
- `authz.enforcement_boundary` = resource owner.
- `authz.decision_source` = IS-003.
- default authorization outcome = DENY.
- events/CDC remain `declared_only` unless already-deployed infrastructure is required by architecture.

## Non-goals
Do not implement:
- another Identity or Tenant Context mechanism;
- IAM/OIDC provider/credentials/MFA;
- full RBAC/ABAC or policy DSL;
- OPA/external policy engine;
- API gateway/service mesh;
- event broker/CDC infrastructure;
- centralized universal data-access service;
- distributed database infrastructure;
- Catalog, Composer, Golden Bundles, release trains, or other factory mechanics;
- microservice decomposition;
- broad ORM/data-platform abstractions.

## Architecture Gap protocol
If implementation requires changing `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, contradicts a ratified ADR, introduces a new architectural mechanism, or requires scope outside this Issue: STOP the affected work, record an Architecture Gap in GitHub, and wait for architectural decision. Do not silently expand scope.

## Arena restrictions
Arena may implement, test, document, and open a PR. Arena may not:
- change the active architecture;
- ratify architectural decisions;
- expand scope;
- merge `main`.

## PR report must contain
- CHECKED
- CHANGED
- NOT CHANGED
- VERIFICATION
- RISKS OR GAPS
- SOURCE OF TRUTH
- Issue link

Include test results and explicitly state architecture/ADR impact.

## Completion
Lifecycle is:
`READY → IN PROGRESS → IMPLEMENTED → REVIEW → ACCEPTED → MERGED`.

Implementation is not complete until the PR has passed architectural/technical review, the user explicitly approves it, and it is merged into `main`.

items.title: Data anonymization for research

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
## Situation

The brief separates OLTP from OLAP absolutely: analytics must hold de-identified or aggregated data only, and identifiable PHI must never be exposed in analytics without a lawful basis. The pipeline that makes that true does not exist. Today the only way a tenant could answer a research or population-health question — outcomes by procedure, antibiotic resistance patterns across a lab's isolates, readmission rates by ward — is to query the live clinical database with identifiers intact. That breaks the OLTP/OLAP rule, risks degrading the clinical read path, and creates identifiable PHI copies with no consent basis.

There is real demand behind this. Teaching hospitals and NABH-accredited institutions run clinical audit as a condition of accreditation. Labs pursuing NABL accreditation need proficiency and trend analysis across their own results. Research collaborations and public-health reporting are a commercial differentiator for the platform. But under the DPDP Act 2023 the safe route is to take the data outside the Act's scope where possible — genuinely anonymised data is not personal data — rather than to build ever more elaborate consent chains around identifiable extracts.

The trap is that naive de-identification does not anonymise. Dropping the name and ABHA number from a dataset that still contains a full date of birth, a six-digit PIN code and a rare diagnosis leaves individuals trivially re-identifiable, particularly in a small facility. Affected roles: the clinical audit lead and research co-ordinator (need the data), the pathologist (contributes it), the tenant DPO (must be able to assert the output is anonymous, and be right), and the platform data team who must not be asked to hand-roll extracts.

---

## Task

### User or System Story

**As a** clinical audit lead or research co-ordinator at a tenant hospital
**I want** to request a de-identified dataset built to a declared privacy standard, with a re-identification risk assessment attached
**So that** audit and research can proceed on data that is defensibly outside the scope of personal-data obligations, without any manual query against the clinical database.

### Scope

**In scope**

* A dataset definition registry: named research datasets scoped to a tenant, declaring source FHIR resource types, included fields, and the transformation applied to each field.
* A transformation library with the treatments a clinical dataset actually needs: direct-identifier removal, pseudonymisation via a per-dataset keyed HMAC (so longitudinal linkage survives within a dataset but not across them), date shifting with a consistent per-subject offset, date generalisation to month or year, age banding with a top-coded band for ages above 89, geography truncation to district level, rare-value suppression, and free-text redaction.
* Free-text de-identification for narrative fields (discharge summaries, radiology impressions) using Vertex AI with a named-entity redaction pass, followed by a deterministic dictionary and pattern sweep for identifiers the model may miss, and a mandatory human review sample before release.
* **k-anonymity enforcement** over the declared quasi-identifier set, with a configurable minimum k, plus l-diversity on the sensitive attribute where the dataset is small; a build that cannot reach the threshold fails rather than releasing.
* A re-identification risk report generated per build and attached to the dataset artefact, recording the quasi-identifiers, achieved k, suppressed cell count and residual risk.
* Pipeline execution against the OLAP store only, orchestrated in Temporal, publishing `ResearchDatasetBuilt` and `ResearchDatasetReleased`.
* Delivery through the export controls in issue 64, with DPO approval mandatory for every release regardless of size.

**Out of scope**

* Identifiable data sharing for research under specific consent — that is an ABDM consent-artefact flow owned by the consent-management epic, and this dataset path deliberately does not offer it.
* The OLAP warehouse and CDC ingestion from the clinical database — a separate data-platform story; this issue consumes the warehouse.
* AdminConnect operational dashboards and tenant analytics, which read pre-aggregated marts rather than record-level research extracts.
* Model training on clinical data and any inference product.
* Cross-tenant or cross-country pooled datasets. Residency is a hard boundary and pooling is explicitly deferred.

---

## Recommended Solution

A `research-dataset` domain that never touches the clinical OLTP database. All builds read the OLAP warehouse; the tenant's clinical Postgres is not a source.

**Data model (control tables in Postgres, outputs in the warehouse):**

```sql
dataset_definition(
  id uuid pk, tenant_id uuid not null, name text not null,
  source_resources text[] not null,             -- fhir: Encounter, Condition, Observation
  min_k smallint not null default 5,
  min_l smallint,                               -- l-diversity on sensitive attribute
  quasi_identifiers text[] not null,
  sensitive_attribute text,
  status text not null,                          -- draft | approved | retired
  approved_by uuid, approved_at timestamptz,
  unique (tenant_id, name)
);

dataset_field_rule(
  id uuid pk, definition_id uuid not null references dataset_definition(id),
  source_path text not null,                     -- fhir path
  treatment text not null,                       -- drop|hmac|date_shift|generalise|band|truncate_geo|suppress|redact_text
  params jsonb not null default '{}',
  unique (definition_id, source_path)
);

dataset_build(
  id uuid pk, definition_id uuid not null, tenant_id uuid not null,
  status text not null,                          -- running|risk_failed|built|approved|released|expired
  row_count bigint, achieved_k smallint, suppressed_cells bigint,
  risk_report jsonb, salt_key_id text not null,
  workflow_id text, built_at timestamptz,
  check (status <> 'released' or achieved_k is not null)
);
```

The pseudonymisation salt is per definition, held in the secret store and referenced by `salt_key_id`; it is never written to the control tables and never exported. A subject's pseudonym is `HMAC(salt_dataset, patient_master_id)`, so two different datasets cannot be joined on subject even by a party holding both.

**Temporal** `DatasetBuildWorkflow`: `ResolveDefinition` → `ExtractFromWarehouse` (partitioned, read-only) → `ApplyFieldRules` → `RedactFreeText` (Vertex AI activity with retries and a deterministic sweep afterwards) → `AssessRisk` (compute equivalence classes over the quasi-identifiers; if achieved k < `min_k`, attempt the declared generalisation ladder; if still short, fail into `risk_failed`) → `Materialise` → `AwaitDpoApproval` signal → hand to `export-service` for release. The risk assessment sits *before* materialisation of a downloadable artefact, so a failing build never produces a file that could be released by mistake.

**API surface:**

* `GET|POST|PUT /api/v1/research/definitions`, `POST /api/v1/research/definitions/{id}/approve`
* `POST /api/v1/research/definitions/{id}/builds` — start a build
* `GET /api/v1/research/builds/{id}` — status, achieved k, suppression counts
* `GET /api/v1/research/builds/{id}/risk-report`
* `POST /api/v1/research/builds/{id}/approve-release` — DPO only, requires the risk report to have been viewed
* `GET /api/v1/research/builds/{id}/review-sample` — free-text redaction sample for human review

**Events:** publishes `ResearchDatasetBuilt`, `ResearchDatasetRiskFailed`, `ResearchDatasetReleased`; consumes `ConsentRevoked` so that where a definition is built on a consent basis rather than pure anonymisation, subsequent builds exclude the withdrawn subject.

**OpenFGA:**

```
type dataset_definition
  relations
    define tenant: [tenant]
    define author: research_coordinator from tenant
    define approver: dpo from tenant
    define builder: author or approver
    define releaser: dpo from tenant but not author
```

**Sequencing and risks.** Depends on the OLAP warehouse, the export controls (issue 64), the audit store (issue 67) and the patient master for stable subject keys. Risks: (1) re-identification through rare combinations — mitigated by mandatory k-anonymity with suppression and a hard build failure rather than a warning; (2) free-text redaction missing an identifier — mitigated by the model pass plus a deterministic pattern and dictionary sweep, a mandatory human-reviewed sample, and never treating a narrative field as safe by default (definitions must opt in explicitly); (3) linkage across datasets — mitigated by per-definition salts; (4) an operator lowering `min_k` to force a build through — mitigated by requiring DPO approval to change `min_k` and auditing the change; (5) analytics load on clinical systems — structurally prevented by the warehouse-only source.

---

## Acceptance Criteria

### Primary Scenario

**Given** an approved dataset definition for diabetic outcomes with `min_k = 5`, dates generalised to month, ages banded with 90+ top-coded and geography truncated to district
**When** the research co-ordinator starts a build and the DPO approves release after reviewing the risk report
**Then** the pipeline reads only the OLAP warehouse, produces a dataset in which every equivalence class over the declared quasi-identifiers contains at least 5 records, attaches a risk report stating achieved k and suppressed cell count, emits `ResearchDatasetReleased`, and delivers the artefact through `export-service` with an expiring signed URL and a full audit trail.

### Failure or Validation Scenario

**Given** the same definition applied to a small facility where 3 patients share a rare condition, district and age band
**When** the risk assessment runs
**Then** the build applies the declared generalisation ladder, and if k = 5 still cannot be reached it terminates in `risk_failed`, materialises no downloadable artefact, publishes `ResearchDatasetRiskFailed` with the failing equivalence classes described by size only, and presents the co-ordinator with the option to broaden generalisation — the dataset is never released with k below the threshold.

### Edge Cases

* A definition includes a narrative field without explicitly enabling `redact_text`: the definition fails approval validation.
* Human review of the redaction sample finds a residual identifier: release approval is blocked until a re-build passes with an updated redaction dictionary.
* Two builds of the same definition run concurrently: the second is rejected by an idempotency guard so two different salts cannot produce inconsistent pseudonyms for the same declared dataset.
* A subject withdraws consent after a build but before release, on a consent-basis definition: release is blocked until a rebuild excludes them.
* The Vertex AI redaction activity is unavailable: the workflow retries with backoff and then fails the build; it never falls through to publishing unredacted narrative text.
* A definition authored in tenant A references warehouse partitions from tenant B: the extract activity resolves partitions from the definition's tenant only, and a cross-tenant reference fails the build — covered by an adversarial test.
* The releaser and the author are the same person: release is refused by the OpenFGA `but not author` relation.

---

## Engineering Guardrails

Complete the applicable items before the story is closed.

### Code Quality

* [ ] The change is limited to the agreed scope.
* [ ] Existing behaviour remains backward-compatible unless explicitly approved.
* [ ] Code follows the team’s agreed standards and architecture.
* [ ] No temporary code, debug output or unnecessary complexity remains.
* [ ] Error handling is explicit and does not silently ignore failures.

### Test-Driven Development

* [ ] Acceptance criteria were converted into test scenarios.
* [ ] New or changed business logic was developed using Red–Green–Refactor where practical.
* [ ] Bug fixes include a regression test that fails before the fix and passes afterwards.
* [ ] Tests validate behaviour rather than private implementation details.

### Automated Testing

* [ ] Unit tests cover new and changed logic.
* [ ] Positive, negative and important boundary scenarios are covered.
* [ ] Integration or contract tests are updated where service boundaries change.
* [ ] Critical user journeys are covered by Playwright or an equivalent E2E framework.
* [ ] Existing tests pass.
* [ ] No new flaky or skipped tests are introduced without justification.

### Security and Access

* [ ] Authentication and authorisation are enforced at the appropriate layer.
* [ ] Users and services can access only the data and actions they require.
* [ ] Input is validated and sensitive information is not exposed in logs or errors.
* [ ] Secrets and credentials are not stored in source code.
* [ ] Security and dependency scans pass.
* [ ] Tenant, account or customer isolation is tested where applicable.

### Accessibility and User Journey

* [ ] The primary user journey works from start to completion.
* [ ] Loading, empty, success and error states are handled.
* [ ] Keyboard navigation and focus behaviour work correctly.
* [ ] Controls have clear labels and accessible names.
* [ ] The change meets the team’s agreed WCAG accessibility level.
* [ ] The experience works across supported devices and browsers.

### Performance and Reliability

* [ ] The change does not introduce unnecessary API calls, database queries or processing.
* [ ] Timeouts, retries and failure behaviour are defined where applicable.
* [ ] Duplicate requests do not create inconsistent data.
* [ ] Performance-sensitive changes are tested against an agreed threshold.
* [ ] Partial failures do not leave the system in an invalid state.

### Observability

* [ ] Important failures are logged with useful diagnostic context.
* [ ] Logs do not contain sensitive information.
* [ ] Metrics or traces are added where the change affects a critical workflow.
* [ ] The team can determine whether the feature is working correctly after deployment.

### Documentation

* [ ] Relevant README, API or technical documentation is updated.
* [ ] Configuration or environment changes are documented.
* [ ] Deployment, migration or rollback steps are documented where required.
* [ ] Known limitations are recorded.

---

## Result

* **Expected user or system outcome:** clinical audit and research datasets are produced by a repeatable, risk-assessed pipeline reading only the warehouse, with a documented privacy standard attached to every release.
* **Expected business or operational outcome:** tenants can run accreditation-required clinical audit and research collaborations on the platform instead of exporting raw records, and the DPO can assert the anonymity of released datasets with evidence.
* **Success metric or validation method:** 100% of released datasets meet or exceed the configured k threshold, verified independently by a post-release equivalence-class check that runs against the artefact; zero direct identifiers detected in released datasets by an automated identifier scanner run on every build; ≥98% recall on the free-text redaction benchmark set before the first release is permitted; zero research queries executed against the clinical OLTP database, asserted by connection-level policy.
* **Monitoring period:** 90 days, tracking build success versus `risk_failed` rate, achieved k distribution, suppression rates, and human-review findings on redaction samples.

---

## Pull Request Evidence

The pull request should include:

* [ ] Link to this story.
* [ ] Summary of the change.
* [ ] Test evidence.
* [ ] Screenshots or recordings for UI changes.
* [ ] Security, accessibility or performance evidence where relevant.
* [ ] Deployment and rollback notes for higher-risk changes.
* [ ] Known risks or follow-up work.

---

## Definition of Done

The story is complete when:

* [ ] All acceptance criteria pass.
* [ ] Required tests pass locally and in CI.
* [ ] No critical or high-severity security or quality issues remain.
* [ ] The critical user or system journey has been validated.
* [ ] Documentation is updated.
* [ ] Code review is complete.
* [ ] The change has been deployed or is ready for deployment through the standard pipeline.
* [ ] Post-deployment validation is defined or completed.
* [ ] Any exception is documented with an owner and reason.

---

## Exceptions

None — all guardrails apply. Dataset definition authoring, the risk report and the redaction review sample are AdminConnect console surfaces, so accessibility applies in full; the build pipeline itself is a backend worker covered under performance, reliability and observability.

items.body:
# Gate G3 — preparação do piloto controlado HelpUS Zap Pro

**Origem:** Gate G2 do sandbox local, Ordem 008, 31/10/2026. **Status:** BACKLOG / NÃO AUTORIZADO PARA EXECUÇÃO REAL.

## Fronteira de autorização
A aprovação do G2 cobre **somente testes sintéticos locais em 127.0.0.1**, com mocks de pagamento, fixture de WhatsApp e CI dos módulos. Não inclui autorização de merge/deploy produtivo, conectar números de WhatsApp reais, utilizar PIX real, habilitar clientes, emitir cobranças, nem ativar automaticamente a fase 2.

## Itens bloqueadores para eventual G3 / piloto
1. **Integração de serviços de verdade (arquitetural, mas ainda com mocks):** `helpus-pay PR #2` contém helper standalone de cobrança, enquanto `helpus-whatsapp-ia PR #1` possui seu próprio PaymentMockService. O E2E HTTP G2 exercita o mock embutido no WhatsApp, **não uma chamada HTTP real ao repositório helpus-pay**. Planejar integração contratual explícita versionada, autenticada e com testes cross-service antes de G3.
2. **Identidade e tenant:** integrar com `helpus-auth`; derivar tenant no backend; não confiar em IDs, preço e ordem do cliente. Validar vínculos charge/order/tenant em ambos os serviços, inclusive ordem inexistente, já quitada ou divergente.
3. **Persistência e concorrência:** `Map`/`Set` de sessões, mensagens e cobranças não sobrevivem reinício; introduzir persistência transacional, deduplicação durável, controle concorrente e proteção contra eventos fora de ordem. Testar crash, retry, cancelamento simultâneo e webhook atrasado.
4. **Segredos e segregação de ambientes:** eliminar segredos HMAC hardcoded dos módulos executáveis (mesmo como fallback em futuros serviços hospedados); obter do ambiente/secret manager, rotacionar, verificar se nenhum token real foi exposto. Bloquear mocks em preview/staging/prod e impedir rotas de teste expostas. Mesmo código de sandbox com segredos conhecidos NÃO oferece autenticidade real.
5. **Superfície HTTP e compliance:** o servidor G2 fica em loopback; endurecer limite do body bruto, timeout, schemas, IP/rate limit, logs redigidos, privacy/consent, segurança e políticas da Meta, incluindo API oficial/números autorizados. O servidor `server.js` legado não foi integrado ao novo adapter e tem caminho de produção separado.
6. **Revisão técnica e governança:** alinhar branch padrão do repositório privado `HelpUSA/helpus-whatsapp-ia` à `main` e proteger branches; manter PRs Draft até plano de integração, auditoria e autorização de merge; separar QA independente da autoria. Adicionar cenários HTTP negativos com assinatura *válida* mas tenant/txid/valor/estado inválidos, restart, concorrência e falha de rede.
7. **Voz, pagamentos reais e autorização comercial:** resolver licenças e segurança do TTS, selecionar PSP e validar cobrança server-to-server, modelo de consentimento e retenção, estimativa de custos e critérios stop/go. Nada disso está incluído no G2.

## Evidências G2 disponíveis
- [Pay PR #2](https://github.com/HelpUSA/helpus-pay/pull/2), SHA `5dde90293660c438b9e4f7524fd2c1064b1faa3d`; GitHub Actions [PR run 41215370886](https://github.com/HelpUSA/helpus-pay/actions/runs/41215370886) **SUCCESS**, typecheck + 4/4 testes.
- [WhatsApp IA PR #1 (privado)](https://github.com/HelpUSA/helpus-whatsapp-ia/pull/1), SHA `9f9c8bae3570807e831ca97ec0c17d7c6121f240`; GitHub Actions [PR run 41215804189](https://github.com/HelpUSA/helpus-whatsapp-ia/actions/runs/41215804189) **SUCCESS**, 15/15 testes unitários e 4/4 HTTP E2E locais.
- [Gate G2 / HUB #8](https://github.com/HelpUSA/hub/issues/8) — revisão independente e aprovação estritamente limitada à demonstração local.

## Próximo marco
Aguardar autorização específica do Master SuperAdmin para qualquer execução de G3. Antes dela, somente planejamento, documentação e QA preparatório; nenhuma conta real, dados reais ou cobrança real.

items.title: IS-002: Реализовать Tenant Authority / Tenant Lifecycle
items.body:
# IS-002 — Tenant Authority / Tenant Lifecycle

## Статус
`READY`

## Архитектурная цель
Доказать, что Platform Instance имеет единственный авторитетный механизм управления Tenant и его lifecycle, а Identity / Tenant Context корректно подчиняется этому состоянию.

Архитектурная основа: `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` v1.2.0, в частности модель Tenant, Tenant Authority, lifecycle и data scope classification. Не изменять архитектуру в рамках этой задачи.

## Уровень
- Class B — Platform Service
- Level 0 — Modular Monolith
- First implementation foundation after IS-001

## Контекст
IS-001 доказал verified identity, tenant context, authorization boundary, tenant isolation, audit/observability и API idempotency. IS-002 должен доказать следующий фундаментальный инвариант: Tenant Authority является единственным источником истины для Tenant registry/lifecycle и корректно ограничивает операции в зависимости от состояния Tenant.

Цепочка:

```text
Verified Identity
      ↓
Identity / Tenant Context
      ↓
Tenant Authority
      ├─ tenant exists?
      ├─ belongs to Platform Instance?
      ├─ lifecycle state?
      └─ operation permitted?
      ↓
Authorization Boundary
      ↓
Tenant-owned Resource
```

## Scope

### 1. Tenant Registry
Минимальная модель Tenant:
- `tenant_id`
- `platform_id`
- `state`
- `created_at`
- `updated_at`

Инварианты:
- `tenant_id` immutable;
- Tenant принадлежит ровно одной Platform Instance;
- Tenant не может иметь более одного текущего state;
- `deleted` — terminal state.

### 2. Tenant lifecycle
Поддержать lifecycle из архитектуры:
`provisioning → active → suspended → deletion_requested → deleted`

Разрешённые переходы минимум:
- `provisioning → active`
- `active → suspended`
- `suspended → active`
- `active → deletion_requested`
- `suspended → deletion_requested`
- `deletion_requested → deleted`

Недопустимые переходы должны быть отклонены, включая любые переходы из `deleted`.

Не придумывать дополнительную operational policy для состояний, если она не требуется для доказательства инвариантов.

### 3. Platform ownership
Проверять:
`tenant.platform_id == current_platform_id`.

Нельзя получить Tenant одной Platform Instance из контекста другой.

### 4. Integration with IS-001
Не создавать второй механизм определения effective tenant.

IS-001 остаётся источником `effective_tenant_id`; Tenant Authority предоставляет authoritative lookup состояния и принадлежности Tenant.

### 5. Lifecycle enforcement
Обычные tenant-scoped операции должны быть запрещены для состояний, в которых Tenant не должен обслуживаться, прежде всего `suspended`, `deletion_requested`, `deleted`.

Точные operational details для `provisioning` не расширять без необходимости.

### 6. Audit
Каждый lifecycle transition должен быть аудируемым минимум с:
- `tenant_id`
- `previous_state`
- `new_state`
- `actor/service_id`
- `timestamp`
- `request_id`
- `correlation_id`

Security-sensitive denials также должны быть наблюдаемы/аудируемы в соответствии с IS-001.

### 7. Observability
Использовать установленный архитектурой observability context, включая tenant/request/correlation context там, где применимо.

### 8. Component Contract
Tenant Authority должен иметь machine-readable Component Contract с минимумом:
`api`, `events`, `data_export_cdc`, `ui`, `configuration_schema`, `data_ownership`, `authn`, `authz`, `compatibility_policy`, `dependencies`.

Data ownership Tenant Registry: `platform-scoped`.

Не объявлять несуществующие events/CDC/infrastructure.

## Invariants

- T-001: один `tenant_id` идентифицирует ровно один Tenant.
- T-002: `tenant_id` immutable.
- T-003: Tenant принадлежит ровно одной Platform Instance.
- T-004: Tenant Authority — authoritative source of Tenant state.
- T-005: lifecycle transitions ограничены state machine.
- T-006: `deleted` не может быть resurrected.
- T-007: caller не может изменить effective tenant простым изменением `tenant_id`.
- T-008: запрещённые lifecycle states блокируют обычные tenant-scoped операции.
- T-009: другие компоненты не получают прямого доступа к внутреннему storage Tenant Authority.
- T-010: lifecycle transitions auditируются.
- T-011: операции поддерживают установленный observability context.

## Security acceptance scenario

1. Создать Platform Instance P.
2. Создать Tenant A и Tenant B.
3. Активировать Tenant A.
4. Verified Identity A получает Tenant Context A.
5. Операция с tenant=A → `ALLOW`.
6. Та же Identity A с `tenant_id=B` → `DENY`.
7. Tenant A: `active → suspended`.
8. Обычная tenant-scoped write для A → `DENY`.
9. Tenant A: `suspended → active`.
10. Операция снова → `ALLOW`.
11. Tenant A: `active → deletion_requested`.
12. Обычная tenant-scoped операция → `DENY`.
13. Tenant A: `deletion_requested → deleted`.
14. Любая обычная операция Tenant A → `DENY`.
15. `deleted → active` → `DENY`.
16. Для transitions существуют audit records.
17. Security-sensitive denials observable/auditable.

## Failure cases
Обязательно проверить:
- tenant не существует;
- Tenant принадлежит другой Platform Instance;
- запрещённый lifecycle transition;
- попытка resurrection `deleted`;
- операция над `suspended`;
- операция над `deletion_requested`;
- операция над `deleted`;
- tenant spoofing;
- отсутствие verified identity;
- отсутствие authorization;
- прямой доступ другого компонента к внутренним данным Tenant Authority.

## Non-goals
Не входит:
- Component Catalog;
- Component Registry;
- Composer;
- Golden Bundles;
- factory release trains;
- billing/subscriptions;
- users management;
- organizations;
- полноценный IAM;
- сложный RBAC/ABAC framework;
- tenant UI;
- provisioning infrastructure;
- Kubernetes;
- distributed databases;
- production orchestration;
- cross-tenant analytics;
- физическое удаление всех данных всех компонентов.

`deleted` в этой задаче — lifecycle state Tenant Authority, а не реализация полного data deletion engine.

## Tests
Требуются behavioral tests:
- positive lifecycle transitions;
- negative/invalid transitions;
- platform ownership;
- tenant spoofing;
- lifecycle enforcement;
- deleted terminality;
- authorization;
- audit;
- observability;
- Component Contract conformance.

Не использовать source-string tests вместо поведенческих проверок.

## Architecture Gap protocol
Если реализация требует изменения `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` или выявляет противоречие с ним:
1. остановить затронутую работу;
2. зафиксировать Architecture Gap в GitHub;
3. предложить варианты/ADR при необходимости;
4. не менять архитектурный закон самостоятельно;
5. продолжить только после архитектурного решения.

## DoD
- [ ] Tenant Registry реализован.
- [ ] Tenant lifecycle реализован как ограниченная state machine.
- [ ] Platform ownership проверяется.
- [ ] Tenant Authority — единственный source of truth для Tenant state.
- [ ] Интеграция с IS-001 не создаёт второй tenant-context mechanism.
- [ ] Lifecycle enforcement реализован.
- [ ] Audit реализован.
- [ ] Observability реализован.
- [ ] Machine-readable Component Contract опубликован.
- [ ] Data ownership объявлен как `platform-scoped`.
- [ ] Positive/negative/security behavioral tests проходят.
- [ ] Архитектура не изменена.
- [ ] PR содержит обязательный отчёт: CHECKED / CHANGED / NOT CHANGED / VERIFICATION / RISKS OR GAPS / SOURCE OF TRUTH / Issue link.

## Arena execution rules
Arena может реализовать, тестировать и открыть PR.
Arena не может:
- менять `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` самостоятельно;
- расширять scope без решения;
- создавать factory mechanics раньше соответствующего gate;
- merge PR без явного разрешения владельца проекта.

## Acceptance
Работа считается завершённой только после:
`IMPLEMENTED → REVIEW → ACCEPTED → MERGED`.

Merge выполняется только после отдельного явного разрешения владельца проекта.

## Source of Truth
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` v1.2.0 — технический закон;
- `docs/adr/ADR-0010-architecture-gap-review.md` — архитектурная история и решения;
- IS-001 implementation / Issue #8 — существующий Identity / Tenant Context foundation;
- данный Issue — self-contained implementation specification.

items.title: [Task 2 - Story 5] Proctus: Optimization Job Orchestration & Baseline Execution
items.body:
# Story 5: Optimization Job Orchestration & Baseline Execution

## Overview
Implement the optimization job lifecycle that executes baseline workload runs against the original stored procedure, capturing results, CDC deltas, and telemetry for comparison with variants.

## Goals
- Create optimization job management API
- Implement baseline run execution with CDC and telemetry capture
- Store run results, CDC deltas, and trace data as artifacts
- Support concurrent workload entry execution
- Implement progress tracking and status reporting
- Handle error cases and partial failures gracefully

## Technical Requirements

### Optimization Job Entity

#### Metadata Store Schema

**New table: `optimization_jobs`**
```sql
CREATE TABLE optimization_jobs (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    tenant_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(id),
    session_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES sessions(id),
    procedure_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES stored_procedures(id),
    workload_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES workloads(id),
    status VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, -- QUEUED, RUNNING, COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELED
    progress DECIMAL(3,2) DEFAULT 0.00,
    current_phase VARCHAR(64),
    variant_count INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
    job_config JSONB,
    created_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    started_at TIMESTAMP,
    finished_at TIMESTAMP,
    CONSTRAINT optimization_jobs_tenant_fk FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id) REFERENCES tenants(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    CONSTRAINT optimization_jobs_session_fk FOREIGN KEY (session_id) REFERENCES sessions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    CONSTRAINT optimization_jobs_proc_fk FOREIGN KEY (procedure_id) REFERENCES stored_procedures(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    CONSTRAINT optimization_jobs_workload_fk FOREIGN KEY (workload_id) REFERENCES workloads(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);
CREATE INDEX idx_optimization_jobs_tenant ON optimization_jobs(tenant_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_optimization_jobs_session ON optimization_jobs(session_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_optimization_jobs_status ON optimization_jobs(status);
```

**New table: `variants`**
```sql
CREATE TABLE variants (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    job_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES optimization_jobs(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    variant_index INT NOT NULL, -- 0 is baseline, 1+ are generated variants
    is_baseline BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    ddl_script_ref TEXT, -- Storage URI for variant DDL
    model VARCHAR(64), -- LLM model used for generation
    prompt_version VARCHAR(32),
    status VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, -- PENDING, GENERATED, RUNNING, COMPLETED, FAILED
    created_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    metadata JSONB,
    CONSTRAINT variants_job_index UNIQUE (job_id, variant_index)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_variants_job ON variants(job_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_variants_status ON variants(status);
```

**New table: `runs`**
```sql
CREATE TABLE runs (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    job_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES optimization_jobs(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    variant_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES variants(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    workload_entry_index INT NOT NULL,
    status VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, -- PENDING, RUNNING, COMPLETED, FAILED
    started_at TIMESTAMP,
    finished_at TIMESTAMP,
    timing_ms BIGINT, -- Total execution time
    result_ref TEXT, -- Storage URI for procedure results
    cdc_ref TEXT, -- Storage URI for CDC delta
    trace_ref TEXT, -- Storage URI for telemetry/trace
    error_ref TEXT, -- Storage URI for error details
    metadata JSONB, -- CPU, reads, writes, etc.
    CONSTRAINT runs_variant_entry UNIQUE (variant_id, workload_entry_index)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_runs_job ON runs(job_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_runs_variant ON runs(variant_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_runs_status ON runs(status);
```

### API Endpoints

#### POST /v1/optimization-jobs
Start an optimization job for a stored procedure

**Request**:
```json
{
  "session_id": "660e8400-e29b-41d4-a716-446655440001",
  "procedure_id": "proc-001",
  "workload_id": "770e8400-e29b-41d4-a716-446655440002",
  "variant_count": 3,
  "config": {
    "parallel_executions": 5,
    "timeout_seconds": 300,
    "enable_trace": true,
    "trace_options": {
      "collect_query_plans": true,
      "collect_wait_stats": true
    }
  }
}
```

**Response** (202 Accepted):
```json
{
  "job_id": "880e8400-e29b-41d4-a716-446655440003",
  "status": "QUEUED",
  "progress": 0.0,
  "estimated_duration_seconds": 600,
  "links": {
    "self": "/v1/optimization-jobs/880e8400-e29b-41d4-a716-446655440003",
    "variants": "/v1/optimization-jobs/880e8400-e29b-41d4-a716-446655440003/variants",
    "runs": "/v1/optimization-jobs/880e8400-e29b-41d4-a716-446655440003/runs"
  }
}
```

#### GET /v1/optimization-jobs/{jobId}
Get job status and progress

#### GET /v1/optimization-jobs/{jobId}/variants
List variants (baseline + candidates)

#### GET /v1/optimization-jobs/{jobId}/runs
List all runs (baseline and variants)

#### POST /v1/optimization-jobs/{jobId}/cancel
Cancel a running job

### Optimization Job Execution Workflow

#### Phase 1: Baseline Execution
```
For each workload entry:
  1. Restore snapshot to baseline state
  2. Enable CDC on all relevant tables
  3. Get starting LSN marker
  4. Enable SQL trace/Extended Events
  5. Execute stored procedure with workload parameters
  6. Capture execution results/errors
  7. Capture telemetry (duration, CPU, I/O, query plan)
  8. Disable trace
  9. Get ending LSN marker
  10. Capture CDC changes (delta between start and end LSN)
  11. Disable CDC
  12. Store all artifacts (results, CDC delta, trace, telemetry)
  13. Create run record with status COMPLETED
```

#### Parallel Execution
- Execute multiple workload entries concurrently (configurable limit)
- Each execution gets independent database snapshot restore
- Use worker pool pattern to manage concurrency
- Track progress and update job metadata

#### Error Handling
- **Recoverable errors** (e.g., expected procedure errors):
  - Mark run as COMPLETED
  - Store error details as part of results
  - Continue with next workload entry
- **Unrecoverable errors** (e.g., SQL Server crash, CDC failure):
  - Mark run as FAILED
  - Log error details
  - Retry with exponential backoff (up to max attempts)
  - If max attempts exceeded, mark entire job as FAILED

### SQL Server Telemetry Collection

#### Extended Events Session Configuration
```sql
CREATE EVENT SESSION [proctus_trace_{run_id}]
ON SERVER
ADD EVENT sqlserver.sql_statement_completed
(
    ACTION (
        sqlserver.session_id,
        sqlserver.database_name,
        sqlserver.sql_text,
        sqlserver.query_plan_hash
    )
    WHERE sqlserver.session_id = @session_id
),
ADD EVENT sqlserver.rpc_completed
(
    ACTION (
        sqlserver.session_id,
        sqlserver.database_name
    )
    WHERE sqlserver.session_id = @session_id
)
ADD TARGET package0.ring_buffer
WITH (MAX_MEMORY = 4096KB);

ALTER EVENT SESSION [proctus_trace_{run_id}] ON SERVER STATE = START;
```

#### Query Execution Statistics
```sql
SET STATISTICS TIME ON;
SET STATISTICS IO ON;

-- Execute procedure
EXEC dbo.GetCustomerOrders @CustomerId = 12345, @StartDate = '2025-01-01', @EndDate = '2025-01-31';

-- Capture results from STATISTICS messages
```

#### Collect Query Plan
```sql
SET SHOWPLAN_XML ON;
-- Execute procedure
-- Capture XML query plan
SET SHOWPLAN_XML OFF;
```

### Artifact Storage Structure

```
s3://proctus-artifacts/
  {tenant_id}/
    jobs/
      {job_id}/
        baseline/
          runs/
            run_{entry_index}/
              result.json           # Procedure output
              cdc_delta.json        # CDC changes
              telemetry.json        # Timing, CPU, I/O, etc.
              trace.xml             # Extended Events trace data
              query_plan.xml        # Query execution plan
              error.json            # Error details (if applicable)
        variants/
          variant_{index}/
            ddl.sql               # Variant procedure definition
            runs/
              run_{entry_index}/
                ... (same structure as baseline)
```

### Run Result Artifacts

#### result.json
```json
{
  "run_id": "run-001",
  "workload_entry_index": 0,
  "parameters": {
    "CustomerId": 12345,
    "StartDate": "2025-01-01",
    "EndDate": "2025-01-31"
  },
  "return_code": 0,
  "result_sets": [
    {
      "columns": ["OrderId", "OrderDate", "Total"],
      "rows": [
        [1001, "2025-01-05", 250.00],
        [1002, "2025-01-12", 175.50]
      ]
    }
  ],
  "messages": [
    {"severity": 0, "text": "2 rows affected"}
  ],
  "success": true
}
```

#### cdc_delta.json
```json
{
  "run_id": "run-001",
  "start_lsn": "0x00000027:00000420:0001",
  "end_lsn": "0x00000027:00000428:0003",
  "tables": {
    "dbo.Orders": [
      {
        "operation": "INSERT",
        "primary_key": {"OrderId": 1005},
        "columns": {
          "OrderId": 1005,
          "CustomerId": 12345,
          "OrderDate": "2025-01-15",
          "Total": 320.00
        }
      }
    ]
  },
  "captured_at": "2025-01-15T11:30:20.150Z"
}
```

#### telemetry.json
```json
{
  "run_id": "run-001",
  "duration_ms": 125,
  "cpu_ms": 78,
  "logical_reads": 450,
  "physical_reads": 12,
  "writes": 8,
  "row_count": 25,
  "execution_count": 1,
  "wait_stats": {
    "PAGEIOLATCH_SH": 15,
    "CXPACKET": 3
  },
  "query_plan_hash": "0x1234567890ABCDEF",
  "captured_at": "2025-01-15T11:30:20.125Z"
}
```

## Implementation Tasks

### 1. Database Schema
- [ ] Create optimization_jobs table migration
- [ ] Create variants table migration
- [ ] Create runs table migration
- [ ] Add indexes for query performance

### 2. API Handlers
- [ ] Implement POST /v1/optimization-jobs
- [ ] Implement GET /v1/optimization-jobs/{jobId}
- [ ] Implement GET /v1/optimization-jobs/{jobId}/variants
- [ ] Implement GET /v1/optimization-jobs/{jobId}/runs
- [ ] Implement POST /v1/optimization-jobs/{jobId}/cancel
- [ ] Add request validation and quota checking

### 3. Job Orchestration
- [ ] Implement OptimizationJobExecutor
- [ ] Implement baseline execution workflow
- [ ] Add worker pool for parallel execution
- [ ] Implement progress tracking and updates
- [ ] Add cancellation support
- [ ] Implement retry logic with exponential backoff

### 4. Run Execution
- [ ] Implement executeRun method
- [ ] Add snapshot restore before each run
- [ ] Integrate CDC enable/disable/capture
- [ ] Add trace session management
- [ ] Implement procedure execution with parameters
- [ ] Capture execution results
- [ ] Handle procedure errors gracefully

### 5. Telemetry Collection
- [ ] Implement Extended Events session creation
- [ ] Capture STATISTICS TIME/IO output
- [ ] Capture query execution plans
- [ ] Parse and structure telemetry data
- [ ] Store telemetry in standardized format

### 6. Artifact Storage
- [ ] Implement artifact storage for results
- [ ] Implement artifact storage for CDC deltas
- [ ] Implement artifact storage for telemetry
- [ ] Implement artifact storage for traces
- [ ] Add artifact retrieval methods
- [ ] Implement artifact compression (optional)

### 7. Testing
- [ ] Unit tests for job orchestration logic
- [ ] Unit tests for run execution
- [ ] Integration tests with SQL Server
- [ ] Test parallel execution with worker pool
- [ ] Test error handling and retries
- [ ] Test CDC capture accuracy
- [ ] Test telemetry collection
- [ ] Test job cancellation
- [ ] Load test with large workloads

### 8. Monitoring
- [ ] Add metrics for job execution duration
- [ ] Add metrics for run success/failure rates
- [ ] Add metrics for parallel execution utilization
- [ ] Track artifact storage usage
- [ ] Add alerts for job failures
- [ ] Monitor SQL Server resource usage during runs

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Can create optimization job successfully
- [ ] Baseline variant is created automatically
- [ ] All workload entries are executed
- [ ] Each run restores snapshot before execution
- [ ] CDC changes are captured for each run
- [ ] Telemetry is collected for each run
- [ ] Results, CDC deltas, and telemetry are stored as artifacts
- [ ] Run errors are captured and stored
- [ ] Job progress is tracked and reported accurately
- [ ] Parallel execution respects concurrency limits
- [ ] Failed runs are retried appropriately
- [ ] Can cancel running job
- [ ] Job status transitions are correct
- [ ] All artifacts are retrievable via API

## Dependencies
- Story 1 (Project Bootstrap)
- Story 3 (SQL Server Substrate & Session Management)
- Story 4 (CDCME Integration & Workload Generation)

## Estimated Effort
- **Size**: Very Large (8-10 days)
- **Complexity**: Very High (complex orchestration, CDC operations, telemetry, parallel execution)

## Notes
- Baseline execution is the foundation for variant comparison
- Accurate CDC capture is critical for correctness validation
- Telemetry collection must be consistent across all runs
- Worker pool sizing impacts overall execution time and resource usage
- Consider implementing incremental progress saves for long-running jobs
- Monitor SQL Server instance capacity during parallel execution
- Extended Events is preferred over SQL Trace (deprecated)
- Query plans can be large - consider storage optimization
- Future: implement run result caching to avoid re-execution
