items.title: Adopt schema baseline (ADR-0011)
items.body:
Schema adoption for **Anand** after [ADR-0011](https://github.com/shri-ai-org/SHRI_HEALTH/blob/vimal/adr-0011-single-database/docs/adr/0011-single-postgresql-retire-hapi.md) (PR #11). The baseline is Sam's proposal, #9. Sources: `docs/context/P0_SCHEMA_SCOPE.md` (approved) and your guide v2 (`docs/context/03_Anand_Implementation_Guide.md`), Steps 1–2.

### Step 1 (with Sam): the schema is locked as of 2026-10-24 (D72, #32). The open items below go in as migrations and reviewed PRs; none of them gates other work
- [ ] Tag all 218 tables P0, P0 stretch, P1 or P2 in the data dictionary, following P0_SCHEMA_SCOPE.md.
- [ ] Add what is missing for the eight P0 items (all **approved as P0**):
  - claim details for corrected claims;
  - employer of patient and subscriber;
  - MRN numbering per practice;
  - HIPAA amendment requests;
  - accounting of disclosures;
  - visit status history;
  - staff messages in the inbox;
  - occupation, industry and tribal affiliation.
- [ ] Load-test (D35; gates nothing) the visit, results and claims write paths with the composite foreign keys in place (**D35:** Synthea-based loader, 3 clinics × 2,000 patients, 20,000 visits, 200,000 observations, 20,000 claims; median and p95 for create visit, file result and create claim, on the three-schema version).
- [x] ~~Re-verify migrations and tests on **PostgreSQL 18**; UUID defaults move to `uuidv7()`.~~ **Done (D28):** your 17-vs-18 verification passed; commit the report in your adoption PR as `backend/app/db/docs/pg18-verification.md`. **IDs stay UUIDv4 (D29, ADR-0009); `uuidv7()` is not adopted.**
- [x] Three schemas (`clinical`, `admin`, `audit`) and five roles with minimum grants (D23) — **done**, `anand/schema-adoption`:
  - `shri_app`
  - `shri_fhir_reader`
  - `shri_integration`
  - `shri_reporting`
  - `shri_migrator`

  RLS stays forced on every clinic table. Table-to-schema mapping and the per-role grant table are my own design (not independently reviewed yet) — flagged in the adoption report.
- [ ] **US Core version** (Q6, owner Sena) is no longer a schema gate; if it needs schema changes, they are a migration. The **CPT license** (Q7) is needed before the pilot.
- [x] ~~Team review, then lock the P0 tables only.~~ **Locked as of 2026-10-24 (D72):** Sam's schema with D38–D43, A43 and Thulasi's core tables. Your approval of #32 also records that you accept Thulasi's tables from her comment here.

Already decided, nothing to do:
- diagnosis removal = entered-in-error with "removed before signing" (D24);
- the deliberate 0..1 simplifications are approved as listed;
- PostgreSQL 18;
- a full SSN is never stored (D27), and **P0 collects no SSN at all (D43)**: see A38 below for the constraint to drop or relax.

### Step 2: adopt the schema into `backend/app/db/`
- [x] Copy the models, constraint generator, SQL and Alembic files from `proposals/fhir-schema/` in your own PR — **done**, not yet opened as a real PR / #9 not yet closed (waiting on the P0 lock items below first).
- [x] Remove what the team replaced:
  - the generated admin CRUD endpoints;
  - the proposal's login and token-claim reading;
  - its error mapping.

  **Done.** `backend/app/fhir/api.py` has a documented `machine_token_auth` seam instead of inventing Thulasi's machine-token check (see issue #12's open "Machine tokens for `/fhir`" item — still pending on her side).
- [x] Agree the `tenant_db` settings with Thulasi: `app.current_tenant_id`, `app.current_user_id`, `app.correlation_id`. The clinic comes from the server-side session. **Done in #7** (merged): `tenant_db` sets exactly these three, per transaction.
- [x] Regenerate the rules and docs. Run migrations, `alembic check` and the tests in CI — rules/docs regenerated, migrations + tests pass **locally** (43/43); **not yet in CI** (no PR open against this code yet, and `backend.yml`'s `TEST_DATABASE_URL`/asyncpg convention doesn't match my tests' `SHRI_DATABASE_URL`/psycopg yet - needs reconciling, noted on #7's review). **Done in #45:** migrations 0001 to 0004 run as `shri_migrator` on the real image in CI, `alembic check` is clean, every test passes (37f6a12).
- [x] **After the three-schema split, rerun everything (D36):** migrations, `alembic check`, the full test suite, the trigger and role checks, and the `content_tsv` GIN index build — **done** (`alembic check` itself is unreliable across these 3 schemas, two different runs gave two different false-positive diffs, both disproven directly against the catalog; relying on the schema-wide pytest assertions instead).
- [x] **Schema test that fails on any computed column that is not STORED (D34).** — `test_no_virtual_generated_columns`, passing.
- [x] **Collation C.UTF-8 (D33)** — done. **RDS pgvector version 0.8.2 (D31)** — my local verification used 0.8.7 (already assessed safe, not the exact pin); #7's actual dev/CI image now has 0.8.2, so this should be re-tested against that image rather than my own build before the lock. Re-tested on the image in #45's CI.
- [x] Publish the data dictionary in the repo — generator exists (`tools/gen_docs.py`), not yet run and committed. **Done in #45:** `backend/app/db/docs/data_dictionary.md`, with contract names.

### From the batch 1 contracts (PR #17; details in `contracts/docs/notes/NOTE_FOR_ANAND.md`)
- [x] **A38:** the masked-SSN uniqueness defect (`uq_identifier_patient_value`) — **done**: excluded the SSN system from the per-owner uniqueness indexes (masking is meant to collide across patients; uniqueness on it was the actual bug).
- [x] **A39:** a practice-level payer table for `/practice-payers` — **done**: new `admin.practice_payer` (tenant_id, payer_id, is_active).
- [x] **A41:** version columns on admin tables — **mostly done**: new `VersionedMixin` + `shri_bump_version()` trigger on facility, appointment_type, note_template, lab_provider, lab_account, patient_pharmacy, payer, fee_schedule, practice_payer. **Not done:** setting the preferred pharmacy bumping the *patient's* own version (**Vimal's patients service does this**: it updates the patient row in the same transaction, #34) — that's cross-table behavior for whoever builds the preferred-pharmacy endpoint, not a schema change.
- [x] **A42:** drop `UNIQUE (appointment_id, step)` on `visit_flow_event` — **done**, replaced with a plain index for the status-board query; stayed insert-only.
- Already decided there, nothing to do: lab providers are read-only, set up by onboarding or the platform (D48, was A40).

### Open now (added 2026-10-24 by Vimal, after D72)
- [x] **Open the adoption PR** from `anand/schema-adoption` (807144c) to `main`. It *is* the locked schema, but it's only on a branch: #34 (batch 1 alignment) and #38 (batch 2) are written against it, and no backend module can use it until it's on `main`. When it's open, close Sam's #9 as superseded. **Done:** #45, ready for review.
- [ ] **Thulasi's core tables** (her comment above): `admin.app_session`, `admin.idempotency_record`, `admin.operation`, `admin.event_log`, and the changes to `admin.integration_message`, `audit.audit_event`, `audit.break_glass_access`, in the adoption PR or its first migration. Her `enqueue()` work (#12) waits for the `integration_message` changes.
- [ ] **A43** (batch 1 follow-up): `admin.consent_requirement`, `admin.patient_payment.receipt_file_id`, the license-image link on `identifier`, the per-merge undo rule (you took these on above).

items.title: Spec: Core Transactional Path & Stock Reservation Engine (Phase 1)

labels.name: ready-for-agent
labels.description: Fully specified, ready for an AFK agent

items.body:
## Problem Statement

High-volume multi-tenant e-commerce merchants experience overselling, race conditions during flash sales, lost audit trails, and inventory sync discrepancies across multiple warehouses. Current systems struggle to handle concurrent stock reservations for hot SKUs with sub-100ms response times while maintaining strict transactional consistency.

## Solution

Build Phase 1 of the Distributed Inventory Management System: a Go-based gRPC Stock Service and Reservation Service utilizing PostgreSQL Row-Level Security (RLS) for multi-tenancy, row-level locking (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`) on the fast write model (`stock_levels`), atomic audit log generation (`stock_events`), Transactional Outbox pattern for asynchronous event publication, and all-or-nothing reservation semantics.

## User Stories

1. As a tenant merchant, I want inventory mutations isolated per tenant using PostgreSQL Row-Level Security, so that my stock data is never visible to or mutated by other tenants.
2. As a merchant system, I want to reserve stock across one or more SKUs for an order during a payment window, so that items are held exclusively for the customer without overselling.
3. As an order service, I want all-or-nothing reservation guarantees across multi-item orders, so that an order fails immediately if any requested SKU cannot be reserved.
4. As an order service, I want reservations to automatically expire after a configurable TTL (15 minutes default), so that abandoned order holds are released back to Available Stock.
5. As an order service, I want to transition Reserved Stock to Allocated Stock synchronously via gRPC post-payment, so that TTL expiry sweepers can no longer release confirmed order inventory.
6. As a warehouse manager, I want an immutable audit trail of every stock mutation recorded synchronously in `stock_events`, so that inventory changes are fully traceable.
7. As an integration worker, I want stock mutations to write domain events to a Transactional Outbox table in the local database transaction, so that Debezium CDC can stream events to Kafka without dual-write race conditions.
8. As an API client, I want gRPC write endpoints to enforce exact-once execution via `processed_idempotency_keys` in the local database transaction, so that duplicate retries return cached responses without re-executing state changes.
9. As a warehouse manager, I want nightly reconciliation to detect drift between `stock_levels` and `stock_events`, automatically placing an `Audit Lock` (`is_locked_for_audit = true`) on the SKU to block reservations until cleared.
10. As a warehouse manager, I want to clear an Audit Lock via an explicit `UnlockStockForAudit` admin endpoint after reviewing discrepancies, so that normal reservation traffic can resume safely.
11. As an external channel worker (e.g. Shopify POS), I want to adjust stock via `AdjustStock`, clamping negative Available Stock to 0 and emitting an urgent deficit alert, so that external inventory sync does not crash or leave invalid stock states.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Domain Vocabulary Alignment**: Strictly enforces terms defined in `CONTEXT.md` (`Available Stock`, `Reserved Stock`, `Allocated Stock`, `Fulfilled Stock`, `Stock Level`, `Stock Event`, `Outbox Event`, `Audit Lock`, `Idempotency Record`, `Tenant`).
- **Architecture Foundations**: Adheres to `ADR-0001` (Shared Tables + Postgres RLS, Transactional Outbox + Debezium CDC, Row-Locked Write Model + Audit Log).
- **gRPC Services & Protobuf Schemas**:
  - `StockService`: `AdjustStock`, `ConfirmStockAllocation`, `UnlockStockForAudit`
  - `ReservationService`: `Reserve`, `Release`
- **Database Schemas & Multi-Tenancy**:
  - PostgreSQL Row-Level Security (RLS) enabled on all service tables using `tenant_id`.
  - `stock_levels`: `tenant_id`, `sku_id`, `warehouse_id`, `available_qty`, `reserved_qty`, `allocated_qty`, `is_locked_for_audit`, `updated_at`.
  - `stock_events`: `id`, `tenant_id`, `sku_id`, `warehouse_id`, `delta`, `reason`, `source`, `actor_id`, `created_at`.
  - `reservations`: `id`, `tenant_id`, `order_id`, `expires_at`, `status` (`ACTIVE`, `RELEASED`, `ALLOCATED`, `EXPIRED`), `created_at`.
  - `outbox`: `id`, `tenant_id`, `aggregate_type`, `aggregate_id`, `event_type`, `payload`, `created_at`.
  - `processed_idempotency_keys`: `tenant_id`, `idempotency_key`, `payload_hash`, `created_at`.
- **Locking & Concurrency**: Row locking (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`) inside PostgreSQL transactions for `Reserve`, `Release`, `AllocateStock`, and `AdjustStock`.
- **Outbox Pruning**: Managed per service via `pg_partman` daily partitioning or scheduled worker cleanup.

## Testing Decisions

- Tests will focus exclusively on external behavior at the gRPC API surface and atomic database state boundaries without coupling to internal function structures.
- **Unit & Integration Tests**: Test `StockService` and `ReservationService` gRPC handlers against a live PostgreSQL instance.
- **Concurrency Test**: Execute parallel benchmark tests hammering `Reserve` on a single hot SKU with 50 initial units, asserting exactly 50 succeed, remaining fail with insufficient stock, and `available_qty` never drops below 0.

## Out of Scope

- Multi-region active-active database replication.
- Kafka broker cluster and Debezium Connect deployment (Phase 2).
- Order Service Saga orchestrator & Payment gateway integration (Phase 2).
- Frontend UI or real-time analytics dashboard (Phase 3).

## Further Notes

- Protobuf definitions to be located in `proto/stock/v1/stock.proto` and `proto/reservation/v1/reservation.proto`.
- Services built in Go using `sqlc` for type-safe database queries.

items.body:
## Contexte

Ticket de l'épique #843. Les confirmations, rappels et avis d'annulation font partie du parcours client (CDC §1.4). Une cliente anglophone doit donc les recevoir en anglais.

Aujourd'hui, les modèles par défaut n'existent qu'en français (`notification-default-templates.ts`). Les personnalisations en base, elles, ne sont indexées que par type et par canal (`NotificationTemplate` dans `apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma`).

## Critères d'acceptation

- [ ] La plateforme fournit des modèles par défaut en `fr` et en `en` pour chaque type (confirmation, rappel J-1, annulation côté cliente, annulation côté équipe, **réinitialisation du mot de passe** `PASSWORD_RESET`) et pour chaque canal. Chaque valeur de `NOTIFICATION_TYPES` a ses modèles dans les deux langues, et un test échoue s'il en manque un.
- [ ] Un message part dans la langue préférée du destinataire, sinon dans la langue par défaut de l'établissement (`en` sauf choix contraire, #844). La langue retenue est enregistrée sur la notification émise.
- [ ] Les dates et heures du message sont formatées dans la langue d'envoi et dans le fuseau de l'établissement.
- [ ] Les personnalisations se font par langue :
  - `notification_templates` gagne une dimension `locale`, avec une unicité établissement × type × canal × langue ;
  - quand une langue n'a pas de personnalisation, le message retombe sur le modèle par défaut de la plateforme **dans cette même langue**, jamais sur l'autre langue.
- [ ] L'API des modèles (lecture, écriture, aperçu) accepte la langue. Chacun de ses endpoints a son test d'isolation inter-tenant.
- [ ] La langue du rappel J-1 (chaîne EventBridge → SQS → Lambda) est déterminée au moment de l'envoi, pas au moment de la planification.
- [ ] Un test vérifie que les modèles SMS anglais respectent la même limite de longueur que les modèles français.
- [ ] L'idempotence des envois reste la même.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Code revu et approuvé
- [ ] Tests unitaires et d'intégration passants
- [ ] Test d'isolation inter-tenant pour tout endpoint nouveau ou modifié
- [ ] Déployé et vérifié en recette
- [ ] Documenté (README de module, ADR si décision structurante)

---

Epic : #843 · Effort indicatif : 1.5 j·h · Dépend de #844

Risque à impact élevé du CDC §6. Une vérification applicative suivie d'un INSERT est structurellement fausse sous concurrence : la garantie doit venir de la base. Voir ADR 0002.

## Critères d'acceptation

items.body:
<!-- local-draft: D:\Proyectos\Encina\artifacts\local-ai\out\rewrite-2013.md -->
## Summary

A dead letter replay runs under the identity stored with the message (tenant, actor, correlation and cause), not under the operator's context, and every operator replay and delete is recorded in the operation audit store.

## Motivation

Today an operator replays a dead letter through `DeadLetterManager.ReplayAsync` (`src/Encina.Messaging/DeadLetter/DeadLetterManager.cs:172`; the dispatch is `ReplayStoredMessageAsync` :312, `ReplayRequestAsync` and `DispatchAsync`). The stored request is deserialized and sent through `IEncina.Send` or `IEncina.Publish` under whatever request context the operator's call carries. The original text cited lines 122-141; they moved. This violates the identity persistence model of #1705 and the deferred dispatch rules of SPEC-002 REQ-015 and P-50 (#1164): the originating actor must be persisted and rebuilt, never replaced.

State of the code (verified on `7a0049c07`):

| Item | Today |
|------|-------|
| Stored fields | `IDeadLetterMessage` (`src/Encina.Messaging/DeadLetter/IDeadLetterMessage.cs`) has `TenantId` and `CorrelationId` (added by #583, closed), and no `ActorId` or `CausationId` |
| Tenant at replay | `DeadLetterManager` defaults reads, replays and deletes to the ambient tenant and rejects a replay of another tenant's message (`AmbientTenantId`, `DenyTenantRequired`), but dispatches under the operator's context, not the stored one |
| Restore API | Exists: `PersistedRequestIdentity(Kind, ActorId, TenantId, CorrelationId, CausationId)` (`src/Encina/Identity/PersistedRequestIdentity.cs:25`), `IRequestContextScopeFactory` and `RunRestoredAsync` (`RequestContextScopeFactoryExtensions.cs:101`), `PersistedIdentitySource` `Internal` and `External`; #1705 is open for later phases |
| Audit | `DeadLetterManager` writes no audit entry for replay, replay-all, delete or delete-all (`ReplayAsync` :172, `ReplayAllAsync` :430, `DeleteAsync` :556, `DeleteAllAsync` :601); `IOperationAuditStore.RecordAsync` exists (`src/Encina.Security.Audit/Abstractions/IOperationAuditStore.cs:50`) |
| Dependency direction | `Encina.Security.Audit` references `Encina.Messaging` (`Encina.Security.Audit.csproj`), `Encina.Messaging` references only `Encina` |
| #583 | Closed (blocker resolved); its plan left `ActorId` and `CausationId` to this issue (Design Choice B8) |

Decision history. Maintainer decision of 2026-10-09: this issue adds two nullable columns, `ActorId` (max 256) and `CausationId` (max 256), to the dead letter record of all 10 providers, filled from the request context at capture, so a replay restores the original identity and cause chain (SPEC-002 REQ-015); `ActorId` is personal data when it is a person: never in logs or telemetry, deleted with the row by the DLQ retention. Maintainer decisions of 2026-10-16 on replay and delete under the stored context are in Alternatives Considered (C1 to C5) and go into the `## Maintainer Decisions` section of this issue's implementation plan, which is still to be written (`docs/plans/`), before any brief. This issue and #583 were prioritized to be done right after each other.

## Proposed Solution

Replay restores the stored tenant, actor, correlation and cause through `IRequestContextScopeFactory.RunRestoredAsync` before it dispatches, and the work runs inside that scope. If the stored tenant cannot be resolved, the replay is rejected with an error code and nothing is dispatched. Replay and delete are recorded through a small audit port in `Encina.Messaging`, implemented by an adapter in `Encina.Security.Audit` over `IOperationAuditStore`.

Corrected sketch of the original pseudocode (the original used `ITenantContext.ResolveAsync`, `RequestContext` constructor and `IOperationAuditStore.LogAsync`, none of which exist; `throw` is replaced by the Railway-oriented result):

```csharp
public async Task<Either<EncinaError, ReplayResult>> ReplayAsync(Guid messageId, CancellationToken ct = default)
{
    // ... existing tenant scoping, replayability check and atomic claim ...

    var persisted = new PersistedRequestIdentity(
        message.IdentityKind, message.ActorId, message.TenantId, message.CorrelationId, message.CausationId);
    var source = message.SourcePattern == DeadLetterSourcePatterns.Inbox
        ? PersistedIdentitySource.External       // crossed the trust boundary: anonymous, tenant from trusted data
        : PersistedIdentitySource.Internal;

    // 1. audit the intent: if this write fails, nothing is replayed (fail-closed)
    // 2. restore the identity and dispatch inside the scope
    // 3. audit the outcome (outcome code only)
}
```

Audit port (name and members settled by the plan): `IDeadLetterAuditSink`-style interface in `Encina.Messaging` with operations for replay intent, replay outcome and delete; adapter `OperationAuditDeadLetterSink` in `Encina.Security.Audit`. Under the module-requires-module rule decided on #2239 (ADR-050) the dead letter queue requires that adapter: registering the DLQ without it fails at startup.

### Observability

| Metric Name | Type | Description |
|-------------|------|-------------|
| `encina.deadletter.replay_total` | Counter | Replays initiated (tag `status`: `success`, `fail_tenant_unresolved`, `fail_validation`, `fail_audit`) |
| `encina.deadletter.replay_duration` | Histogram | Context restoration plus dispatch |
| `encina.deadletter.delete_total` | Counter | Deletes (tag `status`: `success`, `fail_audit`) |

| Span Name | Attributes | Description |
|-----------|------------|-------------|
| `encina.deadletter.replay` | `outcome` | Replay including context restoration |
| `encina.deadletter.audit` | `action`, `outcome` | Operator action audit |

The attributes `message_id`, `stored_tenant_id`, `stored_correlation_id`, `operator_id`, `restored_tenant` and `tenant_id` of the original table are removed: the tenant is never a telemetry dimension of the dead letter queue and the actor is personal data (see C6). The span `encina.deadletter.tenant_resolution` becomes an event inside `encina.deadletter.replay`. Final names are checked against ADR-054 by the plan.

## Alternatives Considered

Decision register (Trivial, Settled, Dilemma). Three Dilemmas are open; only the maintainer decides them.

**Dilemma D1: How is the identity kind stored?** Restoring needs `PersistedRequestIdentity.Kind` (`IdentityKind`). The 2026-10-09 decision said no `Kind` column until `PersistedRequestIdentity` is merged; it is merged now.
- Option A: a third nullable column (`ActorKind`) stored as a short string. Pros: exact, no inference, and the same shape as `PersistedRequestIdentity`. Cons: a third column on 10 providers. Wins when the kinds can grow (user, service, anonymous, inbound).
- Option B: derive the kind from `ActorId` (the `service:` prefix of `RequestIdentity.ServiceSubjectPrefix`, null for anonymous). Pros: only the two columns the maintainer decided. Cons: inference breaks if an id format changes, and it cannot represent a kind with no marker. Wins when only user, service and anonymous exist.

**Dilemma D2: How is a batch replay or delete audited?** (`ReplayAllAsync`, `DeleteAllAsync`)
- Option A: one entry per message (intent and outcome). Pros: complete trail for each message, matches single replay. Cons: many entries for a large batch. Wins when auditors reconstruct what happened to each message.
- Option B: one batch entry (filter, count, outcome) plus per-message entries only for failures. Pros: compact. Cons: a message replayed in a batch has no entry of its own. Wins for very large batches.

**Dilemma D3: What does "unresolvable tenant" mean?** The decided behaviour is to reject the replay with an error code; the check is open.
- Option A: the stored tenant is missing, malformed or refused by the scope factory (`RunRestoredAsync` returns a refusal). Pros: no new dependency, `Encina.Messaging` stays free of tenancy. Cons: a tenant that was deleted since capture still passes. Wins when tenant lifecycle is managed outside Encina.
- Option B: also ask a tenant-existence port that `Encina.Tenancy` implements (`ITenantProvider`). Pros: a deleted or disabled tenant is refused. Cons: a new port in Messaging and a Tenancy dependency in the registration. Wins when tenants are created and removed at run time.

Settled choices (maintainer decisions of 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-16, and rules):

- **C1, audit placement (settled, maintainer A1).** A small audit port in `Encina.Messaging`, implemented by an adapter in `Encina.Security.Audit` on `IOperationAuditStore` (ADR-036); the dead letter queue requires that adapter and registering without it fails at startup. Citation: maintainer comment of 2026-10-16 on this issue; the rule decided on #2239; ADR-050.
- **C2, audit order (settled).** Audit the intent before dispatch (if that write fails, nothing is replayed, fail-closed) and the outcome after. Citation: maintainer comment of 2026-10-16; SPEC-002 REQ-019; `AGENTS.md` section 3 (gates fail closed).
- **C3, delete is a hard delete (settled).** Hard delete plus an audit entry without payload; no soft delete. This replaces the soft-delete alternative of the original text. Citation: maintainer comment of 2026-10-16; GDPR Art. 17 and Art. 5(1)(e).
- **C4, restored context (settled).** Original tenant, actor, correlation and cause (SPEC-002 REQ-015); the operator is recorded in the audit entry. The original alternative "restore the tenant only and keep the operator's correlation id" breaks causal tracing and is not taken. Citation: maintainer comment of 2026-10-16; SPEC-002 REQ-015; #1705.
- **C5, unresolvable tenant rejects the replay with an error code (settled).** The check itself is Dilemma D3. Citation: maintainer comment of 2026-10-16; SPEC-002 DEC-006.
- **C6, columns and privacy (settled).** `ActorId` (max 256) and `CausationId` (max 256), nullable, on all 10 providers, filled from the request context at capture; `ActorId` never in logs or telemetry and deleted with the row by the DLQ retention. Citation: maintainer comment of 2026-10-09; SPEC-002 REQ-062; `PersistedRequestIdentity.ToString()` hides the actor.
- **C7, inbox dead letters restore as external (settled).** A dead letter whose source is the inbox crossed the trust boundary; the identity is restored as anonymous with an inbound origin and only a trusted tenant is used, never the persisted actor. Citation: `PersistedIdentitySource` documentation (`src/Encina/Identity/PersistedIdentitySource.cs`); #1164. Related defect: #3442.
- **C8, errors travel as codes (settled).** The audit record and the replay result carry outcome codes only, never `EncinaError.Message`. Citation: `AGENTS.md` section 3; the existing `ReplayResult` rule of #2012.
- **C9, time (trivial).** Audit timestamps come from `TimeProvider`, not `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow` (the original sketch used it). Citation: `AGENTS.md` section 3.
- **C10, database calls (trivial).** Asynchronous with a `CancellationToken`. Citation: `AGENTS.md` section 3.
- **C11, retention cleanup is not an operator action (settled).** `CleanupExpiredAsync` (:630) and the cleanup processor are system retention and are not audited by this issue. Citation: the title and scope of this issue (operator replay and delete).

## Affected Packages

- [ ] Encina (core): no change; the restore API already exists
- [ ] Encina.EntityFrameworkCore: listed under Provider Implementation Matrix
- [ ] Encina.Dapper.*
- [ ] Encina.ADO.*
- [ ] Encina.AspNetCore: ticked in the original; no change is planned here
- [ ] Encina.MongoDB
- [ ] Encina.OpenTelemetry
- [ ] Encina.Caching.*
- [x] Encina.Messaging (`IDeadLetterMessage`, `DeadLetterManager`, `DeadLetterOrchestrator` capture, audit port, registration requirement)
- [ ] Encina.Polly
- [ ] Encina.Cdc
- [x] Other: `Encina.Security.Audit` (adapter), the 10 database provider packages (ADO.NET SqlServer, PostgreSQL, MySQL; Dapper the same three; `Encina.EntityFrameworkCore` for its three providers; `Encina.MongoDB`)

## Provider Implementation Matrix

> Per `AGENTS.md` section 5: this feature changes the dead letter record on every database provider, so all 10 are required (schema, capture, read, and the restored replay).

| Provider | ActorId / CausationId columns | Identity kind (D1) | Notes |
|----------|:-:|:-:|-------|
| ADO-SqlServer | | | |
| ADO-PostgreSQL | | | |
| ADO-MySQL | | | |
| Dapper-SqlServer | | | |
| Dapper-PostgreSQL | | | |
| Dapper-MySQL | | | |
| EFCore-SqlServer | | | |
| EFCore-PostgreSQL | | | |
| EFCore-MySQL | | | |
| MongoDB | | | |

The adapter of the audit port uses `IOperationAuditStore`, which is already implemented on the 10 providers (#1633, closed).

## Cross-Cutting Integration

> Per `AGENTS.md` section 6 (ADR-018): each function is Integrate, Defer or Not applicable.

| # | Function | Status | Notes |
|---|----------|--------|-------|
| 1 | **Caching** | Not applicable | Replay is an operator action on a single row. |
| 2 | **OpenTelemetry** | Integrate | Replay span and counters; no actor or tenant as a dimension (C6). |
| 3 | **Structured Logging** | Integrate | New `[LoggerMessage]` events in the messaging range, error codes only, `ForLogging()` for exceptions. |
| 4 | **Health Checks** | Not applicable | Operator-initiated action, not a dependency; the existing dead letter health check is unchanged. |
| 5 | **Validation** | Integrate | Stored identity values are validated on capture and on restore (lengths, format). |
| 6 | **Resilience** | Not applicable | The existing replay has its timeout; no external call is added. |
| 7 | **Distributed Locks** | Not applicable | The replay claim is already atomic (`TryClaimForReplayAsync`, #2012). |
| 8 | **Transactions** | Defer (plan) | Intent before and outcome after (C2); the audit store may live in another database, so a shared transaction cannot be assumed. |
| 9 | **Idempotency** | Integrate | The restored correlation and cause keep the idempotency key stable; related to #3442 for inbox dead letters. |
| 10 | **Multi-Tenancy** | Integrate | Core of the feature: the stored tenant is restored or the replay is rejected (C5, D3). |
| 11 | **Module Isolation** | Defer (#747) | A stored `ModuleId`, if present, is restored under the module isolation issue. |
| 12 | **Audit Trail** | Integrate | Operator replay and delete are audited (C1 to C3). |

## Test Matrix

> Per `AGENTS.md` section 9 (Testing obligations).

| Test Type | Required? | Scope | Notes |
|-----------|:---------:|-------|-------|
| **UnitTests** | Required | `DeadLetterManager` restore path, fail-closed branches, audit order, adapter | Real manager with substituted store and sink at the boundary |
| **GuardTests** | Required | New public methods and constructors | `ArgumentNullException` |
| **ContractTests** | Required | The audit port and `IDeadLetterMessage` additions | |
| **PropertyTests** | Required | Persisted identity round trip (capture to restore) | FsCheck |
| **IntegrationTests** | Required | Capture, restore and audit on all 10 providers, cross-tenant isolation | Shared `[Collection("<Family>-<Database>")]` fixtures; never a `.md` justification for database features |
| **LoadTests** | Not applicable | Operator-initiated, not concurrent hot path | Justification file `.md` |
| **BenchmarkTests** | Not applicable | Operator-initiated | Justification file `.md` |

## Implementation Tasks

### Core Abstractions

- [ ] `ActorId` and `CausationId` (and the kind, per D1) on `IDeadLetterMessage` and the capture contexts
- [ ] Capture fills them from the request context (`DeadLetterOrchestrator`, `DeadLetterContext`)
- [ ] Audit port in `Encina.Messaging` and its adapter in `Encina.Security.Audit`
- [ ] Startup requirement: the DLQ registration fails without the adapter
- [ ] `DeadLetterManager.ReplayAsync` and `ReplayAllAsync` restore through `RunRestoredAsync` and audit intent then outcome
- [ ] `DeleteAsync` and `DeleteAllAsync` audit without payload (D2)
- [ ] Unresolvable tenant rejects with an error code (D3)

### Provider Implementations (if applicable)

- [ ] ADO.NET providers (3): schema and store changes
- [ ] Dapper providers (3): schema and store changes
- [ ] EF Core providers (3): model and mapping changes
- [ ] MongoDB provider (1): document fields

### Observability

- [ ] OpenTelemetry metrics (3)
- [ ] Traces / spans (2)
- [ ] Structured logging events

### Testing

- [ ] UnitTests
- [ ] GuardTests

items.title: frf-broker-iggy: subscribe and publish target different Iggy streams (realtime receipt impossible against real broker)
items.body:
## Summary

In `crates/frf-broker-iggy`, the **subscribe** and **publish** paths target
**different Iggy streams and topics**, so a subscribe can never observe a publish
against a real Iggy server. `consumer.init()` fails with `Stream: channel-<uuid>
was not found` because nothing ever creates that stream.

## Divergence

| Path | stream | topic |
|---|---|---|
| `publish` / `ensure_channel` (`src/broker.rs:93`, `:265`; `src/channel.rs:7`) | `tenant-{tenant_id}` | `topic_name(path)` (e.g. `entity_smoke_realtime`) |
| `subscribe` (`src/broker.rs:129`) | `channel-{channel_id}` | `"events"` (hardcoded) |

`ensure_channel` and the boot-time fixture (`crates/frf-gateway/src/main.rs:115`)
both create `tenant-<uuid>`. Subscribe consumes from `channel-<uuid>`/`events`,
which nothing creates.

## Reproduction

Against a real Iggy server (not a mock), open a subscribe via the gateway
`/ws/v1/subscribe?channel=<uuid>`, then `POST /v1/publish` an `EventEnvelope` for
the same channel. Observed:

```
ERROR iggy::clients::consumer: Stream: channel-<uuid> was not found.
```

The WS upgrade then fails and the subscribe returns an error to the caller.

This is also latent in the crate's own integration test
`crates/frf-broker-iggy/tests/publish_subscribe.rs`, which `ensure_channel`s +
`publish`es to `tenant-<nil>` but `subscribe`s from `channel-<id>`. That test is
`#[ignore]`, so this path has never run green in CI.

## Impact

End-to-end realtime receipt is impossible against a real broker: a subscriber
never receives published events. Surfaced by `flint-platform-agent`'s real
end-to-end smoke — its `/fabric/subscribe` SSE bridge returns HTTP 502 because
fabric's subscribe errors out on the missing stream. Auth is not involved; the
RS256 bearer verifies and the pipeline reaches `consumer.init()` before failing.

## Suggested fix

Align subscribe's stream/topic naming with publish — use `stream_name(tenant_id)`
+ `topic_name(path)` on the subscribe/offset/poll/ack paths, and wire
`ensure_channel` into the subscribe path (or resolve the channel's tenant/path so
subscribe and publish provably meet on the same stream+topic). Then un-`#[ignore]`
`publish_subscribe.rs` so CI guards this end-to-end.

items.title: [Task 2 - Story 4] Proctus: CDCME Integration & Workload Generation
items.body:
# Story 4: CDCME Integration & Workload Generation

## Overview
Integrate the existing CDCME capabilities for CDC (Change Data Capture) operations and implement AI-driven workload generation for stored procedure testing.

## Goals
- Define and implement CDCME integration boundary (library or service)
- Create workload generation API using LLM
- Store generated workloads for reuse
- Implement procedure introspection and dependency discovery
- Create AI adapter layer for LLM interactions
- Support workload persistence and retrieval

## Technical Requirements

### CDCME Integration Strategy

#### Selected Approach: Library Integration (Option 1 from technical doc)
For MVP, integrate CDCME as a library to minimize operational overhead and network latency.

#### CDCME Interface Contract

**Module/Package**: `pkg/cdcme`

```go
type Manager interface {
    // Enable CDC on database and specified tables
    EnableCDC(ctx context.Context, instanceRef string, dbName string, tables []string) error
    
    // Disable CDC on database
    DisableCDC(ctx context.Context, instanceRef string, dbName string) error
    
    // Capture CDC changes since marker
    CaptureCDCChanges(ctx context.Context, instanceRef string, dbName string, startLSN string) (*CDCDelta, error)
    
    // Compare two CDC deltas for equivalence
    CompareCDCDeltas(baseline *CDCDelta, candidate *CDCDelta) (*DeltaComparison, error)
}

type CDCDelta struct {
    StartLSN     string
    EndLSN       string
    Tables       map[string][]ChangeRecord
    CapturedAt   time.Time
}

type ChangeRecord struct {
    Operation   string  // INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE
    Columns     map[string]interface{}
    PrimaryKey  map[string]interface{}
}

type DeltaComparison struct {
    IsEquivalent bool
    Differences  []DeltaDifference
}

type DeltaDifference struct {
    Table       string
    Description string
    Severity    string  // CRITICAL, WARNING, INFO
}
```

### Workload Generation System

#### AI/LLM Adapter Layer

**Module**: `internal/ai`

```go
type LLMProvider interface {
    // Analyze stored procedure and generate test workload
    GenerateWorkload(ctx context.Context, request *WorkloadGenerationRequest) (*WorkloadGenerationResponse, error)
    
    // Analyze procedure and discover dependencies
    DiscoverDependencies(ctx context.Context, request *DependencyDiscoveryRequest) (*DependencyDiscoveryResponse, error)
    
    // Generate procedure variants (covered in Story 5)
    GenerateVariants(ctx context.Context, request *VariantGenerationRequest) (*VariantGenerationResponse, error)
}

type WorkloadGenerationRequest struct {
    ProcedureDefinition string
    DatabaseSchema      *SchemaMetadata
    WorkloadConfig      *WorkloadConfig
    PromptVersion       string
}

type WorkloadConfig struct {
    NumCalls            int      // Number of test calls to generate
    IncludeErrorCases   bool     // Include intentional error scenarios
    CoverageGoals       []string // e.g., ["edge_cases", "typical_use", "stress"]
}

type WorkloadGenerationResponse struct {
    Entries       []WorkloadEntry
    Model         string
    PromptVersion string
    TokensUsed    int
    GeneratedAt   time.Time
}

type WorkloadEntry struct {
    Index             int
    Parameters        map[string]interface{}
    ExpectedBehavior  string  // "success", "error", etc.
    Description       string  // What this call is testing
}

type SchemaMetadata struct {
    Tables       []TableInfo
    Relationships []ForeignKeyInfo
    Indexes      []IndexInfo
}
```

#### LLM Provider Implementation
- Support OpenAI GPT-4 initially
- Pluggable for other providers (Anthropic, Azure OpenAI, etc.)
- Implement retry logic with exponential backoff
- Add rate limiting and quota management
- Redact sensitive data from prompts

### API Endpoints

#### POST /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/workloads
Generate a workload for a stored procedure

**Request**:
```json
{
  "procedure_id": "proc-001",
  "config": {
    "num_calls": 50,
    "include_error_cases": true,
    "coverage_goals": ["edge_cases", "typical_use"]
  },
  "prompt_version": "v1.2"
}
```

**Response** (202 Accepted):
```json
{
  "workload_id": "770e8400-e29b-41d4-a716-446655440002",
  "status": "GENERATING",
  "estimated_duration_seconds": 30,
  "links": {
    "self": "/v1/workloads/770e8400-e29b-41d4-a716-446655440002"
  }
}
```

#### GET /v1/workloads/{workloadId}
Get workload generation status and metadata

#### GET /v1/workloads/{workloadId}/entries
Retrieve workload entries (test cases)

### Metadata Store Updates

#### New table: `workloads`
```sql
CREATE TABLE workloads (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    tenant_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(id),
    session_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES sessions(id),
    procedure_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES stored_procedures(id),
    status VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, -- GENERATING, COMPLETED, FAILED
    workload_version VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL DEFAULT '1',
    generator_model VARCHAR(64),
    prompt_version VARCHAR(32),
    seed VARCHAR(64), -- For reproducibility
    entry_count INT,
    entries_artifact_ref TEXT, -- Storage URI for full workload entries
    config JSONB,
    metadata JSONB, -- tokens used, generation time, etc.
    created_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    completed_at TIMESTAMP,
    CONSTRAINT workloads_tenant_fk FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id) REFERENCES tenants(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    CONSTRAINT workloads_session_fk FOREIGN KEY (session_id) REFERENCES sessions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    CONSTRAINT workloads_proc_fk FOREIGN KEY (procedure_id) REFERENCES stored_procedures(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);
CREATE INDEX idx_workloads_session ON workloads(session_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_workloads_procedure ON workloads(procedure_id);
```

#### New table: `procedure_dependencies`
```sql
CREATE TABLE procedure_dependencies (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    procedure_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES stored_procedures(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    dependency_type VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, -- TABLE, VIEW, PROCEDURE, FUNCTION
    schema VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL,
    name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    access_type VARCHAR(32), -- READ, WRITE, EXECUTE
    discovered_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    metadata JSONB
);
CREATE INDEX idx_procedure_dependencies_proc ON procedure_dependencies(procedure_id);
```

#### New table: `database_schema_cache`
```sql
CREATE TABLE database_schema_cache (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    session_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES sessions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    table_schema VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL,
    table_name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    schema_json JSONB NOT NULL, -- Full table metadata
    cached_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    CONSTRAINT schema_cache_session_table UNIQUE (session_id, table_schema, table_name)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_schema_cache_session ON database_schema_cache(session_id);
```

### Procedure Introspection & Dependency Discovery

#### SQL Queries for Schema Discovery

**List Tables and Columns**:
```sql
SELECT 
    t.TABLE_SCHEMA, t.TABLE_NAME, c.COLUMN_NAME,
    c.DATA_TYPE, c.CHARACTER_MAXIMUM_LENGTH,
    c.IS_NULLABLE, c.COLUMN_DEFAULT
FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES t
JOIN INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS c 
    ON t.TABLE_SCHEMA = c.TABLE_SCHEMA 
    AND t.TABLE_NAME = c.TABLE_NAME
WHERE t.TABLE_TYPE = 'BASE TABLE'
ORDER BY t.TABLE_SCHEMA, t.TABLE_NAME, c.ORDINAL_POSITION;
```

**Foreign Keys**:
```sql
SELECT 
    fk.name AS constraint_name,
    OBJECT_SCHEMA_NAME(fk.parent_object_id) AS table_schema,
    OBJECT_NAME(fk.parent_object_id) AS table_name,
    COL_NAME(fkc.parent_object_id, fkc.parent_column_id) AS column_name,
    OBJECT_SCHEMA_NAME(fk.referenced_object_id) AS referenced_schema,
    OBJECT_NAME(fk.referenced_object_id) AS referenced_table,
    COL_NAME(fkc.referenced_object_id, fkc.referenced_column_id) AS referenced_column
FROM sys.foreign_keys fk
JOIN sys.foreign_key_columns fkc ON fk.object_id = fkc.constraint_object_id;
```

### Prompt Engineering for Workload Generation

#### System Prompt Template (v1.2)
```
You are an expert SQL Server database testing engineer. Your task is to generate realistic test workloads for stored procedures.

Given:
1. Stored procedure definition (T-SQL)
2. Database schema (tables, columns, types, constraints, relationships)
3. Workload configuration (number of calls, coverage goals)

Generate a comprehensive test workload as a JSON array of test cases.

Each test case should include:
- parameters: Object with parameter names and values
- expected_behavior: "success" or "error" or "special_case"
- description: Brief explanation of what this test case validates

Coverage goals:
- Typical use cases (valid data, common scenarios)
- Edge cases (boundary values, null handling, empty strings)
- Error cases (invalid parameters, constraint violations)
- Performance considerations (large result sets, complex joins)

Ensure:
- Parameters match stored procedure signature exactly
- Values are realistic and respect data type constraints
- Foreign key references exist in related tables
- Date/time values are reasonable
- String lengths respect column limits

Return ONLY valid JSON array, no additional commentary.
```

### Artifact Storage for Workloads

**Storage structure**:
```
s3://proctus-artifacts/
  {tenant_id}/
    workloads/
      {workload_id}/
        entries.json          # Full workload entries
        metadata.json         # Generation metadata
        schema_snapshot.json  # Schema at generation time
```

## Implementation Tasks

### 1. CDCME Integration
- [ ] Create CDCME interface definitions
- [ ] Implement CDC enable/disable methods
- [ ] Implement CDC change capture method
- [ ] Implement delta comparison logic
- [ ] Add transaction handling for CDC operations
- [ ] Create CDCME mock for testing

### 2. Schema Introspection
- [ ] Implement table/column discovery queries
- [ ] Implement foreign key discovery
- [ ] Implement index discovery
- [ ] Create schema cache table migration
- [ ] Implement schema caching logic
- [ ] Add schema snapshot serialization

### 3. Dependency Discovery
- [ ] Create procedure_dependencies table migration
- [ ] Implement SQL parsing for table references
- [ ] Implement dependency analysis
- [ ] Store discovered dependencies
- [ ] Build dependency graph representation

### 4. AI/LLM Adapter
- [ ] Create LLM provider interface
- [ ] Implement OpenAI GPT-4 provider
- [ ] Add API key configuration
- [ ] Implement prompt template system
- [ ] Add retry logic with exponential backoff
- [ ] Implement rate limiting
- [ ] Add redaction for sensitive data
- [ ] Track token usage and costs

### 5. Workload Generation
- [ ] Create workloads table migration
- [ ] Implement workload generation job executor
- [ ] Build prompt construction logic
- [ ] Implement LLM response parsing and validation
- [ ] Store workload entries in artifact storage
- [ ] Add workload versioning support

### 6. API Handlers
- [ ] Implement POST /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/workloads
- [ ] Implement GET /v1/workloads/{workloadId}
- [ ] Implement GET /v1/workloads/{workloadId}/entries
- [ ] Add request validation
- [ ] Handle streaming responses for large workloads

### 7. Testing
- [ ] Unit tests for schema introspection queries
- [ ] Unit tests for dependency discovery
- [ ] Unit tests for prompt construction
- [ ] Integration tests with mocked LLM
- [ ] Integration tests with real LLM (manual/gated)
- [ ] Test workload entry validation
- [ ] Test error handling for LLM failures
- [ ] Test schema caching behavior

### 8. Monitoring
- [ ] Add metrics for workload generation duration
- [ ] Add metrics for LLM API calls
- [ ] Track token usage per workload
- [ ] Add alerts for LLM API failures
- [ ] Monitor cost per generated workload

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Can discover database schema for a session
- [ ] Can discover procedure dependencies
- [ ] Can generate workload via LLM for a procedure
- [ ] Generated workload entries are valid JSON
- [ ] Workload entries match procedure signature
- [ ] Workloads are persisted and retrievable
- [ ] Schema metadata is cached efficiently
- [ ] LLM provider handles rate limits gracefully
- [ ] Failed workload generation jobs are retried
- [ ] Token usage is tracked and logged
- [ ] CDCME interface can enable/disable CDC
- [ ] CDCME interface can capture changes

## Dependencies
- Story 1 (Project Bootstrap)
- Story 3 (SQL Server Substrate & Session Management)

## Estimated Effort
- **Size**: Large (6-8 days)
- **Complexity**: High (LLM integration, SQL parsing, CDC operations)

## Notes
- Prompt engineering is critical - iterate on prompts based on real results
- Consider implementing workload validation step before storage
- LLM responses may not always be perfect - implement validation and fallback
- Schema caching improves performance and reduces database load
- Track LLM costs carefully; implement budget alerts
- Consider implementing workload templates for common patterns
- Future: support manual workload editing after generation
- Future: support workload import from existing test suites

items.body:
## Ce qui est attendu

Un gérant ou une administratrice peut, depuis Personnel, rendre réservable un membre du personnel : créer sa fiche praticien, puis saisir ses horaires et ses prestations (CDC §2.3, horaires du staff et affectation aux praticiens). Sans cela, la boucle réserver, confirmer, encaisser ne peut pas démarrer.

## Ce qui est constaté

La carte « Praticiens — 0 » l'annonce elle-même : « La création d'une fiche praticien n'est pas encore servie par l'API — invitez d'abord le compte ci-dessous ». L'invitation d'un compte praticien·ne aboutit (« Invitation émise », Comptes passe à 4) mais Praticiens reste à 0. Côté API, aucune des 82 routes n'écrit la table staff : StaffController n'expose que GET /staff, dont le docstring dit que « le cycle de vie de la fiche n'appartient encore à aucun module » ; ni POST /users en rôle STAFF, ni l'acceptation d'invitation, ni PATCH /users/{id}/status n'en créent. Seul le seed Prisma en crée (apps/api/prisma/seed.ts:957). En cascade : la prestation affiche « Aucun praticien affecté », « Ajouter un praticien » est désactivé, le tunnel public répond « Aucun créneau sur les 14 prochains jours », le planning n'offre aucune création de rendez-vous. Tout établissement qui n'a pas été semé est inexploitable. #599 ne couvre que le jeu d'essai de recette, pas le produit.

## Mesure

0 route d'écriture sur la fiche praticien sur 82 ; parcours de réservation arrêté à l'étape 2 sur 5

## Preuve

```
Navigateur : admin/personnel, invitation de Léa Praticienne, puis browser_snapshot « Praticiens — 0 » inchangé ; tunnel /recette-2026091502/reservation « Aucun créneau ». API (établissement recette-20260915) : POST /api/v1/users rôle STAFF → 201 ; POST /api/v1/auth/invitations/accept avec le jeton réel → succès ; PATCH /api/v1/users/{id}/status → 200 ; GET /api/v1/staff → 200 [] après chaque étape. Code : aucune écriture prisma.staff dans apps/api/src, une seule dans apps/api/prisma/seed.ts.
```

## Preuve visuelle

![« Praticiens — 0 » au-dessus de « Comptes — 4 » après l'invitation de Léa, et la phrase qui renvoie à l'API](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TMap-Works/spa-booking/qa-captures/docs/qa/captures/20260915-1/b2358220bb9a-1.png)
*« Praticiens — 0 » au-dessus de « Comptes — 4 » après l'invitation de Léa, et la phrase qui renvoie à l'API*

![Tunnel à 360 px — « Aucun praticien ne propose cette prestation » puis « Aucun créneau »](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TMap-Works/spa-booking/qa-captures/docs/qa/captures/20260915-1/b2358220bb9a-2.png)
*Tunnel à 360 px — « Aucun praticien ne propose cette prestation » puis « Aucun créneau »*

## Comment reproduire

1. Établissement neuf, connexion admin 2. Personnel, Inviter un membre, rôle praticien·ne 3. Constater « Praticiens — 0 » 4. Prestations, ouvrir une prestation : « Ajouter un praticien » désactivé 5. /<salon>/reservation, choisir la prestation : « Aucun créneau »

## Critère enfreint

`fe:ux` — parcours et libellés — états vide, en chargement, en erreur.
Gravité **bloquant** (empêche d'accomplir la tâche, ou expose une donnée) → `P0`.

Grille de référence : [.claude/skills/qa/SKILL.md](.claude/skills/qa/SKILL.md).

items.title: SCS-001 — Learning Content Authoring / Slice 1
items.body:
## Status
READY FOR ARENA IMPLEMENTATION

## Source of Truth
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` v1.2.0 RATIFIED
- `docs/adr/ADR-0011-scs-001-learning-content-authoring-boundary.md` RATIFIED
- SCS-001 existing canonical implementation and contracts on `main`

## Goal
Implement the smallest coherent Learning Content Authoring capability that establishes the upstream hierarchy for the existing Submission → Teacher Review flow:

`Course → Module → Lesson → Assignment → Submission → Teacher Review`

This is an implementation task. Do not reinterpret the domain decision.

## Business Scope
Learning owns these tenant-scoped entities within SCS-001:
- Course
- Module
- Lesson
- Assignment

Existing Submission and Teacher Review behavior must remain compatible and unchanged except where a hierarchy relationship is required to connect Assignment to its parent Lesson.

### Course
Minimum fields:
- `course_id`
- `tenant_id`
- `title`
- `description`
- `status`
- `created_by`
- `created_at`
- `updated_at`

Lifecycle implemented in this slice:
- `DRAFT → PUBLISHED`
- `PUBLISHED → ARCHIVED`

No UNPUBLISH.

### Module
Minimum fields:
- `module_id`
- `course_id`
- `tenant_id`
- `title`
- `position`
- `status`

Created as DRAFT.

### Lesson
Minimum fields:
- `lesson_id`
- `module_id`
- `tenant_id`
- `title`
- `content`
- `position`
- `status`

Created as DRAFT.

### Assignment
Preserve the existing Assignment identity/semantics and extend it only as necessary to establish:
- parent Lesson;
- tenant ownership;
- title/instructions;
- lifecycle status.

Created as DRAFT.

## Publication Semantics
Course publication is the single publication command for the first slice.

A Course may be published only when its content hierarchy is structurally valid:
- every Module belongs to the Course and same tenant;
- every Lesson belongs to its Module and same tenant;
- every Assignment belongs to its Lesson and same tenant;
- all existing descendants are in DRAFT state.

Publication atomically changes Course and all descendants in its hierarchy from DRAFT to PUBLISHED.

If validation fails, nothing is published.

After Course publication, Course/Module/Lesson/Assignment structure and content are immutable in this slice. No generic PUT/PATCH/DELETE editing API is introduced.

Course archive is an explicit command and may be executed only for a PUBLISHED Course. Archiving atomically archives the Course and its descendants. No unarchive operation is introduced.

## Read Semantics
Teacher may read the Course hierarchy for a Course in their effective tenant.

Student may read a Course hierarchy only when the Course is PUBLISHED and the effective tenant matches.

Published content must expose enough hierarchy information to navigate:
Course → Module → Lesson → Assignment.

Do not add separate generic CRUD endpoints solely to expose every entity.

## Candidate API
Base path: `/api/v1/learning`

Teacher commands:
- `POST /courses`
- `POST /courses/{course_id}/modules`
- `POST /modules/{module_id}/lessons`
- `POST /lessons/{lesson_id}/assignments`
- `POST /courses/{course_id}/publish`
- `POST /courses/{course_id}/archive`

Hierarchy read:
- `GET /courses/{course_id}`

Keep the existing canonical Submission endpoints intact:
- `GET /submissions/{submission_id}`
- `GET /assignments/{assignment_id}/submissions`
- `POST /submissions/{submission_id}/review`

The exact request/response schema must be documented in OpenAPI and Component Contract.

## Authorization
Use the existing chain only:
`Identity → effective tenant → Authorization → Learning ownership boundary`

Teacher:
- create Course/Module/Lesson/Assignment;
- publish Course;
- archive Course;
- read Course hierarchy.

Student:
- read published Course hierarchy.

All other roles/operations deny by default.

Do not implement RBAC/policy logic inside Learning.

## Tenant and Ownership Invariants
- tenant context comes from verified identity/effective tenant, never caller-supplied tenant_id;
- all four entities are tenant-scoped and owned by Learning;
- no cross-tenant parent/child relationship;
- no orphan Module/Lesson/Assignment;
- resource ownership must be enforced at the Learning boundary;
- no public bypass;
- fail closed on missing/invalid identity or dependency failure.

## Idempotency
Every state-changing command requires `Idempotency-Key` and uses existing IS-005.

Required commands:
- create Course
- create Module
- create Lesson
- create Assignment
- publish Course
- archive Course

Same key + same command/payload/identity/tenant/target => same logical result, no second effect.
Changed payload/identity/tenant/operation/target => conflict.
Authorization denial must not create a successful idempotency record or business effect.

## Errors
Use the established error envelope and stable semantics. At minimum preserve/use:
- `AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED`
- `AUTHORIZATION_DENIED`
- `TENANT_MISMATCH`
- `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`
- `RESOURCE_OWNER_MISMATCH`
- `INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION`
- `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED`
- `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`
- `VALIDATION_ERROR`
- `DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE`

Add only narrowly necessary content-authoring errors.

## Contracts and Verification
Update:
- `components/learning/contract/openapi.yaml`
- `components/learning/contract/component_contract.json`
- `components/learning/README.md`

Implementation must include:
- unit tests;
- integration/behavioral tests;
- authorization negative tests;
- tenant isolation tests;
- ownership tests;
- idempotency/replay/concurrency tests;
- lifecycle transition tests;
- atomic publication/archive tests;
- hierarchy integrity tests;
- OpenAPI/contract validation.

Run the complete applicable test suite and report exact results.

## NOT IN SCOPE
Do NOT implement:
- grading;
- score;
- feedback/comments;
- LearningResult;
- progress tracking;
- enrollment or enrollment completion rules;
- analytics;
- media service;
- payment;
- events/CDC solely for this capability;
- new foundation services;
- Component Catalog;
- Composer;
- Golden Bundles;
- release trains;
- microservices;
- generic CRUD;
- revision/versioning of published courses;
- UNPUBLISH/unarchive;
- automatic grading;
- new identity/tenant/authz/idempotency mechanism.

## Architecture Gap Rule
If implementation requires changing `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, introducing a new architectural law, or violating a ratified ADR, STOP the affected work and report an Architecture Gap. Do not silently modify architecture.

## PR Requirements
PR must contain:
- CHECKED
- CHANGED
- NOT CHANGED
- VERIFICATION
- RISKS OR GAPS
- SOURCE OF TRUTH
- Issue #31 link

Task is complete only after PR is reviewed, accepted, and merged into `main`. Arena must not merge `main` itself.

items.title: Production CRM tables are missing their primary keys

milestone.title: Infrastructure & Data
milestone.description: Database, migrations, framework upgrades, deployment topology, data integrity, import and export. Keeps the platform sound rather than adding user-facing features. Not a release: milestones are themes and never carry a version number.

items.body:
## Summary

Every CRM table in production is missing its primary key. Confirmed by direct query against
production on 2026-08-24:

| Table | Primary key |
|---|---|
| `companies` | **NO PRIMARY KEY** |
| `people` | **NO PRIMARY KEY** |
| `opportunities` | **NO PRIMARY KEY** |
| `tasks` | **NO PRIMARY KEY** |
| `notes` | **NO PRIMARY KEY** |
| `custom_fields` | **NO PRIMARY KEY** |
| `custom_field_options` | **NO PRIMARY KEY** |
| `custom_field_values` | **NO PRIMARY KEY** |

The same tables have their primary keys locally, so this is production schema drift, not a
missing migration.

## Evidence

`custom_field_values` (227,206 rows, 140 MB) carries exactly one constraint in production:

```json
[
  {
    "conname": "custom_field_values_entity_type_unique",
    "contype": "u",
    "definition": "UNIQUE (entity_type, entity_id, custom_field_id, tenant_id)"
  }
]
```

Locally the same table has three: the primary key on `id`, a foreign key to `custom_fields`,
and that unique. The foreign key is missing in production too.

Its index list is also short. Production has 7, local has 12. Missing in production:

- `custom_field_values_pkey`
- `custom_field_values_tenant_entity_idx` (`tenant_id, entity_type, entity_id`)
- `custom_field_values_entity_type_entity_id_index`
- `custom_field_values_entity_id_custom_field_id_index`
- `custom_field_values_tenant_id_index`

## Why this has been invisible

Eloquent generates ULIDs application-side and never asks the database to enforce them, so
nothing in normal operation fails. The damage only shows up as query cost and as the absence
of a uniqueness guarantee.

## Impact

**Uniqueness is unenforced.** Nothing at the database level prevents two rows sharing an `id`.
Whether that has already happened needs the duplicate check below, and it determines whether a
primary key can be added directly or the data has to be repaired first.

**Lookups by id have no index on at least one table.** On `custom_field_values` the only index
leads with `entity_type`, so `where id = ?` scans 227k rows / 140 MB. Whether the other seven
tables retain a standalone index on `id` is not yet confirmed and is part of the check below.

**Tooling that expects a replica identity** (logical replication, some backup and CDC tooling)
degrades or refuses on a table with no primary key.

## Where it came from

This is the ULID recreation fallout. The pre-recreation migration ran against production and
left the table definitions without their named constraints. Prior investigation recorded missing
named uniques and foreign keys; the missing primary keys are a broader instance of the same
event and were not previously known.

## Not caused by PR #506

Surfaced by the pre-deploy preflight for #506, which checks for
`custom_field_values_tenant_entity_idx` because the new chat search depends on it. That index
turned out to be missing, and widening the check found the primary keys were gone as well.

The chat search still works without its index: Postgres falls back to the unique index and the
query returns in ~139 ms per entity type rather than the ~2.4 ms the intended plan gives, so
roughly 700 ms across five entity types, degrading with tenant size. That is a separate, much
smaller fix and should not be bundled with this one.

## Next step, before any repair

```sql
select count(*) from (select id from custom_field_values group by id having count(*) > 1) d;
```

Run per table. Zero everywhere means primary keys can be added directly. Anything above zero
means data repair comes first.

## Repair considerations

- `custom_field_values` is 140 MB. `ALTER TABLE ... ADD PRIMARY KEY` builds a unique index and
  takes an `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` lock for the duration.
- The lock-light path is `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` followed by
  `ADD CONSTRAINT ... PRIMARY KEY USING INDEX`. This repo has no `CONCURRENTLY` precedent, so
  adopting it is a deliberate decision rather than an existing pattern.
- The missing foreign key on `custom_field_values.custom_field_id` should be reviewed in the
  same pass, since validating it requires its own scan.
- Worth auditing whether other tables outside this list lost constraints in the same event.

items.title: Add Document Processing TypeORM persistence and runtime composition
items.body:
Parent Epic: #289
Depends on: #292

## Goal

- Implement the package-owned TypeORM persistence adapter and database schema for `DocumentProcessing`.
- Enforce tenant isolation and one-processing-per-tenant/document uniqueness at the database boundary.
- Expose the package `/typeorm` composition contracts and complete the framework-agnostic `/runtime` manifest so the package is hostable through the existing shared execution runtime.
- Add persistence/composition tests at the boundaries that own those guarantees.

## Instructions

- Follow root `AGENTS.md`, `packages/AGENTS.md` and `docs/engineering/package-guidelines.md`, especially the persistence, TypeORM, tenant-ownership and runtime-manifest rules.
- Use `packages/documents/src/lib/persistence/typeorm/`, `packages/documents/src/typeorm.ts` and `packages/documents/src/runtime.ts` as the closest proven responsibility references. Reuse their ownership boundaries without copying Documents-specific schema fields or uniqueness rules.
- Keep the hosting-service `DataSource` lifecycle outside this package. The package owns entities, migrations, mapper/repository adapter knowledge and its persistence factory; the future service will own the real `DataSource`.
- Tenant-owned lookups and mutations must enforce tenant scope in database predicates. Do not load globally and compare tenant afterward.
- Enforce tenant-local uniqueness for `(tenant_id, document_id)` in the database and translate expected duplicate/create-or-existing behavior into the package persistence contract rather than leaking database-specific errors to handlers.
- Keep state-transition and state-shape business invariants owned by the aggregate and restore/mapping boundary. Add database constraints only where current repository guidance or a concrete concurrency/data-integrity requirement makes the database the owning boundary; do not duplicate aggregate rules mechanically as schema policy.
- Keep EDP transaction propagation, execution log, Outbox and Runner composition in the existing shared runtime. Do not reproduce those mechanisms in the package.
- Create the task branch from the latest `epic-document-processing-package` branch and target the task PR back to `epic-document-processing-package`.

## Success criteria

- A package-owned TypeORM entity persists processing id, tenant id, source document id, status, extracted text and failure reason with persistence shapes that can round-trip every valid aggregate state.
- A package-owned migration creates the Document Processing schema required by this Epic.
- The database enforces uniqueness for `(tenant_id, document_id)`.
- Persistence create/reuse behavior is safe under the database uniqueness rule and returns the contract-level `created | existing` outcome expected by the prepare handler.
- Every lookup required by the persistence port includes tenant scope in its query predicate.
- Update includes tenant scope in the mutation boundary and does not permit cross-tenant mutation.
- Mapper/restore behavior preserves aggregate invariants and rejects persisted state that cannot restore to a valid aggregate rather than moving business rules into the persistence representation.
- `/typeorm` exposes the package entity/migration composition constants, persistence runtime token and factory without exposing concrete adapter internals through the root business entrypoint.
- `/runtime` uses the existing `defineRuntimePackage(...)` contract to aggregate the package execution bindings and TypeORM persistence contributions without duplicating handler or adapter construction knowledge.
- Persistence integration tests prove tenant isolation, tenant-local uniqueness/create-or-existing behavior, valid-state round-tripping and cross-tenant absence semantics.
- Composition tests prove the package execution/TypeORM runtime contributions are complete without introducing Nest imports into the business package.
- No service, HTTP presenter, event consumer, broker/CDC integration, ObjectStorage read or extractor implementation is introduced.
- Relevant Nx lint, typecheck, test and build checks for the package are green.

items.body:
> Constat de la vérification des données et de la conception demandée par le
> PO le 16/09/2026 — demande tracée dans #804.

## Constat

Le CDC §2.4 décrit le paiement ainsi : « Payment — Transaction (montant,
moyen, statut) — 1–1 vers Appointment **ou vente POS** ». Le schéma ne permet
que la première moitié de cette relation.

- `payments` ne se rattache qu'à un rendez-vous (`appointment_id`, unique par
  établissement). **Aucune colonne ne relie un paiement à une vente.**
- Composer une vente (`POST /v1/sales`) n'encaisse rien ; `sales.service.ts`
  en fait deux gestes distincts. À l'inverse, régler un rendez-vous
  (`POST /v1/payments/cash`) ne crée aucune vente.
- Ce que montre la base `spa_dev` :

  | Établissement | Observation |
  |---|---|
  | Barber Tana | 12 ventes, dont 11 sans rendez-vous. Aucune n'a de paiement, et aucune ne **peut** en avoir. |
  | Spa Lumière | 4 paiements et une seule vente. |
  | Spa Lumière | La vente de 106,80 € est adossée à un paiement de 65,00 €. |
  | Spa Lumière | Deux paiements `CASH SUCCEEDED` portent sur des rendez-vous encore `PENDING`, dont l'un est prévu le lendemain. |

  Le règlement en espèces du rendez-vous du 14/09, fait pendant ce test, n'a
  créé **aucune** vente : il n'existe donc aucune pièce à imprimer.
- Le reporting calcule le revenu sur les paiements
  (`reporting/reporting.repository.ts:240`). Les ventes de produits n'y entrent
  jamais. L'écran de Spa Lumière affiche « 385,00 € · 5 encaissements », alors
  que la seule vente enregistrée vaut 106,80 € et n'y compte que pour 65,00 €.

## Critères d'acceptation

1. Une migration ajoute `payments.sale_id`, avec la clé étrangère composite
   `(tenant_id, sale_id)`. Une contrainte garantit que tout nouveau paiement
   porte une vente. `appointment_id` reste lisible, mais le règlement passe
   désormais par la vente.
2. Encaisser un rendez-vous revient à **composer sa vente puis la régler**,
   dans une seule transaction. La vente reprend la prestation au prix figé et
   les lignes ajoutées. Une vente sans rendez-vous se règle de la même façon.
3. Une vente réglée ne peut pas l'être une seconde fois : une contrainte en
   base l'interdit et l'API répond 409 `SALE_ALREADY_SETTLED`.
4. **Règlement mixte.** Une même vente peut se régler en plusieurs fois,
   et par plusieurs moyens. Exemple : un ticket de 78,00 € réglé par
   50,00 € en espèces, puis 28,00 € par TPE.
   - Une vente porte plusieurs paiements. Elle est soldée quand leur somme
     égale son total.
   - Un paiement qui dépasserait le reste dû est refusé en 422.
   - Seules les espèces font exception : leur excédent est la monnaie rendue.

   _Proposé au PO le 16/09, à confirmer._ La carte au comptoir passe par un
   TPE et non par Stripe (arbitrage du 16/09, #834).
5. Le montant réglé est toujours le total calculé par le serveur, jamais un
   montant venu du front.
6. Le reporting calcule le revenu sur les ventes réglées. Une vente de produit
   réglée apparaît dans le revenu de sa journée.
7. Un script de reprise des données :
   - crée la vente manquante de chaque paiement existant ;
   - liste les ventes sans paiement, pour décision. Il n'invente aucun
     paiement.
8. La règle d'encaissement d'un rendez-vous non confirmé est écrite et testée,
   en cohérence avec #800. Deux options : l'acompte est autorisé, ou le
   règlement est refusé en 422.
9. Tests d'intégration, plus un test de concurrence : deux règlements
   simultanés de la même vente, dont un seul réussit.

Dépend de #816

## Captures

**Revenu calculé sur les seuls paiements : « 385,00 € · 5 encaissements »**

![Revenu calculé sur les seuls paiements : « 385,00 € · 5 encaissements »](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TMap-Works/spa-booking/qa-captures/docs/retour-po/captures/retour-po-20260916/po-d1-1.png)

items.title: cdc: outbound change-data-capture to external brokers (Kafka / NATS / Kinesis / Pulsar)
items.body:
## Summary

When the WAL-CDC subscription subsystem ships (separate issue), the same internal WAL event stream becomes the natural source for outbound replication to external message brokers. Many production architectures fan database changes out to Kafka / NATS JetStream / Kinesis / Pulsar for downstream consumers (data warehouses, search indexers, analytics pipelines, third-party integrations). FraiseQL should be able to emit there directly.

## Why

- **Common architectural pattern.** "DB → Kafka → consumers" is the standard event-driven shape. Without native support, operators run Debezium or build a sidecar — both add operational complexity and bypass FraiseQL's audit / tenancy / RLS context.
- **Reuses the WAL-CDC plumbing.** The observability + per-tenant filtering + ordering guarantees are the same.
- **Cleaner than the observer subsystem for high-volume outbound.** Observers are dispatch-with-retry-with-DLQ, optimised for webhook reliability; brokers are throughput-optimised with their own durability story. Different shape, different code path.

## Current state at frozen SHA `d0a4ed4ec`

- Observers can emit to NATS, but the NATS dispatch path is observer-handler-shaped (one handler per event, retry / DLQ). Not a broker-firehose shape.
- No Kafka / Kinesis / Pulsar emit path.
- Per-broker dependencies absent from `Cargo.toml`.

## Target state

- `[cdc.outbound]` TOML section:
  - `[[cdc.outbound.sinks]]` array of broker sinks.
  - Per-sink: `kind` (`kafka` | `nats-jetstream` | `kinesis` | `pulsar`), `endpoint`, `topic_template` (e.g., `fraiseql.{tenant_id}.{table}`), `format` (`avro` | `protobuf` | `json`), `schema_registry_url` (optional).
- Pulls events from the WAL-CDC stream (depends on issue #366) — single source of truth, multiple sinks.
- Per-tenant + per-table sink filtering (don't fan tenant A's events to tenant B's broker topic).
- Outbox pattern: events that fail to publish are retried with exponential backoff + DLQ, similar to observers but at a different scale.

## Implementation sketch

- New crate `crates/fraiseql-cdc-sinks/` with per-broker submodules.
- Each sink implements `CdcSink` trait: `publish(events: &[ChangeEvent]) -> Result<()>` with batching.
- Per-broker Cargo features: `cdc-kafka` (rdkafka), `cdc-nats-jetstream`, `cdc-kinesis` (aws-sdk-kinesis), `cdc-pulsar`.
- Outbox table in Postgres for unpublished events: `tb_cdc_outbox`. Drained by a background worker.
- Schema registry integration: outbound events optionally serialised with their compiled-schema type as the Avro / Protobuf descriptor.

## Dependencies

- Issue #366 (WAL-CDC subscriptions) must land first — the broker sinks consume from the same WAL stream.

## Acceptance

- Writes to `tb_post` emit a Kafka record to `fraiseql.{tenant_id}.tb_post` within < 500 ms.
- Per-tenant isolation: tenant A's events land only on tenant A's topics.
- Broker outage triggers outbox accumulation + retry, no event loss.
- Avro / Protobuf schema registered against external schema registry on first event of each type.
- Documented `/features/cdc-outbound` page.

items.title: [Bug]: Online DROP INDEX with concurrent UPDATE resurrects old versions and duplicates primary keys
items.body:
## Description

在在线 `DROP INDEX` 与并发 autocommit `UPDATE` 重叠后，已经提交的旧 UPDATE 版本重新可见，基表出现重复复合主键。该路径在后续的合法/非法 `ADD UNIQUE INDEX` 之前已经失败，因此它不能归因于唯一索引拒绝或其清理路径。

## Environment

- Branch: `main`
- Commit: `1f9e501594509fb5d2e0284833faf8c3426e2285`
- Deployment: TKE distributed deployment, 3 CN; `mo-bench-tke.yaml`.
- Test date: 2026-08-17

## Steps to reproduce

1. 创建带复合主键 `(tenant_id, row_id)`、一个唯一二级索引和两个普通二级索引的表；写入 300,000 行，`tenant_id = row_id % 48`，`row_id` 与 `external_key` 均全局唯一。
2. 启动 8 个独立 autocommit writer，分别持续更新 tenant `4, 15, 26, 37, 0, 11, 22, 33`。UPDATE 仅修改非主键列 `status/category/amount/version/payload/updated_at`。
3. 在 writer 与 DDL 真实重叠时，在线执行 ADD INDEX；停止该轮 writer 并审计基表。该阶段通过。
4. 再启动同样的 8 个 writer，在重叠窗口内执行：

   ```sql
   ALTER TABLE idx_ddl_probe
     DROP INDEX idx_ddl_row_tenant_reverse;
   ```

5. DDL 成功后，使用新 autocommit 连接执行：

   ```sql
   SELECT COUNT(*)
   FROM (
     SELECT tenant_id, row_id
     FROM idx_ddl_probe
     GROUP BY tenant_id, row_id
     HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
   ) duplicate_keys;
   ```

完整可执行回归脚本和参数见 [mo-nightly-regression PR #1365](https://github.com/matrixorigin/mo-nightly-regression/blob/995cad1927a193f43b95fab25071c6eb660cf29f/script/issue_26804_online_index_race.py)：`--rows 300000 --writers 8 --writer-seconds 8 --generations 10 --ddl-timeout 180`。

## Actual behavior

第一个 generation 在 DROP INDEX 后立即失败：

```text
generation=1 setup=PASS
generation=1 add_index=PASS
issue=26804 status=FAIL cause=duplicate primary-key groups: 50000
AssertionError: duplicate primary-key groups: 50000
```

`50,000 = 8 × (300,000 / 48)`，精确对应 8 个 writer 覆盖的 tenant 行数。writer 从未修改主键列，DDL 前审计为 0 个重复主键分组。

## Expected behavior

在线 ADD/DROP INDEX 与并发 UPDATE 不得改变已提交版本的可见性。DDL 成功或失败后，基表均应保持 300,000 个逻辑主键，重复 `(tenant_id, row_id)` 分组必须为 0；后续 UNIQUE DDL 不应成为发现数据损坏的前置条件。

## Stability and controls

- Reproducer: TKE `main` 两次独立 CI 运行均在 generation 1 复现同一 `50,000` 个重复主键分组：
  - `43923c5e64abdc174f82ef4055ca653e501c3d34`（修复 #26905 之后 64 commits）
  - `1f9e501594509fb5d2e0284833faf8c3426e2285`（修复 #26905 之后 101 commits）
- Control: 同一 300,000 行、8 writer、10 generation 的单 CN 隔离运行已全部通过；该差异表明跨 CN 并发 DDL/DML 时序是必要条件之一，而非初始化数据或审计 SQL 的错误。
- Fixture checks: 每次失败前 `setup=PASS` 和 `add_index=PASS`；脚本要求每个 writer 至少一次成功 UPDATE 且至少一次 UPDATE 与 DDL 重叠。运行环境、Python 依赖及脚本启动均成功。
- Data integrity: 失败发生在基表主键完整性 gate，脚本立即停止，避免在已损坏的数据上继续执行 UNIQUE DDL 或掩盖根因。

## Evidence

- Official-main failing CI job: https://github.com/matrixorigin/mo-nightly-regression/actions/runs/32017014626/job/95350892463
- Independent earlier failing CI job: https://github.com/matrixorigin/mo-nightly-regression/actions/runs/31786586823/job/94725032612
- Existing regression PR: https://github.com/matrixorigin/mo-nightly-regression/pull/1365

## Code analysis

PR #26905 (`c3ba9c7df14388956cb38d78681c6c35b75c42b8`) fixed transferred tombstone write/sync failures. Both failing main commits contain that fix. The new evidence therefore indicates an uncovered distributed concurrent-DROP path or another cross-CN version/tombstone visibility path. This is a hypothesis; the black-box evidence above establishes incorrect committed-data visibility.

## Regression coverage

Keep the existing #26804 scenario in nightly big-data/concurrent regression. Do not change its expected result or reduce scale while the product remains failing. After the fix, retain the ADD INDEX and DROP INDEX phase-level audits separately so this DROP-triggered regression is caught before UNIQUE DDL.

## Related

- Closed source issue: https://github.com/matrixorigin/matrixone/issues/26804
- Earlier fix PR: https://github.com/matrixorigin/matrixone/pull/26905
- This report is intentionally scoped to the DROP INDEX boundary: the failing run never reaches the later valid or intentionally invalid UNIQUE index operations.
